# Production parity drive

Date: 2026-07-30
Mode: Build under `/goal` + `loop-build`
Branch: `task/20260730-TSK-HUM-rvp9-production-parity-with-pinned-libvp`
Worktree: `/Users/md/worktrees/rvp9-2/20260730-TSK-HUM-rvp9-production-parity-with-pinned-libvp`

## Objective

Bring the scoped one-pass realtime VP9 encoder matrix to reproducible production
parity with pinned libvpx v1.14.1. Final gates are correctness, aggregate PSNR
BD-rate no worse than +0.5%, no important unexplained clip regression above
+2%, corpus geomean encode time no worse than 1.05x vpxenc, and the absolute
720p30/1080p30/1080p60 latency budgets.

## Canonical open stage

`PLAN.md` leaves Stage 4a open. Its immediate exits are:

- cpu-used 7, realtime, one-pass VBR, lag 0, tune-content default;
- 720p30 median no worse than 33 ms;
- BD-rate within +2% of matched vpxenc;
- clean decode under rvp9-decoder, vpxdec, and ffmpeg;
- documented deliberate divergences.

Later Stage 4b–4e and final cpu-used 6–8 parity remain downstream. Do not treat
the historical Foreman-only or cropped-testsrc evidence as final corpus parity.

## Rejected hypotheses to preserve

- Global integer-pel interpolation-filter shortcut: speed win, Foreman BD-rate
  regression.
- Track2 block-size diamond start and coefficient sign-bit cost: did not transfer
  to the current tree.
- High-precision MV, forced max TX, RECT disable, loop-filter disable, broad
  NEWMV masks, GF target boost, keyframe/GF extra spend, and raw q-only scaling:
  none produced a reproducible Pareto improvement.
- Do not use numerical BD-rate from non-overlapping or badly shaped curves as
  completion evidence.

Fixed three repository build-script defects:

- Darwin arm64 now selects libvpx's newest macOS arm64 target,
  `arm64-darwin23-gcc`; the unversioned `arm64-darwin-gcc` target is iOS and
  requires an unavailable iPhoneOS SDK.

## Unit 3 — portable fixed-Q reference harness

The E9 fixed-Q diagnostic silently skipped libvpx on macOS because it only
looked for `D:\language\libvpx-stock\vpxenc.exe`. It now prefers the repository's
approved `build/libvpx` tools, retains the known Windows locations, and finally
searches `PATH`. The sibling decoder derives the correct platform suffix.

Fresh pinned-reference E9 results at commit `79667d8`:

- Q80: rvp9 `40.50 dB / 28,540 bits`; libvpx `41.78 dB / 30,595 bits`;
  gap `1.29 dB`
- Q120: rvp9 `37.61 dB / 15,004 bits`; libvpx `39.23 dB / 15,602 bits`;
  gap `1.62 dB`
- Q160: rvp9 `34.50 dB / 7,678 bits`; libvpx `36.19 dB / 7,329 bits`;
  gap `1.69 dB`

This confirms a coding-efficiency gap independent of the VBR rate controller.
The product baseline also chooses intra prediction for `20.34%` of blocks at
250 kbps versus libvpx's `2.00%`, so the next single hypothesis is that the
real-time intra fallback over-selects intra blocks.

The existing `RVP9_RT_NO_INTRA_FALLBACK=1` diagnostic produced only small
fixed-Q gains:

- Q80 gap `1.25 dB` (`+0.04 dB`)
- Q120 gap `1.61 dB` (`+0.01 dB`)
- Q160 gap `1.64 dB` (`+0.05 dB`)

It lowered mode-syntax cost but worsened prediction PSNR and raised coefficient
bits, so it is not established as a Pareto improvement. Next: run the legacy
Stage 4a VBR curve with the diagnostic enabled. Reject it unless the curve-level
gain and timing justify a production policy change.

The legacy VBR gate had the same native-tool defect: it found `vpxenc` but
hardcoded `vpxdec.exe`, silently omitting the reference curve. The gate now uses
the approved repository tools and derives the platform suffix.

Paired legacy four-point curves:

- default: matched-bitrate deficit `0.96 dB` across 2 in-range points
- no intra fallback: matched-bitrate deficit `0.64 dB` across 2 in-range points

The diagnostic improves the useful VBR points by `0.32 dB`, much more than its
fixed-Q movement. The legacy BD-rate result (`-4.59%` default versus `+13.47%`
diagnostic) is not trustworthy here: the curves overlap narrowly and the two
lowest rvp9 points are outside the reference range. Next: commit the portable
gate unit, make the no-intra policy a clean-tree candidate, and judge it with
the strict seven-point product gate.

## Unit 5 — post-policy hypothesis triage

Clean-tree strict and `Slack1Over8` product reports at commit `31329be`:

- strict:
  `target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-31329be00b25-1785411821194086000-p32109/stage4a_product_report.json`
- slack:
  `target/stage4a_product/candidate-31329be00b25-1785411832426320000-p32109/stage4a_product_report.json`

Slack lowered BD-rate from `+15.7683%` to `+15.4795%` and the matched-rate
deficit from `0.81462 dB` to `0.80200 dB`, but raised aggregate median time
from `11.9760 ms` to `12.1105 ms`. The important 250/400 kbps points slowed
about `2.8%/2.4%`. The quality movement is too small to justify the measured
speed loss, so this remains rejected.

The dormant libvpx-style VBR golden-frame allocator was also retested under
the accepted no-intra policy with `RVP9_VBR_GF_RC=1`. Its four-point legacy
curve produced `+18.52%` BD-rate and a `2.61 dB` matched-rate deficit, worse
than the accepted allocator. This hypothesis remains rejected.

A matched-rate block-stat comparison used rvp9's 400 kbps point
(`285.075 kbps`) against libvpx's 250 kbps point (`278.895 kbps`). Despite
rvp9 using the finer average inter Q (`146.37` versus `151.27`), it remained
about `0.83 dB` worse. The key-frame payload was only `68,376` bits versus
libvpx's `109,608`, while rvp9 spread inter bits almost uniformly instead of
libvpx's roughly ten-frame boosts. Rvp9 also used substantially more NEWMV
and ZEROMV area, much less skip, and many 4x4 transform leaves; libvpx used no
4x4 transform leaves in this sample.

This rules out a simple quantizer-only explanation. The next experiment is
raw per-block picker evidence from a separately patched, exact-revision
libvpx build and the current rvp9 VBR product path. The tracked F.0.2
comparator remains untouched because claiming its existing comparison defect
would require an external claim push, which this goal does not authorize.

## Unit 7 — exact zero MV at frame edges

The VBR picker record localized the remaining ZEROMV excess to the frame
edge. The strict no-halo envelope covers `21.32%` of inter-frame area, but it
contains `71.45%` of all rvp9 ZEROMV area (`15.99` of the total `22.38`
percentage points). At the top-left leaf, `(0,0)` was classified out of
bounds because the conservative sub-pel envelope starts at `(+6,+6)`.

That invariant is stale for exact zero motion. An integer `(0,0)` prediction
reads only the visible block and needs no interpolation halo. The candidate
now treats only exact ZEROMV as safe outside the strict envelope. Non-zero
and fractional vectors keep the existing bounds, so the motion search cannot
introduce a tight-plane over-read.

The focused bound test passes. The paired legacy VBR gate moved:

- matched-rate deficit: `0.64 dB` → `0.56 dB`
- 100 kbps point: `29.11 dB` → `29.24 dB`
- 250 kbps point: `33.87 dB` → `33.90 dB`

Its secondary BD-rate is `-13.92%`, but the curve still has only two
in-range points, so that number is not an acceptance result. Promote this
safe edge candidate to a clean tree and judge it with the strict seven-point
product gate.

Strict product report for `6ec4b93`:

`target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-6ec4b9332a33-1785413498436589000-p71741/stage4a_product_report.json`

The candidate is a reproducible coding-efficiency win:

- BD-rate: `+15.7683%` → `+14.0148%`

- 250 kbps ZEROMV area: roughly `22%` → `9.70%`
- 250 kbps NEARESTMV area: roughly `44%` → `56.92%`
- all seven streams: rvp9-decoder PASS, vpxdec BYTE-EXACT, ffmpeg BYTE-EXACT

## Unit 8 — visible full-chroma-pel edge candidates

The post-ZEROMV VBR picker record is:

`/tmp/rvp9-f02-edge-6ec4b93/run_6a6b3ff0/foreman_250kbps_rvp9.jsonl`

The strict edge band covers `21.10%` of inter area. Its mode distribution is
ZEROMV `21.37%`, NEARESTMV `65.19%`, NEARMV `0.04%`, and NEWMV `13.41%`.
The interior distribution is ZEROMV `6.67%`, NEARESTMV `54.02%`, NEARMV
`11.08%`, and NEWMV `28.23%`. Within the edge band's selected NEARESTMV
area, `81.22%` has a zero vector and `18.78%` has a non-zero vector.

The next bounded candidate admits a motion vector outside the conservative
filter-halo envelope only when it lands on integer samples for both luma and
4:2:0 chroma, and its complete visible block remains inside the frame.
Motion search limits remain unchanged; this affects only already-derived
candidate vectors such as NEARESTMV and NEARMV.

The first implementation admitted any whole-luma-pel vector. The legacy gate
immediately exposed that rule as unsafe with an out-of-bounds chroma filter
read: an odd whole-luma-pel displacement becomes chroma half-pel and still
needs a filter halo. The corrected predicate requires both Q3 components to
be multiples of 16. Its focused test covers zero, safe and unsafe frame
translations, the excluded odd-luma-pel case, fractional motion, a partial
leaf, and the unchanged strict-envelope path.

The focused test passes. The paired legacy VBR gate moved:

- matched-rate deficit: `0.56 dB` → `0.55 dB`
- 100 kbps point: `29.24 dB` → `29.27 dB`
- 250 kbps point: `33.90 dB` → `33.89 dB`

The evidence is small and mixed. Promote the safe candidate to a clean tree,
then use the strict seven-point product gate to decide whether its aggregate
quality movement is reproducible enough to keep.

`target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-d9cc5a97aaf9-1785413975514980000-p75688/stage4a_product_report.json`

## Unit 9 — isolate realtime residual-policy differences

At 250 kbps after the edge-motion fixes, rvp9's inter-mode distribution is
close to libvpx's, but rvp9 skips `55.64%` of area versus libvpx's roughly
`77.8%`. rvp9 also emits 4x4 transforms while libvpx's realtime picker floors
transform size at 8x8.

Reusing the ported picker-side `calculate_tx_size` decision in isolation with
`RVP9_RT_EMIT_TX_RD=0` made every meaningful legacy-gate point worse:

- 100 kbps: `29.2725 dB` → `29.1459 dB`
- 250 kbps: `33.8879 dB` → `33.7500 dB`
- matched-rate deficit: about `0.55 dB` → `0.66 dB`

This independently confirms the rejected minimum-Tx8 result. The 4x4
transforms compensate for another mismatch and are not themselves the next
lever.

libvpx speed 7 sets `use_quant_fp = !is_keyframe`; rvp9 still defaulted its
inter-frame emit path to the regular quantizer. Isolating fast quantization
with the existing `RVP9_RT_QUANT_FP=1` diagnostic, while retaining the
accepted emit-side transform RD loop, improved the legacy gate:

- 100 kbps: `71.4898 kbps / 29.2725 dB` →
  `71.2575 kbps / 29.2877 dB`
- 250 kbps: `179.0597 kbps / 33.8879 dB` →
  `179.6591 kbps / 33.9443 dB`
- matched-rate deficit: about `0.55 dB` → `0.52 dB`

Promote fast quantization as the clean-tree realtime default, retain
`RVP9_RT_QUANT_FP=0` as the regular-quantizer diagnostic, and judge the
candidate with the strict seven-point product gate.

Strict product report for `8b295b8`:

`target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-8b295b8b8db1-1785414232706674000-p79106/stage4a_product_report.json`

Fast quantization is a reproducible coding-efficiency win:

- BD-rate: `+13.3964%` → `+12.4005%`
- matched-rate deficit: `0.70910 dB` → `0.67993 dB`
- all seven streams: rvp9-decoder PASS, vpxdec BYTE-EXACT, ffmpeg BYTE-EXACT
- aggregate median: `12.5560 ms`

The median is `2.98%` above the immediately preceding `12.1924 ms` run even
though the quantizer itself is cheaper. Fast quantization changes coefficient
survival and caused more high-rate split work, while the host still has an
unrelated process occupying one CPU. Keep the clear quality win, but do not
claim a speed win from this sample. The remaining Stage 4a gap is `10.4005`
percentage points above its intermediate `+2%` exit.

## Unit 12 — rejected VBR keyframe active-quality port

The matched-rate frame table showed rvp9's first keyframe at Q65 and 68,376
bits versus libvpx at Q33 and 109,608 bits. Two source-level VBR divergences
could explain a higher keyframe floor:

- rvp9 reused its CBR active-quality boost of 32, while libvpx one-pass VBR
  initializes `rc->kf_boost` to `DEFAULT_KF_BOOST=2000`;
- rvp9 omitted libvpx's 0.75 quantizer-value adjustment for CIF-or-smaller
  frames.

An isolated candidate ported both rules in
`/Users/md/worktrees/rvp9-2/20260730-TSK-HUM-rvp9-production-parity-with-pinned-libvp/crates/rvp9-encoder/src/rate_control/vbr.rs:active_best_quality_vbr`.
Its focused VBR tests passed, but the four-point foreman gate was byte-for-byte

Source comparison found
`/Users/md/worktrees/rvp9-2/20260730-TSK-HUM-rvp9-production-parity-with-pinned-libvp/crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/inter.rs:run_newmv_search`
applies libvpx's speed-9 adaptive half/quarter-pel stop to the scoped cpu-used
6–8 path. Replacing it with libvpx's cpu6–8 `EIGHTH_PEL` default while leaving
the product high-precision frame flag off produced:

  `71.1563/29.2245`, and `179.2058 kbps/33.9853 dB`;

- median encode time: `22.7713 ms`, `81.36%` slower than `12.5560 ms`;
- all strict streams still decoded byte-exactly under vpxdec and ffmpeg.

Enabling the existing `RVP9_HIGHMV=1` flag with eighth-pel refinement initially
panicked on a GOLDEN NEWMV at a 16x8 right-edge leaf. Diagnosis showed the
picker replaced an unsafe `(16,-134)` NEAREST predictor with zero, then reused
that zero as NEWMV's coding reference. It consequently chose `(7,-58)` at
eighth-pel precision, while the writer correctly derived `(16,-134)` and could
only signal a quarter-pel delta. Separating the safe sampling predictor from
the actual coding reference removed the panic, but the legacy matched-rate
deficit worsened to `0.60 dB`. The coding-reference fix also perturbed the
default curve without a reproducible Pareto gain.

Both source candidates were removed. Keep the accepted adaptive forced stop
until another measured prerequisite makes full cpu6–8 refinement affordable.
The exact next experiment is a same-leaf prediction comparison: capture rvp9
and libvpx committed LAST/GOLDEN MV, interpolation filter, prediction SSE, and
residual EOB for aligned frame/block coordinates. First determine whether the
remaining residual gap comes from motion search, filter RD choice, or
transform/skip modelling before changing another policy.

## Unit 25 — correct the matched-Q oracle and isolate causal MV propagation

The old E.9 fixed-Q comparison was not actually matched at the keyframe.
libvpx Q mode applied its normal keyframe boost despite `--cq-level`, so the
requested internal qindices `80/120/160` produced keyframe qindices
`15/31/70`. That made the historical `1.3–1.8 dB` whole-stream deficit an
invalid coding-efficiency oracle.

E.9 now invokes libvpx with:

`--end-usage=q --cq-level=N --min-q=N --max-q=N+8`

The eight-step range is libvpx's minimum valid CLI range. It clamps the
keyframe at the requested qindex while leaving inter frames at the same
constant-quality point. The harness parses the first packet with
`rvp9-decoder`, asserts the observed keyframe qindex, parses IVF payloads,
and reports keyframe quality/bits plus average inter bits. The rvp9 leg now
retains the production Stage 4a VBR picker calibration while
`RVP9_FIXED_Q` overrides only rate-control Q selection.

The corrected 64-frame Foreman results are:

| qindex | rvp9 PSNR / bits per frame | libvpx PSNR / bits per frame | rvp9 inter-bit excess |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 80 | `40.39 dB / 26,087` | `40.37 dB / 21,112` | `+25.3%` |
| 120 | `37.55 dB / 13,435` | `37.52 dB / 10,384` | `+32.7%` |
| 160 | `34.34 dB / 6,204` | `34.37 dB / 4,962` | `+30.2%` |

Keyframes at the same qindex are already close:

- q80: rvp9 `40.83 dB / 56,136 bits`; libvpx
  `40.97 dB / 57,192 bits`;
- q120: rvp9 `37.89 dB / 33,592 bits`; libvpx
  `38.03 dB / 35,368 bits`;
- q160: rvp9 `34.77 dB / 18,272 bits`; libvpx
  `34.86 dB / 20,168 bits`.

The real fixed-Q gap is therefore inter-frame bit efficiency, not decoded
quality or keyframe coding. rvp9 spends `25–33%` more inter bits for
effectively the same decoded PSNR.

## Unit 31 — isolate the post-skip fixed-Q residual burden

The refreshed fixed-Q F.0.2 artifact under the accepted luma-skip baseline is:

`/tmp/rvp9-f02-acdc-rate-q120/run_6a6b8000`

It used the instrumented pinned-v1.14.1 encoder at:

`/tmp/rvp9-f02-schema.n5Qsoc/libvpx/build_arm64/vpxenc`

The 63 inter-frame averages at q120 are:

- rvp9 actual inter payload: `12,860 bits/frame`;
- libvpx actual inter payload: `9,886 bits/frame`;
- rvp9 actual coefficient payload: `9,672 bits/frame`;
- libvpx instrumented modeled residual payload: `5,507.714 bits/frame`;
- rvp9 estimated coefficient payload: `9,066.9 bits/frame`;
- libvpx modeled total candidate rate: `8,036.959 bits/frame`.

The default fixed-Q E.9 sweep confirms the same pattern:

| qindex | rvp9 PSNR / inter bits | libvpx PSNR / inter bits |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 80 | `40.36 dB / 25,404` | `40.37 dB / 20,437` |
| 120 | `37.49 dB / 12,860` | `37.52 dB / 9,886` |
| 160 | `34.23 dB / 5,889` | `34.37 dB / 4,619` |

Matched-q quality is nearly equal, while rvp9 spends about `24%`, `30%`,
and `27%` more inter bits. The burden is therefore predominantly a
rate-allocation / residual-selection problem, not a reconstruction-quality
ceiling.

Three transform hypotheses were rejected:

1. Disabling the content DCT-EOB skip veto collapses q120 to
   `30.90 dB / 4,082 inter bits`; this is not a usable quality trade.
2. Reusing the picker transform loses quality and raises payload at q80 and
   q120 (`37.29 dB / 13,136` at q120 versus the accepted
   `37.49 dB / 12,860`).
3. Forcing the maximum transform loses quality at every sampled qindex and
   raises payload at q80 and q120 (`37.09 dB / 12,983` at q120).

The refreshed cross-predictor replay still finds `323` common LAST-reference
leaves where libvpx emits zero luma residual while rvp9 does not. Most already
use TX8 on both sides (`204` leaves), so transform-size selection cannot
explain that subset.

The next measured hypothesis is the missing color-sensitivity consumer gate.
`PreAnalysisState::color_sensitivity_sb` already produces per-SB `[U, V]`
flags, but `pick_and_simulate_inter_encode_partitions` does not pass them to
the picker. Consequently `evaluate_candidate` always adds UV model-RD,
whereas pinned libvpx only does so when either `x->color_sensitivity` flag is
set (`vp9_pickmode.c:2381-2395`). Wire the existing flags into both descent
and final picker calls, add a focused disabled-gate regression, then rerun
fixed-Q E.9 before deciding whether to retain the change.

## Unit 32 — reject the existing color-sensitivity producer as a picker gate

The full libvpx UV gate was prototyped locally: per-SB `[U, V]` flags flowed
through descent and final picks; insensitive planes contributed no UV model
rate or distortion; large-block early termination bypassed UV. Focused model
and picker tests passed.

The fixed-Q E.9 result did not meet the Pareto rule:

| qindex | accepted rvp9 PSNR / inter bits | gated rvp9 PSNR / inter bits |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 80 | `40.36 dB / 25,404` | `40.36 dB / 25,486` |
| 120 | `37.49 dB / 12,860` | `37.50 dB / 12,956` |
| 160 | `34.23 dB / 5,889` | `34.24 dB / 5,883` |

At q80/q120 the gate costs `82`/`96` inter bits per frame for at most
`0.01 dB`; q160 is effectively flat. The source probe was therefore removed
and the worktree returned to the committed baseline.

This does not refute libvpx's gate. It refutes wiring rvp9's current
`PreAnalysisState::compute_color_sensitivity` output into production:
that producer explicitly compares luma against Last_Source and chroma
against each SB's own mean because it lacks libvpx's per-candidate prediction
buffers. Those flags are not an equivalent oracle. Do not reconnect them
without first measuring or correcting the producer.

The residual gap remains: matched-q quality is nearly equal, but rvp9 spends
about `24–30%` more inter payload, mostly coefficients. The next experiment
must target why rvp9 selects predictors / partitions that leave more coded
residual, not transform-size reuse or this approximate chroma gate.

## Unit 33 — reject an isolated 8×8-average partition variance substitution

Pinned libvpx's cpu-used 7 realtime path builds the variance-based partition
hierarchy from 8×8 source/reference averages in
`third_party/libvpx/vp9/encoder/vp9_encodeframe.c:fill_variance_8x8avg`.
rvp9 instead measures every residual pixel in
`crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/partition.rs:block_per_pixel_variance`.
This is a confirmed semantic difference: balanced texture within an 8×8
block affects rvp9's hierarchy but is invisible to libvpx's hierarchy.

A local diagnostic replaced only rvp9's hierarchy samples with rounded 8×8
average residuals. A focused checkerboard test proved the intended primitive,
and the encoder compiled. The paired seven-point foreman sweep was worse:

| metric | accepted full-pixel tree | 8×8-average tree |
|---|---:|---:|
| PSNR BD-rate versus libvpx | `+6.05%` | `+6.75%` |
| matched-bitrate mean deficit | `+0.33 dB` | `+0.36 dB` |
| matched-bitrate maximum deficit | `+0.62 dB` | `+0.69 dB` |

At q120 fixed-Q, the candidate also rose from `12,860` to `13,068`
inter bits/frame while quality moved only from `37.49` to `37.51 dB`.
The isolated primitive is therefore not a Pareto improvement. All diagnostic
source and test changes were removed.

This result does not refute an exact libvpx partition port. Its decision path
also carries conditional 4×4 averages, force propagation, integer-pel motion
compensation, rectangular partitions, and partition reuse. It does show that
changing the hierarchy statistic alone cannot close Stage 4a.

The next experiment is narrower and residual-focused: on the q120 F.0.2
common LAST-reference leaves with identical motion vector and interpolation
filter, measure source-versus-predictor residual energy and quantized
non-zero counts on both encoders. This will distinguish prediction-buffer
differences from transform/quantization differences before another product
change.

## Unit 34 — reject Hadamard-skip ranking and isolate predictor selection

A decoded-reference replay of the q120 F.0.2 traces separated reference drift
from predictor choice. Across `6,933` common in-bounds LAST-reference leaves:

- rvp9's chosen predictor has `1.2493x` libvpx's source-frame SSE;
- using each encoder's own decoded reference reduces that ratio to `1.0995x`;
- on rvp9's decoded reference, the libvpx-selected predictor still has
  `7.95%` less SSE than the rvp9-selected predictor;
- the `1,064` identical MV/filter picks have exactly equal source-frame SSE;
- the `5,869` different picks have `1.2899x` source-frame SSE in rvp9.

Thus reference drift contributes, but the larger measured loss is selecting a
worse predictor. A quantized DCT replay on the common leaves also estimates
libvpx's decision field at `89.59%` of rvp9's coefficient payload when both
use rvp9's reference.

The libvpx trace field previously named `luma_eob_nonzero` was clarified. It
records the winning realtime picker's final luma coding decision
(`!skip && skip_txfm == NONE`), not a raw FDCT EOB. Among the `323`
same-predictor leaves where rvp9 codes luma and libvpx does not, `113` are
libvpx skip-flag-only, `72` are `SKIP_TXFM_AC_DC`-only, and `138` set both.
This invalidates attempts to explain all `323` as transform quantization
disagreement.

One small source candidate made rvp9 rank Hadamard/quantize-fp skippable
leaves on its skip branch, matching libvpx's immediate `block_yrd` control
flow and the luma skip already honored by rvp9's emitter. The focused
self-consistency test and encoder check passed, but the strict seven-point
product curve regressed:

| metric | accepted baseline | Hadamard-skip ranking |
|---|---:|---:|
| PSNR BD-rate versus libvpx | `+6.8761%` | `+7.1759%` |
| matched-bitrate mean deficit | `0.3658 dB` | `0.3831 dB` |

All seven candidate streams still passed rvp9-decoder and remained byte-exact
under pinned vpxdec and ffmpeg. The source and test changes were removed.
The dirty diagnostic report is
`target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-a6cff389c75e-1785432726817555000-p5251/stage4a_product_report.json`.

The exact next experiment is candidate availability. For common-shape
LAST-reference leaves where libvpx's predictor is materially better on the
same rvp9 reconstructed reference, classify the libvpx MV against rvp9's
ZERO, NEAREST, and NEAR candidates. For remaining NEWMV cases, trace the
full-pixel and sub-pixel search result. This distinguishes an available

## Unit 35 — isolate coupled context and harden dormant intra reconstruction

Candidate replay found that the residual predictor gap is not a local
motion-search miss. Among common LAST-reference leaves where libvpx's
predictor is more than 1% better on rvp9's reconstructed reference:

- `58` use rvp9's NEAR candidate, `36` use NEAREST, `38` use ZERO, and
  `15` use rvp9's own NEWMV;
- the remaining `2,250` use another MV;
- `1,034` of those other MVs differ by only one quarter-pel step, but only
  `25/228` same-mode NEWMV pairs at that distance share the same NEAREST
  candidate and only `1/228` shares the same NEAREST/NEAR pair;
- just `189/2,250` other MVs appear within four cells of rvp9's causal or
  previous-frame field.

The nearby search objective often prefers libvpx's vector, but the candidate
contexts almost never match. This confirms the remaining motion difference is
upstream in the coupled partition/mode field, not another isolated sub-pixel
search rule.

Partition stability initially looked causal. Adjacent frames preserve the
exact superblock partition on `140/992` libvpx superblocks versus `10/992`
rvp9 superblocks; per-cell equality is `78.98%` versus `64.84%`. Instrumented
pinned libvpx showed that its low-source-SAD prior-partition copy path fires
`80` times on the q120 F.0.2 encode. The diagnostic binary remained
bit-identical to the canonical reference:

`10608f4a7eb5bd77d496215a345cb3f701899331284f746a1ff1b33059e0e900`

A source-faithful rvp9 prototype reused the prior variance partition for at
most two low-source-SAD frames. It did not improve fixed-Q coding:

| qindex | accepted inter bits/frame | partition-copy prototype |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 80 | `25,404` | `25,404` |
| 120 | `12,860` | `12,904` |
| 160 | `5,889` | `5,896` |

The copy is therefore a speed shortcut in libvpx's current field, not the
missing rate-distortion lever in rvp9's descent. The prototype was removed.

The q120 traces exposed a larger deliberate field difference: rvp9 chooses no
intra blocks on inter frames, while libvpx chooses `1,011`. Retesting rvp9's
dormant intra fallback first exposed two correctness faults. The live causal
grid recorded an intra winner as an invalid inter cell, and the encoder's
loop-filter grid did the same. The writer and decoder recorded both as intra,
so later NEAREST/NEAR resolution and filtering diverged. Before the fixes the
12-frame reference diagnostic first diverged at frame 3 with luma SSE
`44,924` and maximum error `51`; after the causal-grid fix, luma was exact but
chroma still diverged by up to `7`. Preserving intra in both grids made Y/U/V
pixel-exact on all 12 frames.

The reconstruction-safety prerequisite landed as `13dcac2`. Focused
validation passed:

- `cargo test -p rvp9-encoder
  tests::causal_grid_splats_intra_winner_as_intra -- --exact`;
- `cargo test -p rvp9-encoder
  loopfilter::w7_4_tests::inter_frame_lf_grid_preserves_intra_winner
  -- --exact`;
- `cargo test -p rvp9-encoder
  frame_loop::tests::build_inter_mi_grid_intra_winner_emits_block_mode_intra
  -- --exact`;
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`;
- `cargo clippy -p rvp9-encoder --lib --tests -- -D warnings`.

The now-safe policy still failed the Pareto rule:

| qindex | safe intra inter bits / PSNR | accepted baseline |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 80 | `26,402 / 40.34 dB` | `25,404 / 40.36 dB` |
| 120 | `13,604 / 37.44 dB` | `12,860 / 37.49 dB` |
| 160 | `6,268 / 34.22 dB` | `5,889 / 34.23 dB` |

The accepted no-intra product default remains unchanged.

The exact next experiment is an intra-selection cost oracle, not another
policy toggle. On the safe q120 path, record every rvp9 intra candidate's
best-inter and best-intra rate/distortion components, then join by covered
cell with libvpx's emitted intra field. Separate true-positive, false-positive,

## Unit 36 — reject broad intra gating and isolate the RD-domain mismatch

The q120 cost oracle joined `13,611` eligible rvp9 intra evaluations to
libvpx's emitted intra field by frame and covered MI cell. It classified
`250` true-positive leaves, `2,739` false-positive leaves, `251`
false-negative leaves, and `10,371` true-negative leaves. The false positives
cover `9,708` cells versus only `781` true-positive cells, so the dormant
picker overselects intra by roughly one order of magnitude.

The false-positive mean intra-minus-inter components were:

- RD cost `-3,154,695`;
- total rate `+4,020`, comprising coefficient rate `+6,715` and syntax rate
  `-2,695`;
- reconstructed-pixel distortion `-1,750`.

Rate alone does not explain the wins. Even requiring lower total rate leaves
`952` false-positive leaves versus `163` true positives. Requiring lower
coefficient rate leaves `202` false positives versus `90` true positives.

Pinned libvpx's full entry condition additionally rejects low-source-SAD
superblocks and any inter search that set `x->skip`. A source-SAD-only gate
still produced `26,198`, `13,372`, and `6,278` inter bits/frame at
q80/q120/q160. Adding the corresponding rvp9 picker-skip and early-search
guards reduced those to `26,122`, `13,322`, and `6,158`, still above the
accepted `25,404`, `12,860`, and `5,889`. PSNR remained effectively flat at
`40.36`, `37.46`, and `34.22 dB`. The policy therefore fails the Pareto rule,
and all diagnostic source changes were removed.

The remaining measured mismatch is the RD distortion domain. Libvpx's
realtime intra path ranks the Hadamard/quantize-fp coefficient error returned
by `block_yrd`, while rvp9 ranks post-reconstruction pixel SSE. The exact next
experiment is to rank safe intra candidates with the existing
`BlockYrdResult::coef_dist` (`pixel SSE << 4` for the all-zero shortcut),
while retaining pixel SSE only as the surfaced reconstruction diagnostic.
Retest fixed q80/q120/q160 before enabling any product policy.

## Unit 40 — reject intra-aware partition descent

Enabling the coefficient-domain intra fallback in partition descent did move
the field toward finer shapes. At 250 kbps, 8x8 area rose from `1.0293%` to
`4.4767%`, and intra area rose from `3.3606%` to `5.4750%`. Fixed-Q
prediction quality improved at all three points, but q160 inter payload rose
from `5,914` to `5,984` bits/frame.

The clean strict report is:

`target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-f6eee898378d-1785436285048786000-p58990/stage4a_product_report.json`

It rejects the coupling:

- BD-rate worsened from `+4.9246%` to `+5.3802%`;
- matched-rate deficit moved from `0.2841` to `0.2882 dB`;
- aggregate median time rose from `13.2028` to `14.7600 ms`;
- 250/400 kbps medians rose to `39.8026`/`42.2440 ms`;
- all seven streams remained cross-decoder byte-exact.

The descent evaluates candidates before reconstructing their within-SB
causal neighbours, so its intra edges are stale. More importantly, the full
curve shows that buying finer partitions this way costs too much syntax and
search time. The one-line candidate was removed.

The exact next experiment is intra chroma semantics. Pinned libvpx assigns
`mi->uv_mode = this_mode` when a realtime intra-in-inter candidate wins,
while rvp9 currently hardcodes UV DC in the simulator, causal grid, and
loop-filter grid. On the accepted field, q120 contains `309` V/H intra
leaves and the 250 kbps product point has `3.36%` intra area. Make UV follow
the selected Y mode for these leaves, add a focused grid/reconstruction

## Unit 44 — add the pure cpu7 fixed-tree parity seam

Arthur approved the bounded partition architecture change. A partner-tier
source audit agreed that pinned libvpx cpu-used 7 uses a fixed
`choose_partitioning` tree followed by one causal `nonrd_use_partition` pass,
not rvp9 A4's speculative recursive mode/partition search. The audit also set
the safe sequence: prove the pure variance tree against pinned libvpx before
changing the product default.

`crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/partition.rs::choose_fixed_tree_inter`
now accepts a materialized 64x64 source and selected predictor plus the exact
thresholds, visible extents, force flags, segment state, qindex, and noise
tier. It returns:

- the final square/rectangular partition grid;
- all 21 force-split bits;
- the exact sum-square/sum/count accumulators and derived variances for the
  canonical 64x64, 32x32, and 16x16 nodes;
- the separate low-resolution 4x4-average `vt2` nodes;
- parent partition symbols and leaves in VP9 coding order.

The source audit found and the implementation fixed three subtle rules:

- low-resolution `vt2` is local to the 16x16 decision; 32x32/64x64 parents
  still aggregate the original 8x8-average `vt`;
- the low-noise spread rule tests the full frame height, not the visible
  height inside the current superblock;
- partial-mi edge superblocks bypass the 64x64 parent probe before descending.

`PartitionDecision::is_valid_partition` now validates legal HORZ/VERT trees as
well as the legacy square-only tree. Eight new focused tests cover flat,
horizontal, vertical, forced, partial-edge, separate-`vt2`, and invalid
rectangular cases.

Observed validation:

- `cargo test -p rvp9-core mode_decision::partition::tests`: 28 passed;
- `cargo clippy -p rvp9-core --lib -- -D warnings`: passed;
- `cargo fmt --all` and `git diff --check`: passed.

This seam is intentionally not wired into encoding, so the accepted product
baseline remains `+4.924609930460733%` BD-rate and `13.202833 ms`. The exact
next unit is the pinned-libvpx replay oracle. It must capture the selected
partition predictor, exact thresholds/flags, original `vt`, local `vt2`,
force bits, visible extents, final parent symbols, and ordered leaves. Product
wiring stays blocked until that oracle is exact across q80/q120/q160.

The later product adapter must also restore libvpx's full six-state
`CONTENT_STATE_SB` producer and raw source-SAD/`zero_temp_sad_source` signal.
The current pre-analysis collapses those states to Normal/VeryHighSad, which
is insufficient for source-faithful cpu7 threshold scaling and partition-copy
shortcuts.

## Unit 56 — do not charge filter syntax for integer-pel MVs

The 16x16 rate investigation found a direct source mismatch before the full
component schema was needed. Rvp9 charged the selected switchable-filter
symbol on every inter candidate. Pinned libvpx adds that rate only when
`(mv.row | mv.col) & 7 != 0`, because integer-pel blocks do not signal an
interpolation filter. In the Unit 53 q120 same-winner set, `38/55` common
16x16 inter leaves used integer-pel MVs.

The picker now makes the same conditional charge. A focused regression
proves that two filters with an integer MV have identical rate and RD cost;
the existing first-filter tie behavior remains EightTap.

| 160 | `5,800 / 34.26 dB` | `5,853 / 34.27 dB` |

promotion:

## Unit 75 — install byte-exact AArch64 realtime fast quantization

Pinned libvpx quantizes coefficients in raster order with NEON and uses

and reduces the one-based inverse-scan positions of nonzero outputs. Other
targets retain the scalar oracle.

q-indices `0/1/20/80/160/255`, full-range i16 coefficients widened to i32,
and 4x4/8x8/16x16 transform sizes. Skip-block output zeroing is pinned
separately.

## Unit 81 — install byte-exact AArch64 SAD reductions

The AArch64 SAD dispatch table still pointed all 13 VP9 block shapes at the

- 4-wide blocks pack two exact 4-byte rows per vector;

## Unit 84 — correct the Stage 4a thread-count baseline

The pinned `vpxenc` profile showed four OS threads even though the prior
comparison omitted `--threads`. The CLI's VP9 default requests the maximum
legal number of tile columns (`tile_columns = 6`, clamped by frame width);
at 1280 pixels that is four column tiles. In contrast, rvp9 parses
`--threads` and `--tile-columns` but does not copy either value into
`EncoderConfig`; its frame loop always emits and encodes one tile.

Fresh warmed ten-encode aggregates used identical explicit thread counts,
120 frames of `testsrc_1280x704_120f.y4m`, one-pass VBR, 2 Mbps,
`--rt --cpu-used=7 --lag-in-frames=0 --aq-mode=0`:

- one thread: rvp9 `15.58 s`, vpxenc `3.73 s`, ratio `4.18x`;
- four threads: rvp9 `15.57 s`, vpxenc `1.71 s`, ratio `9.11x`.

The rvp9 `--threads=4` result is identical to `--threads=1`, proving the
flag is currently inert. Pinned vpxenc's default output is byte-identical
to explicit `--tile-columns=2`; explicit log2 tile columns `0`, `1`, and
`2` produce distinct streams. Pinned vpxenc four-thread `--row-mt=0`
matches its default stream and time (`1.70 s` for ten encodes);
`--row-mt=1` produces a distinct stream and measured `1.63 s`. Therefore
the relevant canonical speed mechanism is four independent column tiles,
not row-mt.

The corrected measurement invalidates the earlier 9–11x single-thread
interpretation but exposes the more important product defect: rvp9 cannot
meet the required same-thread-count gate until encoder tile columns and
tile workers are real. The next unit is architecture, not another scalar
leaf optimization: wire explicit tile/thread configuration, make tile
boundaries semantically correct, then parallelize independent column
tiles while keeping a one-thread/single-tile oracle.

## Unit 85 — establish tile-column configuration and writer isolation

Commit `b999c3a` added the encoder-side parallelism contract without changing
the emitted stream. `EncoderParallelism` now carries the maximum worker count
and requested log2 tile columns, clamps the latter through VP9's legal-width
rules, and preserves the legacy single-thread/single-tile constructor.
The CLI now maps its existing flags into that contract and uses libvpx's
eight-thread, maximum-column defaults when the flags are absent.

The next prerequisite made both keyframe and inter tile writers independent
at nonzero column origins. Mode/MV/transform neighbour lookup now rejects
frame cells across any tile edge. Coefficient reads, writes, and skip resets
subtract the tile's starting MI column before indexing `TileCoefCtx`.
Focused tests prove that the second tile cannot see the first tile's left
mode cell and that both inter and keyframe residual walks update local
coefficient columns `0..8`, not frame-relative columns `16..24`.

All 122 `modes_writer` tests passed. Warnings-denied `rvp9-core` all-target
clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.

including the asymmetric 640-pixel two-column case. Then construct and

## Unit 86 — centralize exact VP9 tile geometry

The core now exposes libvpx's `get_tile_offset` geometry and a
`ModesTileBounds` constructor. It divides the aligned superblock count before
converting back to MI units, so odd superblock counts do not accidentally
become equal-width pixel or MI partitions.

Focused cases cover 320, 640, 1280, and 1920 pixels. The verified libvpx
formula splits 320 pixels as `2 + 3` superblocks, 640 as `5 + 5`, 1280 as
four `5`-superblock columns, and 1920 as `7 + 8 + 7 + 8`. The earlier
architecture note's suggested 640-pixel `4 + 6` split was incorrect; the
pinned `vp9_tile_common.c:get_tile_offset` and decoder implementation both
produce `5 + 5`.

The focused geometry test and warnings-denied `rvp9-core` all-target clippy
passed, along with formatting and diff checks.

The exact next experiment is sequential synthetic multi-tile packet assembly
for keyframes and inter frames. Parse the header and tile size prefixes, then
decode through rvp9 and pinned vpxdec before any picker parallelism.

## Unit 87 — assemble sequential multi-tile packets

The keyframe and inter packet builders can now write any caller-selected

## Unit 89 — isolate adaptive RD thresholds per column tile

`StreamEncoder` now allocates one persistent `RdThreshTable` per effective

walk, so winner decay and loser increments cannot cross tile boundaries.

from show-frame state.

## Unit 90 — extract deterministic inter tile jobs

The inter picker can now restrict an invocation to one logical column tile.

statistics. It merges only the selected tile rectangle and SB state in fixed
column order. Coefficient keys stay in global MI coordinates and are asserted
disjoint during merge.

therefore compares the old one-worker monolithic call with the new

different execution shape.

## Unit 91 — run inter column tiles concurrently

The extracted inter jobs now run through scoped threads, capped at
`min(max_threads, tile_count)`. When fewer workers than tiles are available,
the frame loop dispatches fixed column-order batches and still merges every
result in column order. Each worker owns its reconstruction, partition, MV,
coefficient, VBP-history, split-statistic, and adaptive-threshold state.

The first concurrent oracle exposed a hidden dependency: the content-adaptive
S2 frame gate is thread-local. A worker without the main thread's decision
diverged on frame one. The core now exposes that decision for propagation,
and every worker installs it before mode selection.

## Unit 93 — make the VP9 two-loop count pass count-only

The fixed four-tile layout remains byte-identical at every worker count, but
the warmed medians are 1.55 s with one worker, 1.15 s with two, and 0.91 s
with four. The sub-linear 1.70x scaling confirms a material serial floor.
The post-Unit-92 profile places the inter modes writer and token writer on
that main-thread path.

The encoder previously implemented VP9's two-loop coefficient-probability
update by arithmetic-encoding every tile into a large throwaway buffer before
the real tile encode. Only the explicit `FrameCounts` mutations from that
first traversal are consumed. `BoolWriter::start_count_only` now preserves
the identical syntax/token walk while making its binary-symbol writes no-ops.
It also removes four full-frame-sized scratch allocations per inter frame.

the count-only writer and requires complete `FrameCounts` equality. The
four-tile product oracle remains byte-identical for one, two, and four
workers. A ten-pair alternating warmed comparison measured the count-only
build at

## Unit 94 — encode arithmetic column tiles concurrently

The post-count-only profile placed the real inter tile writer on 10.9% of

owned `TileCoefCtx` and `FrameCounts`. Scoped workers are capped by
`min(max_threads, tile_cols)`. The main thread joins and merges in column
order, preserving deterministic adapted counts and packet assembly.
Thread-local bit-accounting diagnostics deliberately retain the sequential
path.

The existing three-frame four-tile product oracle passed for one, two, and
four workers. Its packets, encoder reconstruction, and persistent per-tile
RD state remain byte-identical across worker counts. The full output stream
also remains byte-identical to Unit 93 with SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

## Unit 95 — run encoder loop filtering on a persistent wavefront pool

`StreamEncoder` now owns a long-lived loop-filter worker pool capped by
configured threads, legal column tiles, and superblock rows. After
reconstruction completes, the encoder reuses the core split-edge
column-wavefront driver: each worker builds its row masks, applies independent
SB rows, and uses the existing Acquire/Release column progress protocol for
the cross-row filter hazard. Single-worker encoders retain the serial driver.

A focused 256x256 differential test filters the same Y/U/V planes through
the serial driver and a four-worker wavefront and requires complete plane
identity. The existing three-frame four-tile product oracle remains
byte-identical for one, two, and four configured workers. The 120-frame
product stream remains byte-identical to Unit 94 with SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

## Post-Unit-95 profile and rejected experiments

A five-encode all-thread samply profile
(`/tmp/rvp9-unit95-profile.json.gz`) collected 3,847 main-thread samples,
5,632 persistent loop-filter worker samples, and 2,725 ephemeral tile-worker
thread records. The main threads spent 71.7% of wall samples below
`StreamEncoder::try_encode_one_popped`, 41.4% below
`encode_inter_internal`, and about 46% waiting in `std::thread::join`.
The ephemeral workers were dominated by
`pick_and_simulate_inter_encode_partitions` (44.7% inclusive),
`nonrd_partition::descend` (43.3%), mode picking (41.7%), and candidate
evaluation. Persistent loop-filter workers spent about 14% of their samples
filtering and the rest waiting between frame jobs, confirming that Unit 95
removed the former serial filter floor.

Three measured hypotheses were rejected and fully reverted:

- Reusing the loop-filter `WorkerPool` for tile picker and packet jobs removed
  ephemeral thread creation but produced no reproducible speed improvement.
  Order-reversed ten-encode aggregates were 7.87 s versus 7.83 s and 7.94 s
  versus 7.89 s. A first attempt also exposed that a pool sized by loop-filter
  SB rows cannot serve wider tile concurrency; any future shared pool must be
  sized for tile jobs and cap filter dispatch separately.
- Replacing the causal MI-grid row/column splat loop with slice `fill` kept
  identical bytes but was flat to slightly slower over ten alternating pairs.
  LLVM already lowers the simple cell loop effectively.
- Caching all segment quantizer/dequant/rdmult packs once per tile kept the
  cyclic-refresh and product oracles exact but split the alternating timing
  comparisons evenly. The per-leaf setup was too small to produce a stable
  end-to-end gain.

A reusable 16 KiB candidate-evaluation scratch pack likewise kept all
inter-mode, cyclic-AQ, and product oracles exact, but a clean 12-pair
comparison split 6–6 with only about 0.1% median difference. The compiler
already avoids the expected repeated initialization. It was fully reverted.

## Unit 97 — expose coefficient reductions to vectorization

The five-encode all-thread Unit-96 profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit96-profile.json.gz`. It collected 46,146 weighted samples,
including 10,788 samples in rvp9 code. Inter tile picking remained the
largest compute region. `reconstruct_via_round_trip` alone held 1,428 self

The main thread spent 35.2% of wall samples joining tile pickers, while
thread creation was below 1%, again confirming that persistent picker-pool
reuse is not the next bottleneck.

The Hadamard kernels were already NEON. The remaining coefficient-domain
SATD and squared-error reductions used `saturating_add` for every element.
Those saturations are impossible in the supported domain: 1,024
`i16::MIN` magnitudes sum to 33,554,432, and 1,024 maximum differences
between two i16-domain coefficients square and sum to
4,398,046,413,824. Both fit their `u32`/`i64` accumulators. Plain addition
preserves every valid result and lets LLVM vectorize the reductions.
Focused extreme-value tests pin both bounds.

The 120-frame output remains byte-identical with SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

extended border at frame edges, but repeated two coordinate clamps for every

the largest picker-self cluster at this call.

rows with the plane stride through the existing canonical projection

## Unit 102 — reject a global EightTap-only interpolation policy

The committed Unit-101 five-encode profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit101-profile.json.gz`. It collected 21,994 weighted samples,
including 5,946 rvp9 self samples. The largest remaining encoder clusters
were reconstruction, candidate evaluation, the tile picker, horizontal
convolution, token packing, loop filtering, and boolean writing. Runtime A4
instrumentation showed that 32x32 and 64x64 descent mode picks still consume
roughly 1.96–2.78 ms per inter frame; the realtime final pick correctly
reuses the descent result and costs zero.

Forcing the existing diagnostic `RVP9_RT_EIGHTTAP_ONLY=1` reduced ten
one-thread pairs from a 1.240953 s median to 1.201840 s, a 3.15% reduction
with ten wins. Twelve four-thread pairs moved from 0.730036 s to 0.712461 s,
a 2.41% reduction with ten wins. Pinned libvpx does not apply this global
shortcut: at cpu-used 7 it searches EightTap versus EightTapSmooth on a
chessboard subset and reuses neighbouring filter choices elsewhere
(`vp9_speed_features.c:699-749`, `vp9_pickmode.c:1851-1869,2307-2325`).

A temporary unshared clean-tree commit `00eeada` made the diagnostic the
default so the strict gate could measure the exact candidate. The canonical
Foreman product curve passed with `-7.9703376854%` BD-rate and a
`-0.3301974356 dB` matched-bitrate mean:
`target/stage4a_product/strict-baseline-00eeada63d73-1785482383954120000-p11178/stage4a_product_report.json`.
The result looked strong but did not generalise:

- 120-frame 320x256 Foreman CBR: `-0.322%` BD-rate versus Unit 101, with
  per-point PSNR movement from `+0.27` to `-0.11 dB`.
- 120-frame 1280x704 testsrc CBR: `+0.081%` BD-rate, but every matched-rate
  point lost `0.23–0.43 dB`.
- 120-frame 1280x704 moving noisy texture CBR: `+52.166%` BD-rate and every
  matched-rate point lost `0.15–0.43 dB`.

The noisy-content regression violates the per-clip and generalisation gates.
The candidate commit and source change were removed completely. Unit 101
remains the accepted baseline at `5ea223c`.

The exact next experiment is to reduce redundant A4 descent candidates using
libvpx's cpu-used 7 adaptive RD-threshold machinery without introducing
cross-tile or traversal-order dependence. Measure candidate counts first,
then test one deterministic threshold policy against Unit 101.

## Unit 103 — reject adaptive RD thresholds in speculative descent

The A4 descent normally passes no adaptive RD-threshold table because its
partition shapes are speculative and the persistent table is updated only
after a final leaf is committed. A diagnostic attached the current tile's
table read-only during descent while preserving the existing post-commit-only
updates.

Ten one-thread pairs improved from a 1.251055 s median to 1.243029 s
(`-0.64%`, eight wins). Twelve four-thread pairs improved from 0.736173 s to
0.731728 s (`-0.60%`, nine wins). The quality cost was not acceptable:

- 120-frame 1280x704 testsrc CBR regressed `+10.575%` BD-rate versus
  Unit 101, losing `0.07–0.30 dB` at the four measured targets.
- 120-frame 1280x704 moving noisy texture CBR regressed `+2.366%`
  BD-rate, crossing the per-clip limit.

The candidate did not reach a commit. The source change was removed
completely. Adaptive thresholds derived from previously committed leaves are
not a valid proxy for alternate partition shapes in rvp9's A4 descent.

The exact next experiment is to profile the keyframe path separately. It is
16.9% of main-thread samples and is independent of the inter-frame A4
quality-sensitive search. Select the largest keyframe-only leaf and require a
byte-exact speed improvement.

pre-loopfilter diagnostic snapshot. The regular Unit-101 profile's 289 main-
thread memmove samples had the same inter-frame source: three full-plane
clones on every frame even when no diagnostic read them.

## Unit 105 — share immutable lookahead source planes

The Unit 104 all-thread profile attributed recurring copies to the source
pipeline: `try_encode_one_popped` cloned all three lookahead planes to release
the ring borrow, and `PreAnalysisState::capture_last_source` copied luma again
after every encode. This was an ownership mismatch rather than codec work.
Libvpx retains ref-counted source buffers while rvp9 stored each immutable
plane in a `Vec<u8>`.

`LookaheadEntry::{y,u,v}` now use `Arc<[u8]>`. A popped entry clone increments
three reference counts, keeps the ring's `peek(-1)` source continuously valid,
and leaves pixels in the original lookahead allocations. Pre-analysis retains
the same luma allocation through
`PreAnalysisState::capture_last_source_shared`. The ordinary borrowed-slice
capture helper remains available for isolated callers and tests. TPL forward
lookahead now shares the same source planes instead of deep-copying them.
Focused tests prove cloned entries and Last_Source preserve both contents and
allocation identity.

## Unit 106 — reject packed coefficient-map keys

The Unit 104 main-thread profile attributed 5.13% inclusive time to the
bitstream's coefficient-map inserts and 1.38% to `DefaultHasher` tuple writes.
The tested hypothesis packed `(mi_row, mi_col, plane, tx_x4, tx_y4)` into one
linear `u64`, reducing each map operation from five integer hash writes to
one. Focused uniqueness, coefficient-source round-trip, AQ, release-build, and
byte-exact stream checks passed.

The candidate did not reduce compute cost. Sixteen alternating one-thread
pairs ran while an unrelated `mddosem` suite made wall time unusable, so the
decision used the child process's user CPU time as a provisional micro-oracle.
Unit 105 used a 1.195144 s median and the packed-key candidate used 1.202083 s;
the paired median delta was `+0.413%`, with only six candidate wins. Wall time
also moved `+0.125%` with seven wins, but is explicitly not trusted because
several pairs were descheduled for 0.5-1.1 seconds.

The extra multiply/add chain outweighed the reduced tuple hashing. The source
and test changes were removed completely; the worktree returned exactly to
committed Unit 105. Do not retry coordinate packing without a profile showing
different hardware/code-generation behavior. A custom trusted-key hasher is a
different hypothesis, but its current maximum measured opportunity is too
small to prioritize ahead of picker, packet, transform, or loopfilter work.

## Unit 108 — vectorize the 16x16 forward DCT on AArch64

architectures keep the scalar implementation.

`-255/0/255` blocks, and alternating residual extremes. Every coefficient is
exact.

## Unit 109 — reject preseeded tile reconstruction clones

The five-encode committed Unit 108 profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit108-profile.json.gz`. Its ephemeral tile workers collected
4,370 samples. The new 16x16 forward DCT removed the scalar butterfly:
`fdct16x16` fell to 100 inclusive samples and only 69 self samples remained.
The largest worker costs were partition picking (4,023 inclusive samples),
sub-pixel filtering (`evaluate_filter` at 1,361 inclusive samples),
reconstruction (479 inclusive samples), horizontal and vertical convolution
(308 and 187 self samples), sub-pixel variance (217 self samples), and frame
scratch movement (`memset` at 165 self samples). The main thread collected
3,741 samples; waits held about 38%, while `memmove` held 307 self samples,
including 136 in keyframe processing.

Tile workers allocated zero-filled full-frame Y/U/V reconstruction planes,
then immediately copied the LAST reference into all three planes before
partition picking. The tested candidate instead cloned LAST into each worker
plane and passed a contract flag that suppressed the later copy. Focused tests
proved both the copied and already-seeded paths. A four-tile product encode
was byte-identical to Unit 108, with stream SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

Two independent twenty-pair four-thread timing runs did not show a reliable
compute improvement. The first run measured Unit 108 at a 0.668450 s median
and the candidate at 0.666911 s. Paired wall time moved `-0.329%` with twelve
candidate wins; child user CPU moved only `-0.088%` with eleven wins. The
second run measured Unit 108 at 0.668047 s and the candidate at 0.667909 s.
Paired wall time moved `-0.130%` with eleven wins; child user CPU moved only
`-0.055%` with eleven wins. The candidate merely moved the same full-plane
copy into allocation, and the extra ownership contract added complexity
without a reproducible Pareto gain.

All candidate source and test changes were removed. Do not retry preseeded
full-frame reconstruction clones. A compact tile-local reconstruction layout
is a distinct architectural hypothesis, but it needs its own measured design
and is not justified by this result.

The exact next experiment is the measured AArch64 inverse 16x16 transform.
The Unit 108 profile attributes 91 self samples (2.08% of worker CPU) to
`idct16`, while pinned libvpx has a NEON implementation. Preserve the scalar
kernel as the oracle, add randomized coefficient/EOB coverage, and require
byte-exact stream and cross-decoder output before timing it.

## Unit 111 — vectorize fast 32x32 quantization on AArch64

The realtime 32x32 fast quantizer now dispatches to an eight-coefficient

toward zero, and reduces EOB from raster-order inverse-scan positions.

## Unit 112 — reject explicit vector multiplies in the 32x32 forward DCT

At committed Unit 111 baseline `9627fb7`, the captured `fdct32x4`
disassembly contains 260 lines and 24 scalar x-register multiplications.
The experiment rewrote `mul_add_round` with explicit duplicated constants,
`vmull`, and vector addition, intending to prevent scalarization.

The focused `fdct16x16` and `fdct32x32` scalar differential oracles passed,
but generated code became much worse: the candidate disassembly grew to
1,172 lines and 140 scalar x-register multiplications. The source and test
changes were fully reverted.

The baseline and candidate captures are
`/tmp/rvp9-unit111-fdct32x4.asm` and
`/tmp/rvp9-unit112-fdct32x4.asm`. Do not retry this helper-level rewrite.
A worthwhile 32x32 DCT change would require a faithful eight-wide i16
libvpx-style port, not another expression-level vector rewrite.

The next experiment must measure architecture-level redundant work first:
count speculative versus committed picker calls, candidates actually
evaluated, filter evaluations, and reconstructions by partition shape.
Use those counts to select one cache or work-elimination hypothesis.

## Unit 113 — measure picker work; reject luma-only early termination

Temporary thread-local counters on the exact 120-frame cpu-used 7 VBR input
measured 60,349 picker calls: 45,852 at 32x32 and 14,497 at 64x64. Every
queried `(position, bsize)` was a committed leaf under the large-frame
partition policy, so there is no discarded speculative picker layer to
cache away on this workload.

Those calls evaluated 122,982 mode candidates and 139,413 filter instances.
The averages were 2.356 candidates per 32x32 pick and 1.033 per 64x64 pick.
The exact mode distribution was:

- LAST NEAREST: 60,349;
- LAST NEW: 26,094;
- GOLDEN NEAREST: 20,222;
- GOLDEN NEW: 16,317;
- ZERO and NEAR: zero, because the existing duplicate-MV and mode-mask
  gates remove them before evaluation.

The temporary counters were removed after the measurement. Their
instrumented stream remained byte-identical with SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

A one-line experiment then skipped the Hadamard/quant pass whenever the
large luma model returned `SkipTxfm::AcDc`, mirroring only the luma half of
libvpx's early-termination structure. Sixteen one-thread pairs improved
wall time by `-2.648%` and child CPU by `-2.702%`, with sixteen wins.
Twenty four-thread pairs improved child CPU by `-2.319%`, with twenty
wins; loaded-host wall time improved only `-0.269%`.

The shortcut failed quality immediately. At nominal 2 Mbps, output fell
from 715,048 to 712,593 bytes, while average PSNR fell from 31.849277 dB
to 31.699229 dB and luma PSNR fell by 0.221720 dB. This is far too large
for a 0.34% payload reduction and does not merit a curve run. The source
change was fully reverted.

The remaining picker work is intrinsic candidate evaluation, not duplicate
partition calls. Do not retry luma-only model early termination. The next
byte-exact target is emitted transform/quant storage: each nonzero TX block
currently heap-allocates both qcoeff and short-lived dqcoeff vectors, even
though only qcoeff survives into the writer.

## Unit 114 — reject fixed dequant-coefficient return scratch

The emitted transform/quant experiment reused the existing 1,024-entry
transform-coefficient array as the returned i32 dequant buffer after
quantization. It removed the short-lived dqcoeff heap allocation on each
nonzero TX block while retaining qcoeff ownership in the writer.

The complete 512-test active encoder library suite passed with one ignored,
and the 120-frame product stream remained byte-identical with SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.
The allocation removal nevertheless made the product slower:

- sixteen one-thread pairs: wall `+0.448%`, child CPU `+0.382%`, only three
  candidate wins;
- twenty four-thread pairs: wall `+0.206%`, child CPU `+0.204%`, only four
  candidate wins.

Returning and moving the fixed 4 KiB array costs more than the allocator's
short-lived vector path on this host. The source change was fully reverted.
Do not replace the dqcoeff vector with a large by-value return again.

## Unit 115 — use AArch64 dot products for horizontal interpolation

The unscaled horizontal eight-tap interpolation path now follows pinned
libvpx's AArch64 dot-product arithmetic. Each eight-pixel group shares one
16-byte source load, uses libvpx's three permutation vectors to construct the
overlapping tap windows, and evaluates them with four `sdot` instructions.
The stable Rust toolchain still marks its dot-product intrinsics unstable, so
one scoped inline-assembly helper emits `sdot` under an explicit
`target_feature = "dotprod"` contract. `otool` confirms the release binary
contains the intended four-instruction sequence.

The safe wrapper detects dot-product support at runtime. It retains the
existing widened-i16 NEON path for a filter containing `128`, notably the
full-pel identity phase, because that tap cannot be represented in signed i8.
All other VP9 sub-pel filters use the new kernel. Existing differential
coverage exercised every phase of the regular, smooth, sharp, and bilinear
families over every supported shape; all cases matched the scalar oracle.

The standard 120-frame cpu-used 7 VBR stream remained byte-identical with
SHA-256
`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

## Unit 116 — use AArch64 dot products for vertical interpolation

The vertical eight-tap path now filters four output rows across eight columns
with signed dot products. Each group loads its eleven-row source window,
transposes the eight overlapping four-row groups with libvpx's table layout,
and evaluates four low/high tap pairs per output row. It deliberately reloads
the seven overlapping rows at the next group instead of carrying libvpx's
larger rolling transpose state. The existing widened-i16 NEON path remains the
full-pel fallback, and a scalar-NEON tail preserves arbitrary-height behavior.

The existing all-filter differential oracle covers every codec block shape
plus irregular `7x3`, `12x5`, and `63x9` dimensions. Horizontal, vertical,
and separable 2-D output all matched the scalar implementation.

## Unit 119 — fuse Hadamard quantization and RD metrics

The AArch64 Hadamard-only picker now quantizes native i16 transform
coefficients and returns EOB, qcoeff SATD, and squared coefficient error in
one pass. It no longer writes 64, 256, or 1,024 qcoeff and dqcoeff values to

emitted-coefficient paths remain unchanged.

accumulators. It was exact but introduced two dependent widening
multiply-accumulates per eight coefficients. Sixteen alternating one-thread

across low/high lanes and error across four independent i64 lanes removed
that dependency chain and reversed the result. Keep the split accumulator;
do not retry the compact serial form.

## Unit 120 — gather clamped SAD blocks by row spans

The five-encode committed Unit 119 profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit119-profile.json.gz`. Ephemeral tile workers collected 3,724
samples. Their largest self costs were candidate evaluation at 454
(`12.19%`), `reconstruct_via_round_trip` at 431 (`11.57%`), projection-ME
`sad_block_clamped` at 163 (`4.38%`), sub-pixel variance at 154 (`4.14%`),
32x32 forward DCT at 138 (`3.71%`), `_platform_memset` at 130 (`3.49%`),
and token writing at 129 (`3.46%`). The main thread still spent `36.17%` of
its samples joining ephemeral tile workers.

The fused quantizer is fully inlined into `reconstruct_via_round_trip`, so it
does not appear as an independent symbol. That parent leaf measured 431
samples versus Unit 116's 395, while total worker samples increased from
3,666 to 3,724. Sampling noise and changed inlining therefore cannot verify
Unit 119 by leaf counts; its alternating paired CPU result remains the causal
evidence.

Disassembly made the next cost concrete. An edge call to
`sad_block_clamped` first zeroed a 4,096-byte scratch array, then its nested
loop performed two coordinate clamps, a bounds check, one load, and one store
for every pixel. The new gather computes left/right replicated spans once per
block, clamps the vertical coordinate once per row, copies the visible middle
span, and fills only the two border spans. Interior probes retain their
direct-plane fast path.

A focused oracle compares the rowwise gather with the original per-pixel
`clamp_px` semantics for 8x8, 16x16, 32x32, and 64x64 blocks; partial
crossings on every edge; blocks wholly beyond the top-left and bottom-right;
and an interior block over a padded-stride plane. Every byte matches.

## Unit 121 — lazily initialize and reuse edge SAD scratch

The six post-projection SAD probes in one motion search previously gave each
edge call its own zero-initialized 4,096-byte array. Unit 121 carries one
`Option<[u8; 4096]>` through the search instead. Rust safely leaves the
inactive payload uninitialized. Interior-only searches never activate it;
the first edge probe initializes it once, and later edge probes overwrite and
reuse the active block. This removes repeated zero-fills without adding an
unsafe block.

Focused tests prove an interior probe leaves the option inactive and a second
8x8 edge probe preserves a marker outside its 64-byte active block, so it
cannot have zeroed the whole array again. Release disassembly shows the
expected option-discriminant check and one conditional `_bzero` on first use.

The standard 120-frame cpu-used 7 VBR stream remained byte-identical with
SHA-256

## Unit 124 — reuse encoder coefficient-context scratch

`encode_coefs` allocated and zeroed a token-context vector for every selected
transform block, including empty blocks. The decoder already carries a
thread-local cache without clearing it: VP9 context lookup reads only causal
neighbours, and the current scan writes every such entry before it can be
read. Unit 124 gives the encoder its own 1,024-byte thread-local cache and
puts the common empty-block EOB path ahead of the scratch borrow.

A focused regression first encodes the target sparse 4x4 block, then dirties
all 1,024 cache bytes through a dense 32x32 block, and encodes the sparse block
again. Its bytes remain identical. All 21 focused `encode_coefs` tests pass.

## Unit 126 — eight-wide i16 first pass for the 32x32 DCT

The encoder calls rvp9's full-precision `fdct32x32`, matching
`vpx_fdct32x32`, rather than libvpx's all-i16 `vpx_fdct32x32_rd` shortcut.
Unit 126 therefore keeps the full transform. It factors the audited
seven-stage schedule into one width-generic implementation, instantiates the
bounded first pass over eight i16 NEON lanes, halves intermediate storage,
then widens each eight-lane row group into two existing i32x4 second passes.
This differs from libvpx only in widening the full second pass rather than
selected overflow-sensitive stages; `notes/divergence-ledger.md` records the
trade.

blocks with stride jitter, three constant blocks, and the alternating

The token leaf reveals duplicate work across the two mandatory tile

histogram needed to choose coefficient-probability updates. The later
arithmetic pass nevertheless allocates per-tile count banks, repeats every
count update, and merges those banks solely to recreate the same adaptation
input. `s5_tile_inter_accumulates_frame_counts` already proves that count-only
and arithmetic traversals produce equal counts.

The exact next experiment is to reuse the count-only pass's complete
`FrameCounts` for backward adaptation and run the arithmetic tile traversal
without count banks. Preserve additive output-slot semantics, discard only
the encoder-only full coefficient histogram after building the header plan,
and strengthen the focused oracle to cover coefficient counts across
different probability tables. The product stream and decoded output must
remain byte-identical before timing.

## Unit 130 — reuse pre-header count-pass results

The pre-header count-only traversal is now the canonical source for both the
coefficient-probability update plan and the frame's backward-adaptation
counts. After building the plan, the encoder discards only the encoder-only
full 12-token histogram, adds the remaining decoder-shaped counts to the
caller's output slot, and runs arithmetic tile emission without per-tile
count banks. This preserves the existing additive output-slot contract.

The focused
`s5_tile_inter_count_only_matches_emit_across_probability_updates` oracle now
uses a non-skip block, confirms coefficient EOB counts are exercised, and
compares the complete count banks while the two traversals use different
skip and coefficient probability tables. The count banks are identical.

(`2.80%`).

Two near-equal Unit 130 captures attribute 72-74 inclusive samples to
`BuildHasher::hash_one`, 53-74 to `HashMap::insert`, and 44-64 to
`RawTable::reserve_rehash`. Direct stack inspection found 88 of 91 sampled
hash frames under `pick_and_simulate_inter_encode_partitions`; only four were
under the emitted coefficient source. The dominant hash work is therefore
the per-superblock `descent_pick_cache`, not the coefficient map whose packed
key Unit 106 rejected.

That cache's legal key space is bounded and collision-free without hashing.
One 64x64 superblock can evaluate at most 85 square candidates
(`1 + 4 + 16 + 64`) and 42 horizontal/vertical rectangle candidates
(`2 * (1 + 4 + 16)`), for 127 total. A key maps directly from its local 8x8
cell, `BlockSize::idx()`, and a superblock-scoped fixed slot table.

The exact next experiment is a generic fixed-slot superblock cache backed by
an insertion-order value vector. Preserve replacement behavior, test all 127
legal square/rectangle keys and absolute-superblock alias isolation, and
change only `descent_pick_cache`. Require exact product bytes and repeated
paired speed evidence before keeping it.

## Unit 131 — direct-index the partition-descent result cache

The first focused implementation used the estimated 127 square/rectangle
candidate bound from Unit 131's selection note. The product stream and focused
test passed, but the full encoder library suite correctly found eight
configurations that evaluate more distinct keys and tripped the bound. No
commit was made. The corrected implementation covers the complete bounded
domain: 64 local superblock cells × all 13 VP9 block sizes = 832 slots, with
`u16::MAX` as the empty sentinel and a growing insertion-order value vector.

The focused
`descent_pick_cache_covers_complete_superblock_key_space` oracle exhausts all
832 keys, verifies every lookup, replaces an existing value without growing
the vector, and checks that local-slot aliases remain isolated by the
per-superblock cache scope. The complete encoder suite then passed.

The final-source five-encode Unit 131 profile is

hash-leaf samples below `nonrd_partition::descend` fell from fifteen to zero.

The updated self-time ranking is candidate evaluation at 683 (`15.02%`),

(`3.25%`), sub-pixel variance at 144 (`3.17%`), and memset/vertical
interpolation at 128 each (`2.81%`).

Address-level symbolization attributes 669 of 683 candidate-evaluator samples
to the inlined per-filter call site. Its AArch64 prologue reserves `0x2ab0`
bytes (10,928 bytes) and touches three stack pages. The body declares an
optional 4,096-byte reconstruction array even though the production
Hadamard-only calibration never initializes or reads it. Rust correctly
skips the pixel copy on that path, but a stack-resident `Option<[u8; 4096]>`
still reserves the maximum payload in every call.

The exact next experiment is a second per-worker thread-local 4,096-byte
scratch for the compatibility reconstruction path. The Hadamard-only path
must continue to borrow or initialize no reconstruction pixels; the
compatibility path must overwrite only its active prefix before use. Add a
causal oracle that dirties the scratch with a 64x64 candidate between two
smaller identical evaluations. Require a smaller candidate-evaluator stack
frame, exact results, exact product bytes, and paired speed evidence.

## Unit 132 — reject reusable reconstruction scratch

The experiment moved compatibility-mode reconstruction pixels into a second
thread-local buffer and force-inlined the shared evaluator body. The existing

cover both prediction and reconstruction scratch. All 1,569 applicable core
tests and 514 active encoder tests passed, with the usual two absent-vector
filters and one ignored encoder test. Warnings-denied core clippy also passed.

The structural result was real. Unit 131's inlined evaluator reserved
10,928 stack bytes and touched three pages. The final experimental build
reserved 2,992 bytes and had no out-of-line evaluator call. Product and

`7b60c3c0e59d69ed0199729744aab63c9cde6887438e94e5f905b6ff2158c8da`.

## Unit 134 — exact AArch64 NEON 16-tap loop filter

The four AArch64 16-tap DSP slots now dispatch to eight-lane NEON kernels.
Horizontal kernels load contiguous lanes. Vertical kernels transpose a
16-by-8 neighborhood, filter across vectors, and scatter the changed columns.
Dual slots apply the same single-edge kernel at the two VP9 edge offsets.

The mask deliberately differs from libvpx's saturating-byte implementation:
rvp9 widens
`2 * abs(p0 - q0) + abs(p1 - q1) / 2` to `u16` before comparing it with
`blimit`. That preserves the existing scalar result across the complete
`u8` threshold API, including `blimit = 255`. Staged vector selects preserve
mixed flat/flat2 lanes without aggregate branch shortcuts.

Two randomized differential tests cover 256 seeds each across single and
dual horizontal/vertical kernels, varied strides, random thresholds, flat
regions, step edges, and all-255 thresholds. They compare the complete
backing plane with the scalar kernels. The existing
`split_edge_parallel_filter_matches_serial_planes_bit_exact` reconstructed
Y/U/V oracle also passed. All 1,572 applicable core tests passed after
filtering the two absent-vector cases; all 517 active encoder library tests
passed with one ignored. Warnings-denied core all-target clippy, formatting,
and diff checks passed.

## Unit 135 — select redundant product-picker SSE removal

The committed Unit 134 profile attributes 640 rvp9 self samples (`10.26%`)
to the inlined candidate evaluator. Of those, 460 land in the loop at
binary offsets `+0x10a0..+0x10f0`; disassembly shows source/pred byte loads,
subtract-square-accumulate, and its row/column bounds. This is
`sse_block(src, recon_pixels)`.

The Stage 4a product calibration always enables Hadamard-only picking.
Therefore `recon_pixels` is exactly `pred`, and the scan returns
`SSE(src, pred)`. The earlier `model_rd_for_sb_y{,_large}` call has already
computed that same complete block reduction as `mrd.sse_y`; the skip
tie-break deliberately reuses it later in the function. The product path
currently scans every candidate's luma pixels twice for one identical value.

The exact next experiment is to use `mrd.sse_y` as the surfaced pixel
distortion when `hadamard_only` is true, retaining `sse_block` only for the
compatibility reconstruction path. Add a focused result-identity oracle that
exercises both calibrations and a direct varied-shape SSE/model equality
oracle. Require exact product bytes, cross-decoder identity, and repeated
paired one-/four-thread speed evidence before keeping it.

## Unit 135 — reuse exact model-RD SSE in the product picker

The product Hadamard-only evaluator now surfaces `mrd.sse_y` instead of

reconstruction. The focused oracle independently builds zero-MV predictions
for 8x8, 16x16, 32x32, and 64x64 blocks, then requires direct pixel SSE,
model-RD `sse_y`, and candidate `best_distortion` to agree exactly.

## Unit 136 — select full-width Hadamard dequant multiply

The committed Unit 135 address map puts most
`reconstruct_via_round_trip` samples in the 8x8/16x16 Hadamard
quantize-metrics body. Its `quantize_i16_8` dequant step expresses the low
and high halves as two widening four-lane multiplies, then narrows and
combines them. Disassembly strength-reduces each widening/narrowing chain,
but still emits two `mul.4h` instructions per eight coefficients.

The scalar contract casts `qcoeff * dequant` back to `i16`, so only the low
16 product bits are observable. A single `vmulq_s16` over all eight lanes is
exactly equivalent, and the existing metric accumulator can widen that
result unchanged.

The exact next experiment is to replace only that Hadamard-metrics dequant
expression with one eight-lane low-half multiply. Require the existing
random/extreme metrics differential, exact product bytes, and paired timing.
Reject it if the final machine text or product timing does not improve.

final-scan-only, `i16::MIN`, and `i16::MAX` coefficients for Tx8x8, Tx16x16,
and Tx32x32 across qindices 0, 1, 20, 80, 160, and 255.

## Unit 137 — select mixed direct/clamped integer projections

The committed Unit 135 profile attributes 81 self samples directly to
integer-projection ME: 32 at the clamped row/column loop backedge, 15 in the
projection setup, 17 in `vector_match`, and 17 in its supporting sampled
symbols. Disassembly shows the edge path repeatedly clamping both coordinates
inside every pixel sum.

At a 64x64 frame-edge superblock, most of the 128-column projection window
is still visible. The current all-or-nothing `fill_int_pro_rows` gate sends
all eight 16-column chunks through scalar clamping when only two chunks lie
outside the left or right edge. The column projection similarly sends every
row through per-pixel clamping when only the top or bottom portion is
replicated.

clamped column rows as left/middle/right spans. Add a pixel-oracle
differential for partial and fully outside projection windows. Preserve every
integer projection, selected MV, SAD, and product byte before measuring when
host contention permits.

## Unit 137 — mixed direct/clamped integer projections

`fill_int_pro_rows` now chooses the direct 16-column NEON kernel per chunk,
so six of eight chunks remain vectorized at a 64x64 left/right edge SB.
Clamped row projections hoist their fixed x coordinate and use a direct
vertical walk whenever y is visible. Clamped column projections reduce a
row as replicated-left, contiguous-visible, and replicated-right spans
after clamping y once.
