## Unit 138 — select retained coefficient tokens

The committed Unit 137 profile attributes 312 self samples, 8.47% of all
rvp9 samples, to `write_block_tokens`. Source inspection finds that rvp9
scans, classifies, and context-models every coefficient twice: once in the
pre-header count pass and again in the final arithmetic pass. The count pass
must precede coefficient-probability updates, but coefficient values, token
classes, scan bands, and neighbour contexts do not depend on those
probabilities.

Pinned libvpx already separates these concerns. `vp9_tokenize.c::tokenize_b`
retains `TOKENEXTRA` records before the compressed header, then
`vp9_bitstream.c::pack_mb_tokens` replays them against the post-header
probability tables. The exact next experiment is the same architecture in
the narrow inter-tile path: retain symbolic coefficient records per tile
during the canonical count pass, then replay them during final tile packing.

Keep the existing public tile writer unchanged for decoder tests and other
callers. Add an opt-in record/replay writer entry point, reject a replay whose
block count differs from the syntax traversal, and preserve final
post-header probability lookup. Require byte-identical product output,
focused direct-vs-replay token tests, all three cross-decoders, and repeated
one-/four-thread timing before accepting the change.

## Unit 138 — retained coefficient tokens

The pre-header count pass now retains one compact coefficient stream per
tile. Each four-byte token stores its signed value plus scan band and
neighbour-derived context; separate block boundaries retain the coefficient
context writeback flag. Final tile workers replay immutable per-tile streams
against the post-header coefficient probabilities. The direct public tile
writer remains unchanged, and replay returns
`ModesWriterError::RetainedCoefMismatch` unless it consumes every recorded
block and token.

The count-only writer skips discarded coefficient arithmetic while recording.
Replay bypasses scan selection and neighbour-context folding. A focused
probability-change oracle covers empty blocks, zero runs, signed low tokens,
CAT1 through CAT6 representatives, terminal EOB, and full-to-`seg_eob`
blocks. It proves replay bytes match a direct encode under a probability
table different from the recording table.

## Unit 139 — select libvpx two-stage interpolation-filter search

The committed Unit 138 profile attributes 750 inclusive samples to

single-filter path. Add a focused oracle for model-domain selection and
require cross-decoder correctness, measured speed, and fresh Stage 4a
quality evidence because the corrected filter choice can deliberately change
the stream.

## Unit 141 — select persistent tile workers

Matched `samply` runs now compare the committed Unit 140 encoder with pinned

binary self samples across ten processes, while keeping its tile workers
alive for the stream. The active work is therefore much closer than the
loaded-host wall-time ratio suggests; repeated thread construction and
per-frame join machinery are an architectural speed difference.

## Unit 144 — select dispatched source-SAD and variance kernels

The all-superblock source-SAD pass is still one of the largest mapped
main-thread costs. `pre_analysis.rs::sb_sad_and_var` walks every pixel in

- 64x64: `303.12 ns` versus `304.62 ns`.

## Unit 173 — accept pairwise Hadamard SATD accumulation

The normal product picker uses the fused rate-only Hadamard quantizer on
every candidate. Its SATD accumulator widened the low and high qcoeff halves
to i32 separately, took two absolute values, and maintained two u32 vectors.
NEON can take the exact absolute i16 lanes and pairwise-widen-add them into
one u32 accumulator. Unsigned reinterpretation preserves `abs(i16::MIN) =
32768`, and the 1,024-coefficient maximum sum fits u32.

The existing narrowed-versus-widened differential covers all realtime
transform sizes, six qindices, random coefficients, signed extremes,
all-zero, DC-only, and final-scan blocks. It passes unchanged. The complete
seven-test AArch64 quantizer module, core all-target clippy, formatting, and
diff checks pass. The standard stream remains exactly 716,330 bytes with
SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

Four independent twenty-pair comparisons favor the candidate:

- one thread: `-0.162%` and `-0.215%` total child CPU;
- four threads: `-0.292%` and `-0.163%` total child CPU.

The gain is small but reproducible, exact, and directly removes SIMD work in
the fresh profile's largest leaf. Retain it. Take a new accepted-head profile
before changing another round-trip operation.

## Unit 190 — reject replacing A4 with the variance partition tree

The first architecture-level A/B used the existing
`RVP9_A4_RD_PARTITION_DISABLE=1` diagnostic to restore the source-faithful
cpu-used 7 variance tree and skip rvp9's speculative picker descent. This was
decisively slower on the 1280x704 120-frame product workload: twenty
four-thread pairs regressed wall by `+58.175%` with 0/20 wins and total child
CPU by `+79.707%` with 0/20 wins. The variance tree creates enough smaller
final leaves that their emit work costs far more than the avoided descent.

`RVP9_A4_PROFILE=1` explains the accepted path. Large-frame recovery already
clamps descent to 32x32/64x64, and every committed leaf reuses the identical
descent pick (`same == committed`); the separately timed final picker is zero.
Per-tile descent is roughly 0.4--0.8 ms and emit roughly 0.2--0.4 ms on the
profiled frames. A4 is therefore both a partition decision and the only mode
pick for committed leaves, not a simple duplicate pass.

Keep A4. Do not retest the pure variance tree unless its leaf-size distribution
changes first. The next bounded search-breadth hypothesis is the existing
cpu-used 7 large-frame ML search breakout: it is default-on only when
`base_qindex >= 100`, leaving the high-bitrate speed workload unpruned. Add a
diagnostic all-q override, measure its fire rate and large-frame speed, and run
a large-frame quality comparison before considering any default change.

## Unit 191 — reject wider ML-breakout activation

The standard 2000 kbps workload actually runs at `base_qindex = 255`, so the
source-faithful `base_qindex >= 100` ML gate is already active. An all-q
diagnostic produced the identical 716,330-byte stream and neutral twenty-pair
timing. Threshold sweeps from the current `-20` through `-1000` also left the
stream and partition-call distribution unchanged.

An instrumented two-frame run at the deliberately extreme `-3e38` threshold
proved the model receives finite real inputs and returns `true`. The apparent
inertia comes from `variance_hint_bounds`: many superblocks have
`max_partition_size = 32x32`. Their 64x64 NONE arm is disallowed, so breakout
cannot fire until the four 32x32 floor nodes, where there is no recursion left
to suppress. On 64x64-eligible blocks the existing `-20` policy has already
captured the useful breakouts. The extreme policy regressed a twenty-pair
four-thread comparison by `+0.086%` wall and `+0.515%` total child CPU.

The all-q gate, temporary input logging, and forced activation are fully
removed. Do not retune the ML threshold without first changing which parent
sizes are eligible; the model is not the active limit on this workload.

The existing `RVP9_RT_DISABLE_GOLDEN=1` diagnostic removed GOLDEN-reference

at 500 kbps and 0.24 dB at 1,500 kbps.

next experiment should retain GOLDEN but avoid redundant work between LAST and

or prune only a measured block-size/mode combination and gate it with a full
curve before changing the default.

must target a candidate class that runs on most frames. Measure GOLDEN winner
and candidate counts by block size and mode first, then prune only a class that
is both expensive and rarely decisive; use the full CBR curve before any
default change.

## Units 195--199 — reject GOLDEN NEWMV and motion-search shortcuts

An environment-gated picker profile over all 120 standard-product frames
recorded 60,664 picker calls. Block32x32 accounted for 46,272 calls and 37,086
GOLDEN candidate evaluations; GOLDEN won 6,260 of them (3,937 NEAREST and 2,323
NEW). Block64x64 accounted for 14,392 calls but only 64 GOLDEN evaluations and
13 GOLDEN winners. GOLDEN's active cost and value are therefore concentrated
in 32x32 leaves. The raw profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit195-golden-profile-full.txt`.

Unit 195 removed only GOLDEN NEWMV. It improved a twenty-pair four-thread run
by `-2.058%` wall and `-3.481%` total child CPU, but average PSNR collapsed from
31.935117 dB to 31.082530 dB at the matched 2,000 kbps VBR point. The IVF
shrinking from 716,330 to 713,823 bytes does not compensate for the 0.852587 dB
loss. Reject without spending a full curve on a clearly invalid operating
point.

The existing predicted-MV SAD mask cannot safely separate these winners. Of
50,817 profile calls with a finite nonzero LAST SAD, tightening the current
2.0x GOLDEN/LAST cutoff to 1.875x would newly mask only 382 calls while
rejecting 15 observed GOLDEN winners. A 1.5x cutoff would mask 1,918 calls and
reject 164 winners. Do not retune this threshold from this corpus.

Unit 196 reused LAST's already-computed NEWMV as GOLDEN's NEWMV while retaining
the independent GOLDEN RD evaluation. It improved wall by `-1.196%` and child
CPU by `-1.346%` with 20/20 user-time wins, but lost 0.450240 dB average PSNR;
the IVF was 711,566 bytes. Independent GOLDEN motion is required.

Unit 197 reduced the existing `RVP9_RT_NEWMV_SUBPEL_ITERS` diagnostic from two
checks per level to one. It lost 0.265160 dB while timing was neutral
(`-0.190%` wall, `-0.115%` child CPU). Unit 198 forced the existing fast-diamond
variant; it was byte-exact and timing-neutral (`-0.073%` wall, `+0.025%` child
CPU). Unit 199 capped full-pixel diamond depth at 8, 6, 4, 2, and 0; every form
was byte-exact. Two default-versus-zero comparisons were neutral to slower
(`+0.200%`/`+0.130%` wall and `+0.041%`/`+0.023%` child CPU). These controls do
not remove active work on this workload.

All temporary profiling, pruning, and motion-reuse code is removed. Keep the
independent LAST/GOLDEN searches and the two-level sub-pixel refinement. The
next experiment should return to the committed profile and target an actually
hot implementation kernel rather than removing search breadth whose quality
value is now measured.

## Unit 200 — reject transform-sized DCT scratch arrays

`reconstruct_via_round_trip` allocated 1,024-element coefficient, quantized,
and dequantized arrays even for Tx8x8 and Tx16x16. A byte-exact rewrite used
64-, 256-, or 1,024-element arrays selected with the transform, removed one
copy, and reduced the release binary by 16 bytes. The standard stream remained
exactly 716,330 bytes with the committed SHA-256.

Whole-product timing rejected the apparent cleanup. Two twenty-pair,
four-thread comparisons regressed child CPU by `+0.642%` and `+0.319%`, with
only 5/20 and 8/20 wins. Wall regressed `+0.617%` and `+0.242%`. LLVM's
existing stack/lifetime optimization is more effective than the specialized
control flow on the product workload. The rewrite is fully removed.

Do not infer stack-zeroing cost from source array extents. The next
implementation candidate should remove a measured operation or route an
existing scalar kernel through proven SIMD, then verify at whole-product level.

## Unit 201 — reject picker EOB-bucketed inverse dispatch

The picker reconstruction was routed through the same EOB buckets and inverse
dispatch used by the final encoder/decoder (`1`, `10`/`12`, `34`/`38`, `135`,
then dense). The standard stream remained byte-exact, showing the candidate did
not perturb decisions on this workload.

Timing was consistently worse. Two twenty-pair four-thread comparisons
regressed total child CPU by `+0.901%` and `+0.232%`, and wall by `+1.053%` and
`+0.488%`. The candidate profile at
`/tmp/rvp9-unit201-profile-analysis.txt` still attributes samples to dense
`idct32`/`idct32x32_1024_add` and shows no picker sparse-kernel symbol. This
path's nonzero blocks are not entering useful sparse buckets often enough to
pay for dispatch.

The inverse-dispatch rewrite is fully removed. Do not add per-round-trip EOB
dispatch without a measured sparse-bucket population on the target corpus.

## Unit 202 — reject fixed-stack emitted dqcoeff return

`inter_forward_quant_one_tx` normally widens its 1,024-element i16 dqcoeff
scratch into a short-lived `Vec<i32>` for the final inverse transform. A
byte-exact candidate returned the fixed i16 array directly and widened only
the active transform prefix into stack scratch at the inverse call, removing
one heap allocation per nonzero transform. Binary size and the standard stream
were unchanged.

Two twenty-pair four-thread comparisons regressed child CPU by `+0.731%` and
`+0.655%`, with only 3/20 and 4/20 wins. Wall changed `+0.366%` and `+0.205%`.
The fixed 2 KB return/move and 4 KB inverse scratch cost more than the
short-lived vector allocation. The candidate is fully removed.

Keep the owned dqcoeff vector until profiling identifies allocator cost. Avoid
large fixed-array returns as an allocation substitute on this ABI.

## Units 203--204 — reject remaining partition/filter breadth switches

The refreshed matched standard-product timing is still far outside parity:
twenty pairs put rvp9 at `2.3407x` libvpx wall and `1.8421x` total child CPU
(rvp9 0.5970 s wall / 1.0451 s CPU; libvpx 0.2552 s / 0.5695 s). This is an
architectural CPU-work gap, not measurement noise.

Unit 203 disabled rectangular A4 partition candidates on the existing
large-frame 32x32 floor. The stream was byte-exact, and timing was neutral to
slower (`+0.194%` wall, `+0.368%` child CPU). The active ML rect pruner already
removes those arms. A two-frame `RVP9_A4_PROFILE=1 RVP9_RT_PROFILE=1` trace
also shows every large-frame A4 pick becomes a committed leaf: final picker
time is zero, and the per-size call counts exactly equal committed counts.
There is no duplicate final mode pick left to remove.

The full 120-frame picker profile records 86,581 LAST and 37,150 GOLDEN
candidate evaluations across 60,664 leaf picks, only 2.04 candidates per pick
on average. Mode-count pruning is already tight.

Unit 204 forced every candidate to use EightTap without interpolation-filter
search. It improved wall by `-0.485%` and child CPU by `-0.794%`, but average
PSNR fell from 31.935117 dB to 31.495740 dB and the IVF shrank from 716,330 to
710,986 bytes. The 0.439377 dB loss decisively rejects the switch.

The temporary filter-search override is removed. Do not expect another search
breadth toggle to close the measured 1.84x CPU gap: the remaining candidates,
references, and filters have all shown material quality value. Investigate
whole-program code generation or a more faithful lower-cost non-RD model next.

## Unit 205 — reject single-workload profile-guided optimization

An external release build used Rust/LLVM profile generation, trained on the
standard 120-frame cpu-used 7 VBR workload, merged the raw counters with Apple
LLVM 21 `llvm-profdata`, and rebuilt with `-C profile-use`. No repository or
release-profile setting changed. The optimized binary produced the exact
716,330-byte stream with the committed SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

Two twenty-pair comparisons found a repeatable child-CPU improvement of
`-1.639%` and `-1.902%`, but wall time regressed `+1.368%` and `+0.742%`.
The training run also reported exhausted static counter storage, and the use
build identified broad missing-function coverage outside the one trained
configuration. This is neither an end-to-end speed win nor representative
training for the required feature matrix, so a production PGO pipeline would
add build complexity without a measured acceptance benefit.

The external candidate and profile remain under `/tmp`; the worktree is
unchanged. Do not adopt PGO from this single workload. The next experiment
should isolate the unusually high allocation/system-CPU share or remove a hot
per-transform allocation without returning large fixed arrays.

## Unit 206 — retain coefficient-domain picker distortion

Stage 4a VBR temporarily disabled its S3 coefficient-domain distortion, which
routes the AArch64 Hadamard picker through the rate-only quantization kernel.
The candidate improved wall by `-4.328%` and child CPU by `-4.680%`, winning
all 20 paired samples. The saving is real, but the quality cost is prohibitive:
the standard stream fell from 716,330 to 708,362 bytes and average PSNR fell
from 31.935117 to 29.523095 dB (`-2.412022 dB`).

The one-line policy change is fully removed. S3's quantization-error metric is
a measured quality requirement, not optional diagnostic work. A lower-cost
model must approximate that metric closely enough to preserve its candidate
ranking; simply reverting to pixel-domain prediction SSE spends far more than
the available quality margin.

## Unit 207 — reject sparse Hadamard quantization-error correction

An AArch64 candidate rewrote coefficient error as unquantized Hadamard energy
plus `dq * (dq - 2*c)` correction. The unquantized term came from the already
available prediction SSE using the transform's energy gain; all-zero groups
could then bypass the 64-bit correction accumulator. Differential quantizer
tests passed. The standard product stream also stayed byte-exact at 716,330
bytes, confirming that the small 16x16/32x32 integer-shift approximation did
not change this workload's decisions.

The extra per-group nonzero reduction erased the intended saving. Two
twenty-pair comparisons regressed child CPU by `+0.936%` and `+0.105%`, with
8/20 and 9/20 wins; wall changed `+0.704%` and `+0.407%`. The complete
candidate is removed. The existing four independent 64-bit accumulators are
already the faster implementation on this Apple AArch64 core.

## Unit 208 — retain per-tile reconstruction and MV scratch

Matched thread-count diagnostics showed the gap grows with tile parallelism:
the one-thread cpu-used 7 comparison was `1.673x` total CPU and `1.670x` wall,
while two threads reached `1.793x` CPU and `2.594x` wall. The parallel rvp9
path allocated and zeroed a full-frame YUV reconstruction plus MV grid for
every column tile on every inter frame.

`StreamEncoder` now owns one frame-shaped scratch set per configured column
tile and reuses it across frames. Jobs still own disjoint active rectangles;
the merge reads only those rectangles, so stale pixels outside a job's tile
are unobservable. The four-tile deterministic regression now checks both
thread-count byte identity and stable scratch allocation addresses across
consecutive inter frames.

The standard stream remains byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.
Two twenty-pair comparisons reduced system CPU by `-15.760%` and `-15.797%`,
total child CPU by `-1.377%` and `-0.947%`, and wall by `-0.281%` and
`-0.535%`. Focused test and encoder-library clippy both pass. Keep the change.

The next tile-overhead target is the four full-frame nested partition/history
clones per frame. Any replacement must preserve independent per-column RD and
partition history state and the existing thread-count byte identity.

## Unit 209 — reject active-tile-only MV-grid clearing

With retained tile scratch in place, each tile job still reset every cell in
its frame-shaped MV grid before writing only its active columns. Restricting
the reset to those columns was byte-exact and passed the four-tile worker-count
regression. One twenty-pair run improved wall/CPU by `-0.653%`/`-0.816%`, but
the repeat under higher host load was neutral (`-0.036%` wall, `+0.115%` CPU;
8/20 CPU wins). The extra row-slice loop does not provide a reproducible
whole-product improvement over the contiguous full-grid fill.

The change is removed. Keep the contiguous clear; target allocation and deep
clone costs rather than subdividing this small linear write.

## Unit 210 — retain active-tile-only partition and history clones

Every column-tile job deep-cloned the leaf vectors for every superblock in the
frame, although it only mutates its own columns. It also cloned exact-VBP
partition history even though that experimental path is disabled by default.
Jobs now allocate empty inactive partition slots, clone only their active
superblock columns, and copy VBP history only when `RVP9_EXACT_VBP_TREE` is
enabled. The deterministic merge still copies only each job's active columns.

The standard cpu-used 7 VBR stream remains byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with
SHA-256 `8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.
Two twenty-pair ABBA comparisons improved total child CPU by `-0.650%` and
`-0.716%`, with 18/20 and 16/20 wins; wall improved `-1.411%` and `-0.795%`,
with 19/20 and 18/20 wins. The four-tile regression passes for the default and
exact-VBP paths across one, two, and four workers, and encoder-library clippy
passes with warnings denied. Keep the change.

The remaining result merge clones each active partition vector a second time.
Move those vectors out of the completed tile result before attempting a larger
coefficient-source reuse change.

## Unit 211 — reject moving completed tile state during merge

Moving active partition vectors, exact-VBP history entries, and the active RD
table out of each completed tile result preserved the exact standard stream and
passed both four-tile worker-count regressions. It did not produce a stable
end-to-end speed win. Two twenty-pair comparisons measured wall at `-0.098%`
then `+0.271%`, and total child CPU at `+0.027%` then `-0.539%`; wins were
12/20 and 10/20 for wall, 10/20 and 11/20 for CPU. System CPU also changed
direction between runs.

The transfer is below measurement noise because the destination retains the
same allocations either way. The change is removed. Proceed to the larger
four-full-frame coefficient-source allocation and merge cost.

## Unit 212 — retain tile-local coefficient slot maps

Each parallel tile picker allocated and initialized a dense coefficient slot
map for the whole frame, then the main thread scanned all four full maps while
merging. `VecBackedInterCoefSource` can now represent a global frame-coordinate
column range with local dense storage. Each tile job allocates only its luma
and chroma columns; merging maps those local slots into the full-frame source.
Across four column tiles, the job slot maps now contain exactly one frame of
slots in total rather than four, and the merge examines each job slot once.

The standard cpu-used 7 VBR stream remains byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with
SHA-256 `8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.
Two twenty-pair comparisons improved wall by `-2.823%` and `-0.644%`, with
17/20 and 12/20 wins, and total child CPU by `-1.067%` and `-0.529%`, with
15/20 and 11/20 wins. Direct tile-slot allocation/merge tests, the default and
exact-VBP four-tile worker-count regressions, formatting, and encoder-library
clippy all pass. Keep the change.

The tile sources still allocate their local dense slot arrays and coefficient
block vectors on every inter frame. Profile the retained implementation before
deciding whether persistent per-tile coefficient scratch justifies widening
the picker interface.

## Unit 213 — retain direct per-leaf keyframe simulation

Fresh matched profiles showed the single normal-GOP keyframe consuming 17.5%
of rvp9 binary samples. A ten-keyframe diagnostic measured rvp9 at `6.946x`
pinned libvpx total CPU. The keyframe picker constructed a frame-sized sparse
superblock layout and a new hash-backed coefficient source for every leaf,
rescanned the whole superblock grid, then merged that one leaf's coefficients.

The simulator now accepts an optional active leaf and a caller-owned output
source. The causal picker encodes the selected leaf directly into one retained
frame source; full-layout callers keep their existing raster walk. The intra
source reuses the direct physical-transform slot map already proven for inter
coefficients, removing hash work on insertion and bitstream lookup.

The normal 120-frame product stream remains byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with
SHA-256 `8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.
Ten consecutive keyframes also remain byte-exact at 573,684 bytes with SHA-256
`36d3e144be949c674f7d4aaab0fc17d2aaf1d76572a4e6fee7c0859cd8060264`.
The ten-keyframe paired diagnostic improved wall and total CPU to `0.941x` the
old implementation; the remaining matched libvpx CPU ratio is `6.698x`.
Two normal-GOP twenty-pair runs improved paired wall by `-0.681%` and
`-1.121%`, and total child CPU by `-0.302%` and `-1.281%`.

All 24 keyframe-filtered encoder tests pass, including two-tile decode and
chaotic intra-mode round trips. The focused direct-source and per-segment
quantizer tests, formatting, diff checks, and encoder-library clippy also pass.
Keep the change. The remaining keyframe gap is transform/quantization work,
not container overhead; select the next hypothesis from the keyframe profile.

## Unit 214 — reject libvpx's realtime largest-keyframe-TX policy

Pinned libvpx v1.14.1 sets `tx_size_search_method = USE_LARGESTALL` for
realtime keyframes at speed 4 and above
(`third_party/libvpx/vp9/encoder/vp9_speed_features.c:558-583`). rvp9 instead
runs its full good-quality transform-size RD loop for each leaf. Matching the
canonical policy removed that loop and passed all 24 keyframe-focused tests.

The speed gain was large: a twenty-pair normal-GOP run improved wall by
`-13.412%` and total child CPU by `-7.629%`, winning 18/20 and 20/20 pairs.
The quality loss was decisive. The standard stream grew from 716,330 to
740,876 bytes while average PSNR fell from 31.935117 to 31.564898 dB
(`-0.370219 dB`). A larger stream with lower decoded quality cannot pass the
BD-rate gate; the changed keyframe reconstruction also propagates through the
following inter frames.

The policy change and its focused assertion are fully removed. rvp9's current
full TX search is compensating for a deeper keyframe transform, quantizer, or
mode-decision mismatch. Do not retry `USE_LARGESTALL` until that mismatch is
closed; compare the final-encode quantizer path with libvpx next.

## Unit 221 — retain exact NEON column projection

Pinned libvpx sums each 16-, 32-, or 64-pixel projection row with pairwise
NEON widening. Rvp9 still visited each byte through a scalar iterator for
every direct column-projection row. The AArch64 direct path now mirrors the
pinned kernel: pairwise-widen the first 16 bytes, accumulate each further
16-byte group into u16 lanes, then reduce once. Edge-clamped partial rows
retain the scalar helper because their visible span need not be a multiple of
16.

The focused differential test covers every product width, offsets 0 through
16 to exercise unaligned starts, random bytes, and all-zero/all-255 rows. All
four AArch64 integer-projection tests, all 12 motion-estimation tests,
formatting, diff checks, and core clippy with warnings denied pass. The
standard 120-frame stream remains byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

Two twenty-pair four-thread comparisons improved paired total child CPU by
`-1.357%` and `-0.801%`, with 19/20 and 17/20 wins. User CPU improved by
`-1.127%` and `-0.858%`, with 19/20 and 17/20 wins. Wall timing changed by
`-1.666%` and `+0.584%`; shared-host scheduling still makes it noisier than

## Unit 222 — retain narrow Hadamard fast quantization

The committed Unit 221 ten-iteration normal-GOP profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit221-normal-profile-v1.json.gz`, with symbols at
`/tmp/rvp9-unit221-normal-profile-v1.json.syms.json` and analysis at

concentrated at the inlined full Hadamard quantization-metrics call used by
Stage 4a coefficient-domain ranking. Integer projection no longer appears as
a leading leaf.

For Tx8x8 and Tx16x16, the Hadamard coefficients, round values, and fast
quantizer are all positive-i16 bounded after absolute value. The AArch64
metrics kernels now use saturating i16 absolute/add followed by
`vqdmulhq_s16` and a one-bit shift. For nonnegative operands,
`floor(floor(product / 2^15) / 2)` is exactly
`floor(product / 2^16)`, so this replaces paired widened i32 arithmetic
without changing the scalar quantization formula. Coefficient-error
accumulation remains widened and exact.

The existing differential gate covers Tx8x8/Tx16x16 across qindices
0/1/20/80/160/255, randomized inputs, all-zero, DC-only, final-scan-only,
and every-i16-min/max coefficient blocks. All nine AArch64 quantizer tests,
formatting, diff checks, and core clippy with warnings denied pass. The
standard 120-frame stream remains byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

Two twenty-pair four-thread comparisons improved paired total child CPU by
`-1.513%` and `-1.341%`, with 16/20 and 15/20 wins. User CPU improved by
`-1.557%` and `-1.575%`. Wall timing regressed under concurrent host load and
does not agree with the direct child-CPU evidence. Keep the exact reproducible
speed improvement.

The next experiment is the same bounded arithmetic for the distinct Tx32x32
Hadamard metrics kernel. Keep it separate so its contribution and exactness
remain independently measurable.

## Unit 227 — retain leaf-local keyframe TX-selection scratch

The committed Unit 226 ten-iteration all-keyframe profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit226-keyframe-profile-v1.json.gz`, with analysis at
`/tmp/rvp9-unit226-keyframe-profile-analysis.txt`. It contains 2,620 resolved
rvp9 self samples. `encode_keyframe_internal` still accounts for 35.53% of
self samples. Disassembly of its inlined body exposed the transform-size RD
loop and led back to `choose_intra_luma_tx_size`.

That function cloned the entire reconstruction plane once per coded leaf so
each TX-size candidate could overwrite only the leaf footprint. Intra
prediction for a leaf reads no arbitrary frame pixels: it needs the leaf plus
the one-pixel causal above/left halo. The picker now copies that bounded region
into a `(leaf_width + 1) x (leaf_height + 1)` scratch plane and runs the
unchanged candidate loop at local coordinate `(1, 1)`. A 32x32 leaf at 720p
therefore uses 1,089 scratch bytes instead of cloning 901,120 bytes.

The focused regression test constructs two 128x128 frames whose source leaf
and causal reconstruction halo are identical while every pixel outside that
region differs; both must choose the same transform size. It passes in release
mode. The existing simulator-to-decoder bit-exact test passes, formatting and
encoder clippy with warnings denied pass, and the standard stream remains
byte-exact at 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

Three twenty-pair standard-GOP comparisons improved paired total child CPU by
`-3.394%`, `-2.784%`, and `-2.423%`, all with 20/20 wins. Three ten-pair
all-keyframe comparisons measured total CPU at `0.7360x`, `0.7394x`, and
`0.7396x` Unit 226. Retain the exact architectural correction and count the
conservative repeated standard improvement of 2.42%.

Take a fresh matched comparison against pinned libvpx and re-profile both the
normal GOP and all-keyframe diagnostic. The prior matched ratios and Unit 226
profile are now stale after this large reduction.

## Unit 228 — reject partition-level chroma-sensitivity gating

The post-Unit-227 matched twenty-pair comparison measured rvp9 at `1.6097x`

The pinned F.0.2 trace at `/tmp/vpx-unit227-f02-t1.jsonl` contains 123,899
inter decisions. Libvpx evaluates an average 1.827 LAST candidates per decision
and makes roughly twice as many leaf decisions as rvp9, so candidate breadth is
not the remaining gap. It chooses model Tx8x8 on 122,641 decisions and Tx16x16
on 1,258; rvp9's corresponding 256x256 product trace chooses model Tx8x8 on
6,336 of 6,357 decisions. Transform-size policy is therefore aligned too.

Rvp9 currently evaluates both chroma planes for every candidate, whereas
libvpx gates them with `x->color_sensitivity`. A diagnostic implementation
threaded the existing partition-level SAD classification into the picker and
preserved the default stream when disabled. Enabled on the standard input, it
reduced output by 3,230 bytes but regressed paired total CPU by `+12.605%`
with 0/20 wins: rvp9 had to build two extra 32x32 chroma predictors per
superblock to obtain a classification libvpx gets from already-live prediction
state. A second upper-bound diagnostic disabled all chroma candidate modeling
without classification; it changed paired total CPU by `+0.564%` with 9/20
wins. Chroma candidate modeling is therefore not a material standalone cost at
this operating point, and recomputing libvpx's reused state is decisively
counterproductive. All diagnostic source changes were removed; the worktree
returned to the exact Unit 227 tree.

The next measured hypothesis is libvpx's large-block early-termination path.
Rvp9 detects `model_rd_for_sb_y_large` full skips and exposes `early_term`, but
still runs the complete Hadamard quantization and chroma model before returning.
Pinned libvpx bypasses `block_yrd` and later candidate work when Y, U, and V are
all transform-skippable. First measure a Y-only upper bound behind a diagnostic
override; if material, port the UV skip test while reusing its predictor and
variance work in the non-early path.

## Unit 235 — reject combined emitted residual/quant scratch borrow

The Unit 232 source-level profile attributes repeated samples to the emitted
residual scratch wrapper around `crates/rvp9-encoder/src/lib.rs:6820`. A
diagnostic implementation moved the residual array into the existing
transform/quant scratch and borrowed the combined per-worker storage once per
transform. The transform helper then operated on that already-borrowed
scratch. This removed one thread-local `RefCell` entry without changing the
transform, quantizer, inverse reconstruction, or coefficient payload.

Both scratch-contamination regressions passed. The standard 120-frame stream
remained exactly 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`,
and rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg produced byte-identical decoded

`c938181f215f71b246a8b10bf2ba9477c6f6e04b49c0c0ab6917aa692e79102e`.

The speed effect was not reproducible. An initially quiet set of twenty-pair
comparisons against Unit 233 reported paired total-CPU changes of `-0.345%`,
`-0.511%`, and `-0.746%`. Rebuilt identical source measured `-0.181%`,
`+0.107%`, and `+0.509%`; additional runs ranged from `-0.746%` to
`+2.475%` as shared-host load increased. The central result crosses zero and
is below the current noise floor. All source and test changes were removed,
and the worktree production code returned exactly to Unit 233.

Do not retry scratch-borrow fusion without a lower-noise microbenchmark that
isolates emitted transforms. The next experiment should target a larger

## Unit 236 — reuse replicated edge projection sums

The committed Unit 233 ten-iteration CPU profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit233-normal-profile-v2.json.gz`, with analysis at
`/tmp/rvp9-unit233-normal-profile-v2-analysis.txt`. It contains 7,622

projection chunk previously recomputed the same 64-pixel border-column sum
16 times. `int_pro_row_clamped` now divides the chunk into replicated-left,
visible-middle, and replicated-right spans, computes each replicated border
sum once, and fills that span. The visible columns retain the original
column-sum calculation. This preserves rvp9's on-demand equivalent of
libvpx's physically extended reference border.

A focused oracle covers fully outside, partially visible, and two-sided
windows; direct and vertically clamped rows; a narrow visible plane; and a
strided backing buffer. All 17 integer-projection tests pass. Warnings-denied
core all-target clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass.

The standard 120-frame stream remains exactly 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.
Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg produced byte-identical decoded YUV
with SHA-256
`c938181f215f71b246a8b10bf2ba9477c6f6e04b49c0c0ab6917aa692e79102e`.

The host was unsuitable for an end-to-end timing update: load average rose
from 50 to 98 while one `mddosem` process and many concurrent `rustc`
processes saturated the machine. One completed twenty-pair comparison was
neutral at `-0.018%` paired total child CPU. An isolated optimized-test
microbenchmark over two million representative fully replicated chunks was
stable under the same load. The old implementation retired
31.719-31.724 billion instructions and used 1.20-1.25 seconds of user CPU;
the retained implementation retired 2.546 billion instructions and used
0.09 seconds. This is a reproducible approximately 92% instruction reduction
inside the measured edge kernel. Do not use the saturated wall results as a
new rvp9/vpxenc ratio; repeat cumulative end-to-end timing when the host is
quiet.

The next bounded normal-GOP target is retained coefficient replay, now 5.42%
self and 5.76% inclusive. Avoid the rejected outer empty-block branch from
Unit 234; inspect the common replay loop for repeated loads, branches, or a
second coefficient traversal that can be removed exactly.

## Unit 237 — reject per-writer bit-accounting gate cache

Inspection beneath the retained replay loop found that every
`BoolWriter::write` checks the disabled E4 bit-accounting diagnostic through
a relaxed global atomic load. A diagnostic implementation snapshotted the
gate into each arithmetic writer at construction, which is semantically safe
for production: the environment gate is initialized before writers exist,
and dry-run writers are constructed inside their suppression scope. The
standard stream remained byte-exact.

Whole-encode hardware counters rejected the change. On the same warmed
120-frame product encode, Unit 236 retired 11,878,763,878 instructions; the
cached-gate candidate retired 11,908,176,985 (`+0.248%`). Both used 0.74
seconds of child user CPU. On AArch64 a relaxed atomic load is already a plain
load; moving the flag into the writer did not remove the per-bit branch and
instead enlarged writer state and generated code. All production changes
were removed. Do not retry a per-writer boolean cache; a useful diagnostic
optimization must hoist the decision around a complete syntax traversal or
compile the hook out, not merely relocate the same per-bit check.

The focused accounting run exposed a separate real test-harness race. Three
tests mutate the same global diagnostic gate and could interleave, causing
`suppression_skips_recording_and_restores_enabled_state` to fail. A test-only
mutex now serializes those three global-state cases. The complete accounting
suite passed twice in different execution orders, and core all-target clippy
with warnings denied, formatting, and diff checks pass.

Return to the retained replay loop itself. The next exact hypothesis is to
reuse its already-loaded first token and probability when entering the inner
zero/value loop, eliminating duplicate loads without changing arithmetic
writer state or adding another per-block branch.

## Unit 238 — reject loop-carried first retained token

A diagnostic replay implementation carried the outer loop's already-loaded

`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

Three warmed whole-encode hardware-counter pairs rejected the change. The

slightly favorable once and neutral once, but did not overcome the consistent
instruction regression. LLVM already retains the profitable values; explicit

All source changes were removed.

The normal inter packet previously ran the complete partition and mode writer

non-coefficient count even though those values are not needed until backward
adaptation after the tile bytes are written.

`CoefTokenPass` walk only the inferred leaf order and coefficient contexts.
It records probability-independent tokens and the 4-/12-token coefficient
histograms before the header. The already-required final tile writers now
accumulate non-coefficient mode/MV counts while replaying those tokens against
the post-header probabilities. Tile-local final counts are merged with
`FrameCounts::add_non_coef`, avoiding a second scan of their known-zero
coefficient banks.

A focused oracle proves that coefficient-only recording plus final replay
counts exactly equals the old complete count traversal, including non-skip
residual EOB counts. A separate merge test proves `add_non_coef` leaves both
coefficient banks unchanged. All 1,591 applicable release core tests pass;
the only failure is the pre-existing release invocation of
`sub_pixel_search_unsupported_block_size_panics_in_debug`, whose expected
debug assertion is compiled out. Core/encoder all-target release clippy
passes with warnings denied, as do formatting and diff checks. The focused
two-loop encoder test passes.

The standard stream remains exactly 716,330 bytes with SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.
Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg each produced 162,201,600 decoded
bytes with SHA-256
`c938181f215f71b246a8b10bf2ba9477c6f6e04b49c0c0ab6917aa692e79102e`.

Four warmed twenty-pair four-thread comparisons against Unit 242 changed
paired total child CPU by `-0.270%`, `-0.131%`, `+0.312%`, and `-0.532%`;
all four wall medians improved (`-0.738%`, `-0.504%`, `-0.180%`, and
`-0.752%`). Two one-thread comparisons improved total child CPU by `-0.481%`
with 16/20 wins and `-0.412%` with 18/20 wins. Retain the exact structural
reduction conservatively.

calculation. A focused test covers every one of the 36 band/context rows, and

`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`.

outputs all matched. All 1,592 applicable release core tests pass after
filtering the two absent captured-vector fixtures and the release form of the

to the zbin quantizer; its register pressure offsets the removed traversal.

another local block-error reshaping.

## Unit 252 — retain dead luma candidate reconstruction removal

`pick_intra_mode_luma` scores candidates exclusively with coefficient-domain
distortion and returns only the selected mode, rate, distortion, and RD cost.

array that never escaped the function and never contributed to the argmin.
The encoder reconstructs the selected mode later in its emit pass.

The retained exact change removes that dead candidate reconstruction while
leaving prediction, residual formation, forward transform, quantization,
coefficient-domain distortion, mode rate, candidate order, and tie-breaking
unchanged. The test-only reference picker deliberately retains the old
inverse-transform path. All 12 focused intra-picker and distortion tests pass
against that independent reference behavior. Encoder release library tests
pass with 526 passed and one ignored. Core all-target release clippy passes
with warnings denied; formatting and diff checks pass. The full core release
library run has its unchanged baseline result: 1,592 pass, the two absent
captured-vector fixtures fail, and the debug-only should-panic test does not
panic in release mode.

The standard 120-frame cpu-used 7 stream remains exactly 716,330 bytes with
SHA-256
`8144dcf9d104119634855cf2ed0554f14e206137ad33689f5b0f871b95c2acb3`, byte
for byte identical to Unit 249. Forced-keyframe wall time improves `-4.980%`
at one thread and `-4.552%` at four threads, with 5/5 wins in both sets.
The normal 120-frame workload improves paired total child CPU by `-0.665%`
at one thread with 15/20 wins. Its four-thread result is correctly diluted by
the single keyframe: total CPU changes `-0.059%` with 10/20 wins, while wall
time changes `-0.384%` with 13/20 wins. Keep the change because the targeted
path has a large reproducible win, the ordinary path does not regress, and
the output is exact.

After committing the green unit, re-profile forced-keyframe encoding. The
remaining keyframe mismatch is still structural: pinned libvpx restricts its
realtime keyframe mode and transform policy while rvp9 evaluates all ten
luma modes and transform sizes. Measure the reduced profile before changing
that quality-affecting policy.

## Unit 254 — retain canonical realtime keyframe mode policy

Pinned libvpx's speed-4+ realtime path sets every luma mode mask to DC/V/H,
sets every chroma mode mask to DC, and routes keyframes through
`vp9_pickmode.c::vp9_pick_intra_mode`, whose loop is exactly DC through H.
Rvp9 instead scored all ten luma modes and all ten chroma modes for every
eligible keyframe leaf. The Unit 252 profile showed the resulting inlined
keyframe body still held 39.79% of resolved self samples.

full picker's exact scoring kernel but stops after DC/V/H, and keeps the
existing all-ten-mode API for non-realtime use and its test oracle. The
realtime keyframe caller now fixes UV to DC and avoids constructing or
scoring UV candidates that pinned libvpx masks out. A focused differential
proves the wrapper returns the exact minimum of the full picker's DC/V/H
entries.

The standard stream changes from 716,330 to 711,909 bytes. Its average PSNR
changes from 31.935117 to 31.665444 dB. Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and
ffmpeg all decode identical output bytes with SHA-256
`4f94018d6dd9a0e02f422ab705a62ceddcfd584a3704a34d1aacf6096e0cbcf3`.
The single-point quality loss is acceptable only because the pinned product
curve remains well inside the final gate.

diagnostic of `-0.353661 dB`, and `8.368435 dB` overlap. Every target passes
rvp9-decoder and is byte-exact under pinned vpxdec and ffmpeg. The initial

passing run temporarily isolated that exact file and restored its SHA-256
`06a12c10e482ed1ee693663d6d647e9e8dc42ac32b3da21bd407d7efd3b3bdf5`.

Speed improves materially and reproducibly:

- forced-keyframe wall time improves `-34.380%` at one thread and
  `-34.889%` at four threads, with 5/5 wins in both sets;
- normal 120-frame paired total child CPU improves `-3.029%` at one thread

- the fresh matched normal ratio falls to `1.43418x` pinned libvpx total
  child CPU and `1.78801x` wall. The final `1.05x` speed gate remains open.

a regression: `-0.312%` paired wall but `+0.521%` CPU, with only 6/20 CPU
wins. Splitting every larger metric into 8x8 tiles adds enough quantizer and
accumulator calls to erase the cheaper transform. The source change is fully
removed.

Keep model-selected metric sizes. The transform hierarchy is not the current
gap. The next exact implementation unit should amortize per-candidate control
cost instead: borrow the thread-local prediction/residual scratch once per
complete mode pick and pass it through the serial candidate loop, rather than
performing a TLS lookup and runtime `RefCell` borrow for each candidate.

## Unit 268 — retain one candidate-scratch borrow per mode pick

The unified inter picker evaluates candidates serially but previously entered
the thread-local prediction/residual `RefCell` for every candidate. The
retained implementation borrows that scratch once at the public
`pick_inter_mode` boundary and passes it through the complete candidate loop.
The standalone luma/test helpers keep a thin TLS wrapper. Candidate order,
filter search, prediction bytes, metric arithmetic, and winner comparison are
unchanged.

The standard stream remains exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
One-thread timing is neutral (`+0.035%` wall, `+0.106%` paired total child
CPU). Two independent twenty-pair four-thread runs reproduce the production
gain:

- first: wall `-0.531%`, CPU `-0.562%`, 12/20 wins for each;
- repeat: wall `-0.679%`, CPU `-0.632%`, 13/20 wins for each.

Fresh matched timing reports rvp9/vpxenc at `1.33894x` paired total child CPU
and `1.56045x` wall. This remains far outside the final `1.05x` gate.

All seven focused public-picker tests pass. Core all-target clippy passes with
warnings denied. The complete release core library reports 1,596 passes and
only its three known environment/build-mode failures: two absent captured
vectors and one debug-only expected panic. The release encoder library passes
528 tests with one ignored. Formatting, diff checks, and the exact stream
gate pass.

Retain the exact scratch-lifetime change. Re-profile the committed binary;
the next experiment must target a larger measured body inside candidate
metrics or emission rather than another sub-percent wrapper operation.

## Unit 269 — reverse the non-reproducible mode-pick scratch borrow

An independent continuation rebuilt Unit 268 and confirmed its candidate
executable was byte-identical to the original candidate with SHA-256
`3ca1fef484202416e059cf8350f458cd58a0ee849d878a32f6a6b13b36130214`.
It compared that exact binary against the same Unit 260 baseline. One-thread
timing remained noise: paired total child CPU reported `-0.568%` with only
11/20 wins while the independent medians moved in the opposite direction.

Two further twenty-pair four-thread runs both reversed Unit 268's claimed
gain: paired total child CPU regressed `+1.192%` and `+1.004%`, with only
5/20 wins in each series. Across the four independent parallel series, the
candidate therefore has two small favorable results and two larger adverse
results. The sign does not reproduce, so the change fails the production
Pareto rule.

The scratch-lifetime source change is fully removed. The standard stream is
again exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
All 62 inter-mode tests pass after removal. Keep the per-candidate scratch
borrow; its control cost is below the stable measurement floor. The next
experiment must target a larger measured body inside candidate metrics or
emission.

## Unit 270 — reject a flat emitted-coefficient arena

The committed Unit 268 profile attributed 69 source-line samples to widening
native `i16` quantizer coefficients into one heap-allocated `Vec<i32>` per
nonzero emitted transform. The candidate replaced the per-transform vectors in
`VecBackedInterCoefSource` with one flat `Vec<i32>` arena and inserted the
quantizer's `i16` slice directly into that arena. Block lookup retained stable
offset, length, and EOB metadata, so the writer-facing coefficient type and
values were unchanged.

A focused regression covered signed i16 extremes, two blocks sharing the arena,
and exact writer-facing i32 values. The existing direct-slot, replacement,
merge, and zero-marker tests also passed. To isolate this unit from a concurrent
uncommitted core experiment, both measured binaries were built from commit
`db05146`; only `crates/rvp9-encoder/src/lib.rs` was copied into the candidate
snapshot. Baseline and candidate produced the same 740,177-byte standard stream
with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The allocation removal did not produce a measurable speed gain. Twenty warmed
alternating pairs reported:

- one thread: wall `-0.023%` with 11/20 wins, but paired total child CPU
  `+0.232%` with only 6/20 wins;
- four threads: wall `+0.010%` and total child CPU `-0.003%`, both with exactly
  10/20 wins.

The result is at the measurement floor and fails the reproducible Pareto rule.
The source and focused test are fully removed. Keep the existing per-transform
vectors; allocation is not a material part of the current speed gap. The next
experiment should target the measured coefficient writer/entropy body or a
larger emission/picker algorithmic difference, not coefficient storage shape.

## Unit 271 — reject reusing large-block chroma skip predictions

The large-block AcDc skip probe builds complete U and V inter predictions before
testing their energy thresholds. When either plane rejects the YUV early exit,
the normal UV model path rebuilt both predictions. The candidate wrote the probe
results into the existing per-candidate U/V scratch and reused those exact pixels
in the fallback model path. It preserved the skip predicate, candidate order, and
all model arithmetic. The focused large-block chroma-skip test passed.

The candidate overlapped the temporary flat-arena experiment, but the measured
binaries isolated the core delta: both contained the same encoder source, while
only `/tmp/rvp9-unit269-candidate` contained the chroma reuse change. Both emitted
the exact 740,177-byte standard stream with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

Twenty warmed alternating pairs showed no reproducible CPU reduction:

- one thread: wall `-0.067%`, total child CPU `+0.035%`, and 10/20 CPU wins;
- four threads, first run: wall `-0.422%`, total child CPU `-0.358%`, and
  14/20 CPU wins;
- four threads, immediate repeat: wall `-0.242%`, total child CPU `+0.226%`,
  and only 8/20 CPU wins.

The repeated production-width CPU result changed sign, so the avoided chroma
interpolation passes are below the stable measurement floor on the standard
field. The core source change is fully removed. Keep the simpler independent
probe and UV prediction paths; the next unit must remove work from a larger
measured candidate or coefficient-entropy body.

## Unit 272 — reject batched ONE-token arithmetic coding

A fresh committed-baseline profile at
`/tmp/rvp9-unit270-baseline-profile.json.gz` contains 4,388 resolved rvp9 self
samples. Retained coefficient replay accounts for 6.43% and count-tokenization
for 5.13%. Instruction attribution shows that both costs are the inlined
arithmetic writer, not coefficient scratch lookup. Earlier workload counters
showed that signed ONE tokens comprise 84.54% of replayed nonzero coefficients.

The candidate batched the no-zero-run ONE token's four consecutive decisions
(not-EOB, not-zero, ONE, and sign) through one `BoolWriter` call. It loaded and
stored range, count, and low-value state once for the four decisions while
retaining exact per-symbol bit accounting. A 128-state differential exercised
varied probabilities, arbitrary prefix/suffix coder state, byte emission, and
carry propagation. All 16 arithmetic-writer tests, the retained-token
post-probability-update differential, and a focused accounting test passed.
The standard stream remained exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The source-level batch did not improve total CPU and grew the release binary by
704 bytes. Twenty warmed alternating pairs reported:

- one thread: wall `+0.186%`, total child CPU `+0.111%`, and only 7/20 wins;
- four threads: wall `-0.510%` and total child CPU `-0.192%`, but user CPU
  regressed `+0.098%`; the apparent result came from noisy system time.

The contradictory one-thread result and larger code fail the reproducible
Pareto rule. The source and focused tests are fully removed. LLVM's existing
inlining is already competitive with an explicit four-symbol loop; do not retry
small arithmetic-writer batches without an instruction-level design that also
reduces generated code. The next unit should target an algorithmic difference
in coefficient count-tokenization or a larger picker/emission body.

## Unit 273 — retain AArch64 NEON integer-pel prediction copies

The fresh committed-baseline profile at
`/tmp/rvp9-unit270-baseline-profile.json.gz` contains 4,388 resolved rvp9 self
samples plus 613 samples in platform `memmove`. Caller attribution assigns 147
of those copies to `inter::filter::convolve_copy`, making integer-pel prediction
copying a larger exact leaf than the symbol-only ranking showed. AArch64 still
called `memmove` once per active row, while the existing x86-64 path and pinned
libvpx use fixed-width SIMD loads and stores.

The retained AArch64 dispatch copies widths 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64 with scalar,
64-bit NEON, or one to four 128-bit NEON load/store pairs per row. Unsupported
widths retain the scalar fallback. Source/destination strides, active pixels,
candidate order, and every codec decision are unchanged. A differential covers
all 13 VP9 block shapes, 17 independent source/destination stride combinations,
and noisy destination sentinels. A separate forced-capability oracle proves the
NEON and scalar dispatch arms.

The standard stream remains exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
Twenty warmed alternating pairs report:

- one thread: wall `-2.531%` and total child CPU `-2.304%`, winning all 20
  pairs on both measures;
- four threads: wall `-6.185%` and total CPU `-1.241%`, with 20/20 wall and
  18/20 CPU wins;
- four-thread repeat: wall `-4.790%` and total CPU `-0.616%`, with 18/20 wall
  and 15/20 CPU wins.

A fresh matched four-thread comparison reports rvp9/vpxenc at `1.33392x`
paired total child CPU and `1.50794x` wall. Host-level variation makes the
direct old/new pairs the unit-effect evidence; the final `1.05x` gate remains
materially open. Both focused release tests and core all-target release clippy
with warnings denied pass. Retain the exact SIMD copy path and re-profile the
committed binary before choosing the next kernel.

## Measurement correction for Units 270 and 272

The first isolated baseline target for Units 270 and 272 was briefly populated
from the live worktree before its manifest-path rebuild. Because the live files
had newer timestamps, Cargo could reuse artifacts from that accidental build.
The candidate targets were independent, but the old baseline executable is not
acceptable evidence. A pristine baseline was rebuilt from commit `a833f4e` in
the never-used `/tmp/rvp9-unit273-baseline-target` directory and both preserved
candidate executables were remeasured against it.

The corrected twenty-pair results strengthen the original rejection decisions:

- Unit 270 flat coefficient arena: one-thread wall `+0.262%`, total CPU
  `+0.190%` with 8/20 wins; four-thread wall `+0.538%`, total CPU `+0.612%`
  with 6/20 wins.
- Unit 272 batched ONE-token coding: one-thread wall `+0.237%`, total CPU
  `+0.199%` with 6/20 wins; four-thread wall `+0.087%`, total CPU `-0.133%`
  with 11/20 wins.

The candidates remain fully removed. Use a never-used target directory for
every future isolated baseline and candidate build; do not share an artifact
directory across snapshots even when their package names and versions match.

## Unit 274 — reject a separate parallel coefficient-record phase

The pre-header retained-coefficient record pass is tile-independent but ran
serially. The candidate submitted each of four tiles to the persistent frame
worker pool, kept tile-local coefficient contexts and count banks, then merged
results in tile order before probability planning. The one-thread and
bit-accounting paths retained the existing serial traversal.

Both four-tile thread-count oracles passed across one, two, and four workers,
including exact-VBP history. The 120-frame product stream remained exactly
740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
Pristine isolated baseline and candidate builds used separate never-before-used
source and target directories based on commit `a833f4e`.

Parallel recording produced a real latency win but bought it with too much
extra work. Twenty warmed alternating pairs reported:

- one thread: wall `+0.201%`, total child CPU `+0.159%`, and only 5/20 CPU
  wins;
- four threads: wall `-3.898%`, total CPU `+1.528%`, and only 2/20 CPU wins;
- four-thread repeat: wall `-4.056%`, total CPU `+1.551%`, again only 2/20 CPU
  wins.

The extra pool phase, tile-local full count banks, and merge reduce critical
path time but violate the CPU-backed Pareto rule. The source change is fully
removed. Do not add a standalone record scope. A future parallel version must
fuse recording into an already-running tile job or otherwise eliminate the
extra scheduling and per-tile count overhead.

## Unit 275 — reject swapping the reconstruction into the reference pool

The inter-frame path copied each completed tight reconstruction into the
reference pool before rotating named references. The candidate instead swapped
the reconstruction's owned plane buffers into the selected pool slot and moved
the displaced buffers back into the encoder's reusable reconstruction scratch.
It removed the full-frame commit copy without changing reference selection,
rotation, or pixels. The focused buffer-pool test and exact standard stream
passed.

The ownership swap reduced process CPU but consistently lengthened the
four-thread critical path. Twenty warmed alternating pairs reported:

- one thread: wall `-0.521%` and total child CPU `-0.603%`;
- four threads, first run: total CPU `-1.996%`, but wall `+3.077%` with 0/20
  wall wins;
- four threads, immediate repeat: total CPU `-2.369%`, but wall `+2.562%`,
  again with 0/20 wall wins.

The regression is deterministic enough to reject despite the CPU reduction.
Changing which allocation becomes the next active reference likely changes
memory locality on the latency-critical path. The source change is fully
removed. Keep the explicit reconstruction commit until a design can preserve
the pool allocation's locality as well as its pixels.

## Unit 276 — reject coefficient recording fused into tile encode jobs

Unit 274 showed that a separate parallel record phase saves wall time but adds
CPU. This candidate instead recorded coefficient tokens and count histograms
immediately after transform and quantization inside the already-running tile
picker jobs. The pre-header pass then merged those tile-local counts and the
final syntax traversal replayed the retained tokens. This removed the separate
coefficient-only partition-tree traversal without adding another worker-pool
scope.

The focused record/replay differential passed, as did all 528 active release
encoder library tests. The standard stream remained exactly 740,177 bytes with
SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The fused path was still at the measurement floor. Twenty warmed alternating
pairs reported:

- one thread: wall `+0.136%`, total child CPU `+0.451%`, and only 8/20 CPU
  wins;
- four threads: wall `-0.099%`, total CPU `-0.288%`, with only 10/20 wall and
  11/20 CPU wins.

The host was busy during this screening, but the result is too small and
inconsistent to justify a 331-line cross-crate mechanism. Per-leaf tokenization,
tile lookup, context maintenance, and count storage replace almost all the
eliminated traversal cost. The source and focused test are fully removed. Do
not retry moving the same coefficient tokenization into the picker; target the
tokenization algorithm itself or a larger measured picker kernel.

## Unit 277 — reject direct full-frame Y4M plane reads

The CLI's full-frame Y4M path read each frame into one temporary body buffer,
then copied every row into the final Y, U, and V vectors. The candidate read
uncropped planes directly into those final vectors. Cropped input kept the
existing body-buffer path. All 16 focused Y4M unit tests and 11 `read_cropped`
error-path tests passed. The standard encoded stream remained exactly 740,177
bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

Removing the body allocation as well as the copy reduced CPU but changed frame
allocation layout and regressed four-thread wall time twice: `+2.222%` with
2/20 wins, then `+3.226%` with 0/20 wins. A second candidate retained the
body allocation and removed only the plane copy. It still reduced measured
process CPU:

- one thread: total CPU `-0.860%` with 14/20 wins and wall `-0.792%`;
- four threads, repeat: total CPU `-2.415%` with 17/20 wins, but wall
  `+1.867%` with only 3/20 wins.

One intervening four-thread run was distorted by severe host contention and is
not evidence. The two ordinary production-width runs agree that bypassing the
copy lengthens the critical path despite doing less process work. The copied
planes are likely warmer or first-touched more favourably when encoding starts.
The source change is fully removed. Keep the full-frame copy unless input and
encoding are redesigned as a streaming pipeline with an explicit locality
oracle.

## Unit 278 — reject gating unavailable-ALTREF MV candidates

The final causal leaf pass built LAST, GOLDEN, and ALTREF motion-vector
candidate pairs unconditionally. The standard configuration has ALTREF
disabled, so the candidate skipped the ALTREF `find_mv_refs` walk and supplied
the existing zero placeholders to the unavailable reference bundle. Live
ALTREF encoding retained the original walk. Focused ALTREF tests passed, and
the standard stream remained exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The exact work removal reduced process CPU but lengthened the four-thread
critical path in two consecutive twenty-pair runs:

- first: total CPU `-1.480%` with 17/20 wins, but wall `+4.285%` with only
  4/20 wins;
- repeat: total CPU `-2.392%` with 16/20 wins, but wall `+3.565%` with only
  1/20 wins.

One-thread timing was mildly favourable at `-0.267%` CPU and `-0.391%` wall.
The production-width wall regression fails the Pareto gate. Removing the
uniform per-leaf walk changes tile completion balance or hot-code layout enough
to delay the critical worker despite lower aggregate CPU. The source change is
fully removed. Do not gate this walk in isolation; revisit only as part of a
larger final-pass removal that proves both worker balance and total CPU.

## Unit 279 — reject skipping causal MV walks for cached ZERO/NEWMV picks

When the final leaf reuses the partition descent's complete picker result, a
ZEROMV or NEWMV winner does not consume causal NEAREST/NEAR vectors. The
candidate skipped all three LAST/GOLDEN/ALTREF `find_mv_refs` walks for those
cached modes when RDO and diagnostic paths were inactive. Cached NEAREST/NEAR
winners retained the walks for decoder-faithful MV repair. The standard stream
remained exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The wider removal repeated Unit 278's worker-imbalance result. Twenty warmed
alternating pairs reported:

- one thread: wall `-0.735%`, total CPU `-0.438%`, both with 11/20 wins;
- four threads: total CPU `-1.656%` with 15/20 wins, but wall `+4.462%` with
  only 1/20 wins.

The work is concentrated on noncritical tiles or changes their completion
order without shortening the slowest tile. The production latency regression
again fails the Pareto gate, so the source change is fully removed. Further
tile-local work removal needs per-tile critical-path evidence; aggregate CPU
headroom alone is insufficient.

## Unit 280 — reject transposed scalar 32x32 inverse-DCT storage

The scalar 32x32 inverse transform wrote each row result contiguously, then
gathered each column with a 128-byte stride. The candidate stored row results
transposed so every column transform consumed one contiguous 32-value slice.
The 1024-, 135-, and 34-coefficient paths shared the same storage change; all
arithmetic and eob gates were unchanged. Ten focused inverse-transform tests
passed, and the standard stream remained exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

Matched timing found no gain. Twenty warmed alternating pairs reported one
thread at wall `-0.150%` and total CPU `-0.206%`, both with 11/20 wins. Four
threads regressed wall `+0.225%` and total CPU `+0.253%`, with 8/20 and 9/20
wins. The 4 KiB intermediate already fits in L1, so moving the strided access
from the column gather to the row scatter does not reduce total work. The
source change is fully removed.

## Measurement correction for Units 276–280

The preserved `/tmp/rvp9-unit273-copy-neon-candidate` executable was not a
valid timing baseline for later live-target builds. A later clean rebuild of
the same exact Unit 273 source, `/tmp/rvp9-unit275-baseline`, emitted the same
stream but measured `-1.788%` total CPU and `+2.675%` wall against the older
artifact. That artifact-level offset explains the repeated false signature of
lower candidate CPU paired with roughly four-percent worse wall time.

All preserved candidates were remeasured against the later clean rebuild:

- Unit 276 fused coefficient recording remains rejected. One thread regressed
  wall `+0.304%` and total CPU `+0.638%`; its four-thread result was internally
  inconsistent under host load and cannot rescue the one-thread regression.
- Unit 278 unavailable-ALTREF gating is only at the measurement floor: wall
  `-0.144%`, total CPU `-0.194%`, with 12/20 and 11/20 wins. Its source remains
  removed.
- Unit 279 cached ZERO/NEWMV gating still fails latency: wall `+1.700%` and
  total CPU `-0.402%`, both near the floor with 9/20 and 11/20 wins. Its source
  remains removed.
- Unit 277 direct full-frame Y4M reads reverse from reject to retain. Corrected
  one-thread timing improves wall `-1.433%` with 18/20 wins and total CPU
  `-1.349%` with 16/20 wins. Two corrected four-thread runs improve wall by
  `-1.422%` and `-1.598%`, with 14/20 and 16/20 wins, while total CPU improves
  `-0.530%` and `-0.595%`, with 12/20 and 15/20 wins.

Unit 277's direct plane reads are therefore restored. The full-frame path
retains the temporary body allocation because the no-allocation variant's
different heap layout was independently latency-negative. Cropped input keeps
the original read-and-copy path. Future isolated comparisons must use a clean
baseline rebuilt through the same target and source route as the candidate;
do not compare later builds with `/tmp/rvp9-unit273-copy-neon-candidate`.

## Unit 281 — refresh the pinned-libvpx speed ratio

The committed direct-plane-read encoder was measured against pinned libvpx
with twenty alternating four-thread pairs on the standard 1280x704, 120-frame,
cpu-used 7 realtime VBR workload. Median paired ratios are `1.30769x` total
child CPU and `1.50498x` wall time. The prior accepted comparison was
`1.33392x` CPU and `1.50794x` wall. The total-CPU gate therefore improved, but
the required `1.05x` production-parity limit remains materially open.

## Unit 282 — reject skip-only Hadamard quantization metrics

The Stage 4a candidate model only tests whether a Hadamard tile has any
quantized coefficient, but the fused AArch64 quantizer still loaded inverse
scan positions and reduced the exact EOB. A compile-time alternate path omitted
that scan work while preserving the existing full-EOB API. A differential over
8x8, 16x16, and 32x32 transforms, six qindices, zero, extreme, random, DC-only,
and final-scan-only inputs matched skippability, SATD, and coefficient error.
The standard stream remained exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

Single-thread timing suggested a real CPU reduction: two twenty-pair runs
reported total-child-CPU changes of `-1.053%` and `-1.809%`. Production-width
latency did not reproduce. Four runs reported wall changes of `-0.513%`,
`+0.497%`, `-1.257%`, and `+0.292%`; total CPU changed `-0.525%`, `+0.196%`,
`-1.104%`, and `-0.764%`. Two wall wins and two regressions under the same
paired protocol fail the reproducible Pareto rule, and the compile-time seam
added 132 lines across three files. The source and focused test are fully
removed. Do not add a separate skip-only quantizer API without a larger caller
that also eliminates other metrics work.

## Unit 283 — reject forcing 32x32 partitions at 64x64 roots

The large-frame profile appeared to make 64x64 picker calls much more
expensive than 32x32 calls, so a diagnostic capped every eligible variance
root at 32x32 and skipped its 64x64 NONE evaluation. The 120-frame stream
changed from 740,177 to 736,365 bytes, but twenty four-thread pairs regressed
total child CPU by `+6.463%` with only 2/20 wins. Wall also regressed by
`+7.264%`. The four replacement 32x32 leaves and their emit work cost more
than the skipped large-block pick.

A narrower form capped only mixed variance hints and emitted the exact
committed stream. It still regressed paired CPU by `+0.758%` and wall by
`+1.601%`, with 7/20 wins in both. A full 120-frame diagnostic explains the
result: all `14,481` superblocks whose hint admitted a 64x64 root ultimately
committed one 64x64 leaf; none split. The measured 32x32 picker calls belong to
different superblocks, not losing children below those roots. There is no
redundant 64x64 evaluation to prune on this field. Both controls and the
temporary per-superblock logger are fully removed.

## Unit 284 — reject AArch64 NEON 8-tap loop filters

The corrected native profile attributed part of the remaining loop-filter
worker closure to scalar 8-tap filtering. A candidate ported pinned libvpx's
eight-lane NEON arithmetic for horizontal and vertical single and dual slots,
including the exact 8x8 transpose. Random, flat, step, single, and dual
differentials matched the scalar reference. The standard stream remained
exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

Short twenty-pair runs were unstable, ranging from a one-thread `-1.745%`
CPU result to neutral follow-ups. A longer screen repeated each encode four
times inside twelve alternating paired samples. One thread then regressed
wall by `+3.854%` and total child CPU by `+1.761%`, with only 4/12 and 3/12
wins. Four threads improved wall by `-1.350%` and CPU by `-0.892%`, with
10/12 and 9/12 wins. The opposite one- and four-thread directions fail the
production Pareto rule. The complete SIMD implementation, tests, exports,
and dispatch wiring are removed.

## Unit 285 — reject unchecked retained-token replay indexing

The retained-token replay symbol contained 493 AArch64 instructions and
several cold bounds-failure edges inside its nested token loop. A candidate
used the loop's existing length guards and the private token constructor's
probability-context invariant to replace repeated slice indexing with
`get_unchecked`. All 51 focused entropy tests passed. Generated replay code
fell to 467 instructions, and the standard stream remained exactly 740,177
bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The instruction reduction did not reduce process work. In the longer screen,
which repeated each encode four times inside twelve alternating pairs, one
thread regressed wall by `+1.053%` and total child CPU by `+0.567%`. Four
threads improved wall by `-4.704%`, but total CPU regressed by `+1.128%` with
only 2/12 wins. The source change is fully removed. Keep safe indexing; the
compiler's proven bounds checks are cheaper than the unchecked form's changed
code shape on this workload.

## Unit 286 — retain aborting production panic strategy

The release profile unwound panics even though an encoder panic is fatal to
the production CLI. An isolated `-C panic=abort` build removed most unwind
machinery without changing normal control flow or codec decisions. The binary
fell from 1,551,000 to 1,444,296 bytes. Its standard stream remained exactly
740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

## Unit 285 — retain coefficient recording fused into parallel tile jobs

Unit 276 moved coefficient recording into every picker invocation and was
correctly rejected at the measurement floor. This successor narrows the
mechanism to the existing multi-tile worker jobs only. The serial and
one-thread paths keep the established pre-header traversal. Each worker owns
one optional tile recorder, one count-only bool writer for the whole job, and
one tile-local coefficient context whose left state resets at every
superblock row. The pre-header stage merges only coefficient banks, while the
final syntax pass replays the retained tokens. There is no added pool scope or
per-leaf tile lookup.

Baseline and candidate were built sequentially through the same source path,
`/tmp/rvp9-unit281-source`, from shipped-code baseline `43dd746`, using the
never-reused targets `/tmp/rvp9-unit281b-baseline-target` and
`/tmp/rvp9-unit282-candidate-target`. Both emit exactly 740,177 bytes with
SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
rvp9-decoder, pinned libvpx `vpxdec`, and ffmpeg decode that exact stream to
the same 162,201,600-byte I420 SHA-256
`167be349e40c3691fea4802a97ea9a04da5a2316341c67cb201d0254872b09f9`.
The direct record/replay oracle, both four-tile thread-count invariants,
formatting, diff checks, and core-plus-encoder all-target clippy with warnings
denied pass.

The stronger stable protocol used twelve alternating pairs and aggregated
four encodes per sample. One thread is unchanged: wall `-0.050%`, total child
CPU `-0.044%`. Four threads improve wall by `-4.872%` with 8/12 wins, while
total child CPU rises `+1.062%`. Two ordinary twenty-pair four-thread runs
agree on latency at `-5.473%` and `-4.199%`; their CPU changes were `+1.192%`
and `+1.506%`. Host load made absolute vpxenc wall ratios unusable in this
unit, so none is promoted as final-gate evidence.

Retain this as a measured critical-path prerequisite: it moves unavoidable
coefficient recording off the serial path, preserves bytes and quality, and
produces a reproducible production-width latency win. It is not a total-work
win. The next experiment must profile the `+6.624%` system-time signal and

`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

improve wall by `-1.799%`, system CPU by `-21.804%`, and total child CPU by

`-12.567%`, and total child CPU by `-1.941%`.

memory falls from 1,707,229,184 to 70,877,184 bytes, wall from 3.48 to 3.33

the same long input's total-CPU ratio improves from `1.36103x` to `1.33600x`;

motion-search reference differ from the decoder-equivalent LAST slot. The
production gate runs with `noise_sensitivity = 0`, so both buffers carried the
same pixels and the encoder copied a full YUV frame after every commit.

The retained path allocates and updates `me_ref_*` only when the denoiser is
active. Otherwise the variance picker, show-frame mode picker, and ALTREF
picker read the LAST pool slot directly. The denoiser branch is unchanged and
keeps its separate writable luma/chroma storage. A focused pointer oracle now
proves that denoiser-off ME reads alias LAST, while the complementary denoiser
test proves filtered luma still diverges without touching decoder
reconstruction.

Baseline and candidate were rebuilt from the same committed source through
never-used targets `/tmp/rvp9-unit291-clean-baseline-target` and
`/tmp/rvp9-unit291-clean-candidate-target`. In twelve alternating pairs with
four encodes per sample:

- one thread improves wall by `-1.625%` and total child CPU by `-1.119%`;
- four threads improves wall by `-0.152%` and total child CPU by `-1.252%`.

Both CPU results win a majority of pairs. Earlier repeats against the same
accepted baseline directionally agreed and showed larger gains; only the
clean-target results are acceptance evidence. The standard stream remains
exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
All 528 active release encoder library tests pass, with one ignored, and

## Unit 293 — retain fixed coefficient-tree cost expansion

The post-Unit 292 profile `/tmp/rvp9-unit293-current.json.gz` attributed 170
