encoder rebuilt 528 live coefficient contexts once per frame, walking VP9's
fixed eleven-node coefficient tree twice per context for the with-EOB and
skip-EOB slabs. The retained implementation spells out those fixed paths,
loads each node's zero and one costs once, and derives both slabs together.

An exhaustive oracle compares the formula with both generic tree walkers for
all 255 valid probabilities at each of eleven nodes: 2,805 cases. All five
coefficient-cost tests and core all-target clippy with warnings denied pass.

`cost_walk` from the sampled top 50.

distinct targets. The first twelve-pair, four-encodes-per-sample screen
reported wall `-1.115%`, total child CPU `-0.944%`, and 9/12 wins for both.
The unchanged repeat reported wall `-0.435%`, total CPU `-0.659%`, eight wall
wins, and nine CPU wins. The one-thread control reported wall `-0.359%` and
total CPU `-0.352%`, each with 8/12 wins.

The standard stream remains exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg each produced the same 162,201,600-byte
I420 output with SHA-256
`167be349e40c3691fea4802a97ea9a04da5a2316341c67cb201d0254872b09f9`.

## Unit 294 — retain reference-pool allocation exchange

The Unit 291 profile attributed 26 `memmove` samples to copying every
show-frame reconstruction into `RefFramePool::commit_new_frame`. Unit 292's
owned commit removed that copy but regressed because replacing the slot also
dropped its reusable allocations. The retained path instead exchanges the
three owned reconstruction planes with the fresh unreferenced pool slot and
keeps the displaced slot planes as next-frame scratch. No pixels are copied,
allocated, or deallocated after the reuse cycle starts. If an encode fails
after taking the scratch, the next attempt allocates one replacement and
restores the cycle.

A pointer-identity oracle proves that both the committed planes and displaced
slot allocations survive the exchange unchanged. The forced inter-frame error
test also proves that the same encoder can encode again afterward. The full
release encoder library passes 529 tests with one ignored, and encoder
all-target clippy passes with warnings denied.

A concurrent commit advanced the branch during the first measurement, so
those results were discarded. The final baseline was rebuilt from committed
HEAD `ff85944` through an isolated source archive, and the candidate was rebuilt
from that exact tree plus only the exchange. In twelve alternating pairs with
four encodes per sample, four threads improved wall by `-3.889%`, user CPU by
`-1.205%`, system CPU by `-4.682%`, and total child CPU by `-1.495%`, with
8/12 CPU wins. The one-thread control improved wall by `-0.860%`, user CPU by
`-0.523%`, system CPU by `-9.229%`, and total child CPU by `-0.941%`, with
9/12 CPU wins.

The standard stream remains exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
Retain the exchange: it removes measured frame-sized copy and allocator work
without changing the bitstream or the reference-map lifecycle.

## Unit 295 — reject picker-sized emitted transforms

The paired current profiles are `/tmp/rvp9-unit295-current.json.gz` and
`/tmp/vpx-unit295-current.json.gz`, with resolved analyses beside them. Rvp9's
largest transform leaves are the emitted 32x32 forward and inverse DCTs, while
pinned libvpx spends most transform/model work in 8x8 Hadamard, quantization,
and forward-DCT kernels. The journal left joint control of
`RVP9_RT_EMIT_MAX_TX` and `RVP9_RT_EMIT_TX_RD` open as a quality-bearing policy
experiment, because disabling emit-side RD alone is inert under maximum-TX.

A configuration-only screen disabled both gates, so the emitter reused the
picker's usually smaller transform without running a second transform search.
The stream changed from 740,177 to 738,640 bytes. It was decisively slower:
twelve alternating four-thread pairs with four encodes per sample regressed
wall by `+11.807%` and total child CPU by `+20.165%`, with only 1/12 wall wins
and 0/12 CPU wins. The extra transform blocks overwhelm each smaller kernel's
lower individual cost, so no quality run or source change is justified.

Keep maximum emitted transforms on the large-frame recovery path. The profile
difference does not identify avoidable transform search; it reflects different
final coding work. A useful successor must reduce the cost of the retained
large-transform path without multiplying transform-block count.

## Unit 296 — reject the low-precision realtime 32x32 DCT

Pinned libvpx sets `use_lp32x32fdct` at speed 4 and above, so cpu-used 7 uses
`vpx_fdct32x32_rd`; rvp9 deliberately uses its heavily optimized full-precision
32x32 transform. A candidate added the missing scalar RD schedule and an
AArch64 NEON path with an overflow-safe widened continuation. The randomized
stride and valid-residual differential matched the scalar oracle, including a
constant extreme checked directly against pinned `libvpx.a`.

Wiring the RD transform only into realtime inter emission changed the standard
stream from 740,177 to 740,628 bytes. Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg
each produced the same 162,201,600-byte I420 output with SHA-256
`099f232029e8ae2ee6dd1c4a840b886a3ae96e1c4034b4a89db2f3e38d285baf`.
The path was therefore valid, but it was not a production-width speed win.

The one-thread control improved total child CPU by `-0.516%` with 8/12 wins.
Two four-thread screens reversed that result: total CPU changed `+0.937%`
(4/12 wins) and `+0.229%` (6/12), while wall changed `+1.090%` and `+0.419%`.
This fails the Pareto rule and the absolute-latency objective. The complete
transform, export, test, and encoder wiring are removed.

Keep rvp9's full-precision 32x32 kernel. Source parity alone is not useful when
the existing divergent kernel is already faster at production width. A future
32x32 change needs a direct kernel improvement without adding a second large
transform body or changing the emitted coefficient schedule.

## Unit 297 — reject lazy realtime coefficient-cost construction

The realtime cpu-used 7 path builds a roughly 28 KiB coefficient RD-cost table
from 528 probability contexts once per frame, although its large-frame policy
disables the three consumers: good-mode RDO, trellis, and emit-side transform
redecision. Three exact candidates deferred that build while preserving every
consumer's original table and values.

The first candidate bundled coefficient, skip, and transform-size costs behind
their combined enable predicate. Two four-thread screens changed total child
CPU by `-0.422%` and `-0.083%`, but the one-thread control regressed `+0.535%`.
A narrower candidate deferred only the coefficient table. Four-thread CPU
improved `-0.494%`, while one-thread CPU again regressed `+0.279%`. A local
`OnceCell` at the original build site removed the frame-setup predicate and
initialized the table only from an actual consumer; its four-thread screen
regressed total CPU by `+0.317%` with only 2/12 wins and wall by `+0.312%`.

Reject all three layouts under the Pareto rule. Unit 293's fixed-tree expansion
has already reduced the unused build below a stable whole-process saving, and
the extra optional/lazy control perturbs the monolithic picker enough to erase
it. The isolated source returns to the committed tree. Do not revisit table
laziness unless a fresh profile again attributes a material share to its build.

## Unit 298 — reject tile-scoped MV-grid clearing

The current profile mapped one hot picker address to the final `out_mv_grid`
reset. In four-tile mode each persistent worker owns a frame-sized MV grid, but
the merge reads only that worker's tile columns. An exact candidate therefore
cleared only the active tile's rows, preserving default values for any uncovered
cell while removing three quarters of the apparent reset traffic.

The focused previous-MV-grid regression passed, and the standard stream stayed
exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
The process screen showed that the attributed source line was not a meaningful
standalone bottleneck: twelve alternating four-thread pairs changed wall by
`-0.131%` and total child CPU by `-0.025%`, with 7/12 wall and 6/12 CPU wins.

Reject the extra branch and row-slice loop as measurement-floor noise. The
source is fully restored. Future work should use a symbol or caller-level
profile before treating another line inside the monolithic picker as its own
cost centre.

## Unit 299 — reject carrying the NEWMV seed SAD into diamond search

The realtime NEWMV seed selector measures SAD for the best nearest/near or
integer-projection start. Both full-pixel diamond implementations then measure
that same start block again before visiting their search sites. An exact
candidate carried the raw SAD only when clamping and full-pel conversion left
the measured start unchanged; all other cases kept the original scan.

A focused differential proved that precomputed and ordinary starts return the
same complete result from both diamond algorithms. All 62 inter-mode tests
passed, and the standard stream remained exactly 740,177 bytes with SHA-256
`6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.

The removed scan was too sparse to offset the additional control and API
shape. Twelve alternating four-thread pairs changed wall by `+0.657%` and
total child CPU by `+0.086%`, with only 4/12 wall and 6/12 CPU wins. Reject
the candidate and retain the simpler self-contained search entry points; the
source and test are fully restored.

## Unit 300 — reject pre-search NEWMV adaptive-threshold gating

Pinned libvpx applies its adaptive RD threshold before NEWMV motion search while
the slot still contains `INVALID_MV`; rvp9 applies the same threshold only after
searching and therefore uses the discovered MV for the zero-MV exemption. A
focused test counter proved that moving the gate ahead of NEWMV suppressed both
LAST and GOLDEN searches when their threshold factors were saturated, while the
gate-off control exercised the search.

Two layouts were screened against a same-source-path baseline. Moving the full
gate ahead of every candidate stayed bit-exact on the standard 120-frame screen
and 60-frame foreman inputs. Its two four-thread standard screens changed total
child CPU by `+0.056%` and `+0.080%`; its one-thread control improved `-0.610%`.
On foreman it regressed total CPU by `+2.950%` with 5/12 wins. A narrower layout
gated only NEWMV immediately before its search and left other modes on the old
common gate. Its first standard screen improved total CPU by `-1.874%`, but the
repeat regressed `+0.676%`; foreman again regressed, by `+2.550%`, with 4/12
wins.

Both layouts preserved the canonical standard stream at 740,177 bytes and
SHA-256 `6991a5b50db78b87c4b01ba02e32c948bfb0a97ea693381b9e2ddb8752adfa1d`.
They also preserved the 74,478-byte foreman stream at SHA-256
`fbf49dca6105470b92861d8283fea1c0e6ce4455840f401d168b74c851e002a6`.
The source-order difference is real, but the current production workloads do
not skip enough searches to pay for the extra hot-loop control. Reject both
forms under the Pareto rule; the isolated source and focused instrumentation
are fully restored.

## Unit 301 — retain luma-model distortion reuse in the Stage 4a picker

The Stage 4a Hadamard-only picker ran the luma variance RD model and then
reduced every quantized Hadamard coefficient again with four independent
64-bit error accumulators. Pinned libvpx already treats the model result as a
complete distortion estimate on its `use_simple_block_yrd` path. The retained
typed calibration reuses that model distortion for Stage 4a ranking and runs
the Hadamard quantizer's rate/EOB-only kernel. Other calibrations and candidate
tracing retain exact coefficient-error collection.

A focused oracle rebuilds the selected prediction and proves the result's
ranking distortion equals the luma model output. The existing Hadamard-only
oracle still proves non-Stage-4a calibrations preserve exact coefficient rate
and distortion. Both focused release tests, warnings-denied release core
clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass.

The standard stream changes from 740,177 to 737,009 bytes with SHA-256
`408b1974fc5a1ee0f184a4f3815f129d016c0c576505037091a4a6dc51ef837e`.
Controlled twelve-pair tests, four encodes per sample, show a large and stable
reduction:

- one thread: wall `-7.678%`, user CPU `-6.883%`, total CPU `-6.894%`, all
  twelve wins;
- four threads: wall `-7.310%`, user CPU `-6.968%`, total CPU `-6.680%`, all
  twelve wins.

The clean-tree seven-point product reports both pass at commit `ad8f9a0`:

- strict baseline: `-4.374424%` BD-rate, `-0.160184 dB` matched-rate PSNR,
  `8.195042 dB` overlap;
- candidate split policy: `-4.038715%` BD-rate, `-0.149870 dB` matched-rate
  PSNR, `8.188509 dB` overlap.

Every stream passed rvp9-decoder and decoded byte-exactly under pinned vpxdec
and ffmpeg. Retain the unit. Rebuild the accepted binary, measure the new
pinned total-CPU ratio, and profile the reduced picker before choosing another
operation.

- four threads: wall `-3.798%`, user CPU `-5.453%`, total CPU `-5.221%`, all

The clean-tree seven-point reports both pass at commit `b7afb6c`:

- candidate split policy: `-6.282179%` BD-rate, `-0.248994 dB` matched-rate
  PSNR, `8.236046 dB` overlap.

Every stream passed rvp9-decoder and decoded byte-exactly under pinned vpxdec
and ffmpeg. Retain the unit. The formal quality result improves over Unit 301

## Unit 303 — supersede the SATD-only Hadamard quantizer

Against Unit 301, the product Hadamard quantizer still computed an exact final
scan position even though its only consumer tested zero versus non-zero EOB.
An exact AArch64 candidate removed inverse-scan loads and EOB reduction, derived
skippability from `SATD == 0`, and retained the original SATD arithmetic. A
randomized differential covered Tx8x8, Tx16x16, and Tx32x32 across six qindices,
signed extremes, zero, DC-only, and final-scan-only inputs.

The candidate preserved Unit 301's 737,009-byte standard stream at SHA-256
`408b1974fc5a1ee0f184a4f3815f129d016c0c576505037091a4a6dc51ef837e`.
Three same-path paired screens reproduced a useful saving: four-thread total
CPU improved `-0.684%` and `-1.626%`, with 8/12 and 12/12 wins; the one-thread
control improved `-2.056%` with 10/12 wins.

Do not retain the narrower kernel. Unit 302 landed concurrently and removes
the entire product Hadamard transform and quantizer by reusing the luma model's
rate, distortion, and skip state. The SATD-only kernel would now serve only a
non-product compatibility path outside the active speed gate. The isolated
source and differential test are fully restored. Keep this result as evidence
that exact EOB position is unnecessary if a future product path again consumes
the Hadamard rate kernel.

## Unit 304 — reject removing the integer-projection NEWMV seed

The Unit 302 profile attributes 160 self samples inside the partition wrapper
to the per-superblock integer-projection motion search. A diagnostic skipped

The standard stream changed from 739,474 to 738,812 bytes with SHA-256
`19d604b0b2ffcf2c1bebd762e7ac7b623df8cf1ce234332cab34f4314e9ec148`.

Controlled twelve-pair screens, four encodes per sample, showed that this is a

- four threads: wall `-1.851%` and total CPU `-3.999%`, with all twelve wins.

The clean-tree seven-point oracle rejects the candidate at commit `6e4bab4`.

## Unit 305 — retain picker-owned final mode-info grids

The Unit 302 four-thread profile showed the main thread rebuilding every
mode-info cell from the committed partition descriptors after the parallel
picker barrier. Each tile picker already owned the same causal grid. The
retained change finalizes those cells while it commits the selected leaves,
returns each tile's local column span, and merges the disjoint row slices with
the reconstruction and previous-MV grids. The one-thread path consumes its
full picker grid directly. A debug oracle retains the old descriptor rebuild
and proves both representations agree.

The finalization step is load-bearing. Reusing the causal cells unchanged made
the release four-tile regression fail because those cells still held the
pick-time maximum transform and omitted the finalized compound second
reference. Overwriting each covered cell with `leaf.mode_info()` after the
causal lookup phase fixed the mismatch. Both four-tile release regressions now
pass, including exact output across one and four threads and exact-VBP history.
Warnings-denied release encoder clippy, formatting, and diff checks also pass.

The standard 120-frame stream remains exactly 739,474 bytes with SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`,
so Unit 302's cross-decoder and quality evidence applies byte-for-byte. Three
independent twelve-pair four-thread screens, four encodes per sample, changed
wall time by `-1.560%`, `-2.934%`, and `-2.167%`, with 9/12, 7/12, and 9/12
wins. Total child CPU changed `-1.605%`, `+0.016%`, and `-1.164%`. The
one-thread control was neutral: wall `-0.050%`, total CPU `-0.039%`, and 6/12
wins for both.

Retain the unit as a production-width wall-time improvement. It moves the
final descriptor work into the existing independent tile jobs without adding
single-thread cost or changing the stream. Rebuild the accepted binary and
remeasure the matched pinned-vpx four-thread ratio before selecting the next
parallel-scaling bottleneck.

## Unit 305 — reject loop-filter condition-variable wakeups

The Unit 302 profile attributes 175 self samples to the encoder loop-filter's
256-spin/yield column-wavefront wait. Unit 240 had already rejected lower spin
thresholds because they transferred user work into scheduler work. This unit
tested the remaining structural alternative: per-row condition variables that
wake when the preceding row publishes its next safe column.

Immediate blocking preserved the serial/parallel pixel oracle but failed the
four-thread product screen: total CPU improved `-2.028%` with nine of twelve
wins, while wall regressed `+0.841%`, system CPU rose `+15.655%`, and only five
wall samples won. A hybrid kept the proven 256-spin handoff and blocked only
after that budget. It still regressed wall `+0.272%`, raised system CPU
`+7.971%`, and reduced total CPU only `-0.262%` with seven wins.

The full synchronization candidate is removed. On this field, explicit kernel
wakeups cost more latency and scheduler work than polling. Do not revisit the
wavefront wait without a schedule that eliminates the dependency rather than
changing how workers sleep on it.

## Unit 306 — reject rebuilding collapsed coefficient counts after tile merge

The retained-token count pass increments both libvpx's full twelve-token
coefficient histogram and its exactly derivable four-token model histogram for
every token. A candidate wrote only the twelve-token bank, rebuilt the model
once after tile merge, and preserved the decoder/direct-count path unchanged.
The optimized form also skipped merging each recorded tile's known-zero model
bank before the rebuild.

The focused projection oracle, all retained-token replay tests, and both live
TWO_LOOP tests passed. The latter still updated 30 tables, suppressed 10
would-update tables, and decoded byte-exactly through pinned vpxdec. The
standard stream remained exactly 739,474 bytes with SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

The first form appeared promising in one four-thread screen (`-0.572%` total
CPU, eleven of twelve wins), but regressed the one-thread control by `+0.430%`
and `+0.143%` across two screens. After removing the redundant zero-bank merge,
the one-thread result became neutral-to-positive (`-0.163%`, seven wins), but
the repeated four-thread screen was also neutral: `-0.053%` total CPU,
`+0.077%` wall, and six/five wins. The earlier apparent gain was measurement
noise. The complete source candidate is removed; retaining a second count
representation lifecycle is not justified without a material speed result.

## Unit 307 — retain parallel realtime source-map producers

The post-Unit-305 thread profile left the realtime source SAD/variance pass and
skin detector serial before tile picking. They accounted for roughly ten
percent of sampled main-thread work and write independent state. The retained
path splits each producer into two disjoint row jobs on the existing
caller-participating frame worker pool. The scope joins before scene detection
or the picker consumes either map. One-thread encoding retains the serial
path, and no threads or dependencies are added.

A focused oracle compares the serial and parallel producers on deterministic
luma/chroma inputs, non-uniform zero-MV streaks, and an unequal final row
chunk. The source-SAD values, content-state classifications, and every skin
cell agree exactly. The focused release oracle and both four-tile release
thread-count/exactness tests pass. Warnings-denied release encoder clippy,
formatting, and diff checks pass.

The standard 120-frame stream remains byte-identical at 739,474 bytes with
SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`,
so Unit 302's quality and cross-decoder evidence applies unchanged. The
same-source-path twelve-pair four-thread screen improved wall time `-2.073%`
with 9/12 wins. A separate screen improved `-2.702%` with all twelve wins.
The one-thread control changed wall by `+0.211%`, within the measurement floor,
and remained byte-identical.

The worker-pool coordination raises total child CPU: `+1.173%` in the
same-path screen and `+0.624%` in the separate repeat. Two- and three-job
variants reduced the CPU charge but also reduced the reproducible wall gain to
`-1.475%` and `-1.786%`; retain the four-job layout because the production
acceptance metric is latency, quality is exact, and no single-thread work is
added. The matched pinned-vpx screen now reports `1.263x` wall time. Continue
with the next measured parallel-scaling bottleneck; the final target remains
`<=1.05x`.

## Unit 308 — reject linear retained-coefficient replay

The retained coefficient replay used an indexed outer loop plus an inner zero
run. A candidate replaced it with a single iterator and an explicit
`needs_eob` state, preserving the exact VP9 decision sequence while aiming to
remove repeated indexing and bounds checks. All three retained-token unit
tests passed, and the standard stream remained exactly 739,474 bytes with
SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

The isolated twelve-pair four-thread screen rejects the rewrite. Wall time
regressed `+2.045%` with three wins, and total child CPU regressed `+1.791%`
with three wins. LLVM's original nested-loop shape is materially better for
the zero-run grammar; the complete source candidate is restored.

This unit also independently audited Unit 307 from clean exact-tree binaries,
excluding the replay experiment. Two twelve-pair screens reproduced the
source-map wall benefit at `-0.715%` and `-1.860%`, but measured total-CPU
costs of `+2.629%` and `+1.442%`. Unit 307 therefore carries explicit CPU debt
against the final `<=1.05x` total-CPU gate even though it advances the separate
hard wall-latency gate. Reassess that trade if later CPU work cannot recover
the charge.

## Unit 309 — retain persistent worker-scope completion channels

The post-Unit-307 profile showed balanced codec work but repeated worker parks
across the source-map, picker, loop-filter, and tile-writer scopes. Every scope
allocated a fresh unbounded completion channel and updated a separate atomic
pending counter on submission and drain, even though `scope(&mut self)` makes
scopes mutually exclusive. The retained protocol owns one completion channel
per worker pool, counts submissions with the existing monotonic job index, and
drains exactly that many outcomes before returning. Submission indices use
relaxed atomic ordering; the atomic modification order still gives every job a
unique panic-priority index, while channel send/receive provides the join
synchronization.

The panic and lifetime guarantees remain explicit. Every job still catches its
payload and sends an unconditional outcome; caller-reserved jobs still run
after a closure panic; and the scope still joins all borrowed jobs before it
rethrows the earliest submitted panic. A new regression triggers a worker
panic, catches the propagated payload, and then proves the same pool completes
a second scope, guarding against a stale completion outcome. All 20 focused
tile-threading tests and warnings-denied release core clippy pass.

Three same-source-path twelve-pair four-thread screens improved wall time by
`-2.110%`, `-0.487%`, and `-0.854%`, with 8/12, 7/12, and 8/12 wins. Total
child CPU improved `-0.865%`, `-0.351%`, and `-0.687%`, with 7/12, 8/12, and
9/12 wins. The one-thread control showed no regression (`-1.042%` wall,
`-1.315%` total CPU). The standard stream remains byte-identical at 739,474
bytes and SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

Retain the unit as a synchronization Pareto improvement. Rebuild the accepted
binary and measure the matched pinned-vpx ratio before selecting another
barrier or critical-path hypothesis.

## Unit 311 — retain tile-local reconstruction initialization

Each parallel picker job owned a frame-shaped reconstruction scratch and
copied all three complete LAST reference planes into it before encoding only
one column tile. The main thread later copied only that tile rectangle back,
so four tiles read and wrote roughly three redundant frames per inter frame.
The retained path initializes only the active tile's full-height luma and
chroma column spans. The serial picker still performs the original full-plane
copies.

Tile mode-decision and reconstruction cannot consume pixels across a column
tile boundary: the causal mode-info lookup is tile-clamped, reference
prediction reads the separate immutable LAST/GOLDEN planes, and every emitted
leaf lies inside the active tile. Both release four-tile regressions pass,
including one-versus-four-thread exact output and exact-VBP history. Release
warnings-denied encoder clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass.

Four same-source-path twelve-pair four-thread screens changed wall time by
`-1.562%`, `+0.863%`, `-1.006%`, and `+0.459%`. Their median-of-screen result
is `-0.274%`; wall remains close to the measurement floor. Total child CPU
changed `-2.214%`, `+0.448%`, `-1.513%`, and `-0.256%`, a median-of-screen
improvement of `-0.884%` with three of four screens improving. The standard
stream remains byte-identical at 739,474 bytes and SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

Retain the unit because it removes proven parallel-only memory traffic,
recovers part of Unit 307's total-CPU debt, preserves quality exactly, and has
no serial-path cost. Continue from a fresh accepted profile; do not infer a
large wall gain from the first screen alone.

`+0.167%`, within code-layout noise for a path that does not execute these
slots.

clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass. The standard stream remains exactly
739,474 bytes with SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

12/12 wins. Retain the unit as a small exact-output CPU-and-wall improvement.

## Unit 316 — reject tile-local coefficient sources in the final writer

The refreshed Unit 315 profile places 19 samples at the parallel
`merged_coefs.merge_from(result.coefs)` call, while retained coefficient replay

`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

justified by the small wall movement. Reject the candidate. The next
experiment should target retained replay's measured inner cost rather than

## Unit 317 — reject hoisted coefficient-replay diagnostics check

The Unit 315 profile's hottest replay instructions are arithmetic-coder

neutral and does not justify duplicate arithmetic-coder entry paths. Reject
the experiment and retain Unit 315 unchanged.

## Unit 318 — retain reusable streaming Y4M frame planes

The accepted profile still attributed 77 samples to fresh Y4M plane
allocations and `madvise`. One-pass streaming created three new vectors for

Three twelve-pair four-thread screens against the exact accepted Unit 317
binary improved wall time by `-1.037%`, `-1.165%`, and `-1.114%`, with 12/12
wins in every screen. Total child CPU improved by `-0.381%`, `-0.565%`, and
`-0.375%`; the exact final build won 11/12 pairs. System CPU fell between
`-8.0%` and `-9.1%`. The canonical output remains 739,474 bytes with SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.

The reusable-reader oracle proves both frame order and stable plane pointers.
All 102 I/O tests, the three affected streaming CLI tests, warnings-denied
clippy for both affected crates, formatting, and diff checks pass. A broader
`enc_y4m_` filter also selected two pre-existing diagnostic-wording tests that
expect `exceeds source` while the unchanged reader reports `exceeds y4m`;
those failures are outside this performance unit. Retain reusable frame planes
as an exact-output wall-and-CPU Pareto improvement.

## Unit 319 — reject Hadamard output in residual scratch

The Unit 318 profile attributed 3,298 self samples (`10.56%`) to
`_platform_memset`, almost all beneath the Hadamard-only candidate round trip.
The AArch64 subtract-transform overwrites every coefficient it consumes, and
the existing reusable residual slab is otherwise idle on that product path.
A candidate wrote Hadamard coefficients into that slab and kept a local
coefficient array only for the compatibility reconstruction path. This is
distinct from rejected Unit 161: it removes live scratch rather than adding a
second persistent slab.

The candidate preserved the canonical 739,474-byte stream and SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`, but a
twelve-pair four-thread screen changed wall by only `-0.097%` with 8/12 wins
and total child CPU by `-0.031%` with 6/12 wins. The optimized product path
therefore does not pay the profiler's apparent zero-fill cost in a removable
form; reusing residual scratch only trades stack initialization against buffer
aliasing and locality. Reject the candidate and do not treat caller-attributed
`_platform_memset` samples as a ten-percent opportunity without an operation-
level oracle.

## Unit 320 — reject disabling realtime NEWMV

Existing diagnostic policy switches mapped the remaining quality-bearing mode
cost. Disabling NEARMV, GOLDEN, switchable-filter search, or sub-32 partition
sizes moved standard product CPU only at the noise floor. Disabling NEWMV cut
median total child CPU from `0.474263 s` to `0.432931 s` (`-8.72%`) and wall
from `0.200916 s` to `0.183566 s`, enough by itself to cross the pinned-libvpx
CPU limit. The output grew only 2,152 bytes on the synthetic speed clip.

The official seven-point Foreman quality oracle decisively rejects that trade.
A source-default candidate, run without forbidden environment overrides,
regressed BD-rate from the accepted `-6.340554%` to `+124.623106%` and missed
matched-rate PSNR by `3.395723 dB`. NEWMV is Foreman's only effective motion
mode; removing it left 77.5% of coded area as NEARESTMV and 22.5% intra.
Disabling NEWMV only through 8x8 or 16x16 blocks did not improve the standard
speed workload, while the saving appeared when 32x32 was included. The source
candidate is fully removed. Preserve NEWMV coverage and target its search or
seed kernels without changing the winning motion evidence.

## Unit 318 — reject source-free retained block replay

Valid retained replay already owns every probability-independent coefficient
decision, but the modes writer still looked up the corresponding raw
coefficient block before replay returned without reading it. A detached
same-source-path experiment added a replay-only block API that skipped the raw
source lookup. Malformed or missing retained boundaries still marked the pass
mismatched, and the tile wrapper still rejected the partial packet.

Two twelve-pair four-thread screens changed wall time by `+0.071%` and
`-0.104%`, and child CPU by `+0.121%` and `-0.035%`. The change is neutral;
the lookup is not a useful bottleneck, and the larger replay API is not
justified. Reject the experiment and keep the existing checked fallback.

## Unit 319 — reject empty-vector storage for zero-EOB transforms

`VecBackedInterCoefSource` already interprets an empty coefficient vector with
`eob = 0` as a full all-zero transform, but emission widened and collected the

used the existing empty marker and skipped that collection. The focused
all-zero source oracle covers every transform size.

Two twelve-pair four-thread screens changed wall time by `-0.004%` and
`+0.117%`, and child CPU by `+0.024%` and `+0.063%`. The result is neutral;
zero-block allocation is not on the limiting path. Reject the source change.

The 32x32-and-larger luma model built three fixed 8x8-statistic arrays, then

Two twelve-pair four-thread screens against the exact Unit 318 binary improved
wall time by `-0.473%` and `-0.433%`, with 10/12 and 8/12 wins. Total child
CPU improved by `-0.247%` and `-0.360%`, with 10/12 and 9/12 wins. All 48
model-RD tests, warnings-denied core clippy, formatting, and diff checks pass.
Retain the direct reduction as a smaller, exact large-candidate hot path.

## Unit 322 — fuse variance partitioning into tile picker jobs

The accepted profile placed the whole variance-based partition pass on the
already-busier caller thread: `choose_partitions_for_frame` accounted for

win, but its extra worker scope raised total child CPU by `+2.122%`.

The retained form computes each tile column's partition decisions at the

Three twelve-pair four-thread screens against the same-source baseline

and 11/12 wins. The final form changed total child CPU by `+0.758%`; system
CPU improved by `-0.388%`. This is retained because the acceptance gate is
median wall encode time at the same four-thread budget, and the material
latency win does not change that budget or quality.

The canonical output remains 739,474 bytes with SHA-256
`c1409ab6cfbcc786ca38aa7501f447461e41c2e1ec7a901e0be92ffff3a2b553`.
Both four-tile thread-count determinism tests, exact VBP-history coverage,

`1.135957x`. Continue from the remaining picker, coefficient replay, motion
search, and transform hot paths rather than adding another partition scope.

## Unit 323 — reject shorter caller loop-filter row group

The Unit 322 thread profile still showed 1,133 binary samples on the caller
versus 926–989 on each worker. The caller-participating pool reserves the
first submitted loop-filter job, while 11 SB rows split across four workers
give the final static group only two rows and the other groups three. A
candidate submitted that shorter final group first, leaving the original
dependency-leading groups on OS workers; filter logic and wavefront state
were unchanged.

The canonical stream remained byte-exact, but a twelve-pair four-thread
screen regressed wall time by `+0.510%` with only 4/12 wins and total child

rows and makes the caller spin rather than reducing the critical path.
Reject the ordering change. Keep dependency-leading worker zero as the
caller job unless the wavefront scheduler itself is redesigned and measured.

## Unit 324 — reject adapted MV-cost table cache

The Unit 322 profile attributed 35 caller-thread samples to rebuilding the

than memoizing frame-varying inputs.

The no-high-precision MV-cost builder emits each fractional cost twice for

`splat_inter_leaf_into_mi_grid` accounted for 41 self samples and recomputed

Each realtime NEWMV search compares the causal nearest/near candidates with

The accepted profile attributed 5.28% inclusive time to the superblock

The existing `RVP9_RT_NEWMV_MAX_ITERS` diagnostic controlled the multiscale

Every retained transform block stores a packed nonzero bit alongside its token

is cheaper than extending replay's token-slice dependency. Reject the

## Unit 331 — fuse final mode and MV grid splats

The picker wrote every committed leaf into its causal mode-info grid, then

The canonical product stream remains exactly 738,335 bytes with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

thread-count determinism, both previous-MV-grid tests, ALTREF and compound
cross-decoder round trips, warnings-denied encoder clippy, formatting, and
diff checks pass. Retain the fused grid commit.

The AArch64 Laplacian high-frequency kernel loaded three overlapping vectors

wins and total child CPU by `+0.251%` with 2/12 wins. The load reduction does

and keep the current direct-load kernel.

The 32-wide NEON SAD kernel widened each pair of residual bytes into u32 lanes

add saturates to u8. Runtime dispatch selects it only when `caps.neon` is
true. The realtime inter round-trip and the encoder's full-RDO round-trip now

## Unit 350 — vectorize AArch64 8-tap loop filtering

## Unit 354 — copy narrow prediction rows in pairs on AArch64

The AArch64 copy-convolve kernel previously switched on width for every row
and completed each row's load/store before starting the next. The retained
implementation follows pinned libvpx's scheduling for widths 4, 8, 16, and
32: it selects width once, loads two rows before their stores, and advances by
two. Width 64 remains row-at-a-time. Unlike libvpx's internal even-height
contract, rvp9's safe wrapper permits any positive height, so each narrow
kernel retains an odd-row tail. Focused differential coverage now includes
odd heights for every supported width.

shortcut is not a Pareto improvement under rvp9's surrounding RD model.

## Unit 360 — prune intra modes below an impossible RD floor

Every intra fallback candidate has a fixed nonnegative syntax cost before its
prediction, coefficient rate, or distortion is known: intra mode cost,
INTRA-frame reference cost, and the realtime intra penalty. Coefficient rate
and distortion can only add to that floor. The retained picker therefore
skips a mode when `RDCOST(lambda, fixed_rate, 0)` is already greater than or
equal to the strict current winner, using the better of the inter incumbent
and any prior intra candidate. This cannot change the argmin because ties do
not replace the incumbent. A focused zero-incumbent oracle proves every
nonnegative intra candidate is pruned.

Both product streams remain exact. Canonical cpu-used 7 VBR is 738,335 bytes,
SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`;
exact-VBP CBR is 979,983 bytes, SHA-256
`add36b5d2682bce50c1f76e76c8876651fc64ee5854825f3e1774c0a8ef11ec7`.
Two clean alternating twelve-pair screens against Unit 359 changed wall time
by `-0.989%` and `+0.090%`, with 9/12 and 6/12 wins. Total child CPU fell by
`2.221%` and `0.671%`, with 10/12 and 8/12 wins. The wall repeat is neutral;
both screens reproduce the CPU reduction and neither shows a material wall
regression.

The focused RD-floor/max-intra-size test passes. Core all-target release

## Unit 362 — apply adaptive RD thresholds to realtime intra modes

The P20 threshold table already carried libvpx's DC, V, and H `THR_MODES`
slots, but rvp9 read and updated only LAST/GOLDEN inter slots. The retained
change maps the three realtime intra modes onto those existing slots, rejects
an intra candidate before prediction when the current RD incumbent is below
its effective threshold, and updates the three frequency factors after an
intra winner. A focused oracle proves a high threshold prunes all three modes;
table tests prove the exact slot mapping and winner-decay/loser-increment
state transition.

Two broader shortcuts were rejected while isolating this change. Disabling

100/250 kbps targets. Suppressing intra after libvpx-shaped encode breakout
had the same Foreman regression. Suppressing it only after the large-model
early-termination flag kept three Foreman points exact and improved synthetic
luma PSNR, but regressed the twelve-pair synthetic screen by `0.749%` wall and
`0.280%` total CPU. All three broad variants were removed.

The retained adaptive gate is a reproducible Pareto improvement. On the
canonical exact-VBP 2 Mbps CBR point, the stream moves from 979,983 bytes and
aggregate luma PSNR `37.534496 dB` to 983,226 bytes and `37.669123 dB`.

total child CPU by `4.917%` with 12/12 wins. The standard cpu-used 7 VBR

`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

The seven-point 320x256 Foreman CBR comparison improves `0.047584%` BD-rate

`f12ccfafd437c8778bd0c10380b1f80d01c3582c1455e0de195cf43815c65db9`.

## Unit 364 — reject a standalone partition color-sensitivity gate

Pinned libvpx skips chroma model-RD when both per-SB color-sensitivity flags
are false. Rvp9 already had a source-faithful diagnostic producer but did not
consume it. On the 256x256 Foreman diagnostic all 23,940 recorded leaves had
both flags false; on the cropped synthetic diagnostic, 1,540/3,305 leaves had
both false. This made the missing consumer look like a structural chroma-work
opportunity.

Two product variants were screened. The first selected LAST or GOLDEN for the
SB sensitivity pass, then hid both chroma source planes from the leaf picker
when neither flag was set. The canonical exact-VBP point improved from 983,226
bytes / `37.669123 dB` luma to 982,037 bytes / `37.748038 dB`, but a clean
twelve-pair screen regressed wall time by `1.971%` and total child CPU by
`7.577%`. The second variant avoided the extra GOLDEN 64x64 SAD and always
used the existing LAST projection seed. It produced 979,833 bytes /
`37.584030 dB`, losing `0.085093 dB` luma, and still regressed wall time by
`1.244%` and total child CPU by `2.858%`.

Both variants were removed. Libvpx obtains color sensitivity inside its
partition-prediction flow and can reuse prediction state; rvp9's standalone
pass duplicates two chroma predictions (and, in the first variant, a full
luma SAD) for every SB. Do not retry this as a separate prepass. It only
becomes viable if sensitivity falls out of partition work rvp9 already needs
for another measured reason.

## Unit 370 — vectorize top/bottom-clamped int-pro rows

A fresh twelve-pair absolute comparison after Unit 369 measures rvp9/vpxenc
at `1.922955x` wall and `1.871401x` total child CPU on the canonical
quality-complete CBR point. Median wall times are 0.459926 s versus 0.248955 s;
median child CPU times are 0.937499 s versus 0.502739 s. This is the current
fresh speed baseline; the final quiet-host corpus matrix remains pending.

The matched profiles show another SIMD asymmetry in SB-level integer
projection. Libvpx's physically extended borders keep its 16-column NEON row
reduction active at the top and bottom frame edges. Rvp9 implements equivalent
border replication over a tight visible plane, but its clamped-row helper
summed all 16 columns in scalar Rust whenever the 64-row window crossed a
vertical edge.

The retained AArch64 helper clamps each source-row index, loads the resulting
16-byte row with NEON, accumulates four rows per iteration, and applies the
same height-dependent normalization as the interior kernel. The caller uses
it only when all 16 columns are visible and only Y needs clamping; horizontal
edge replication and all non-AArch64 behavior remain unchanged. All 18
focused int-pro tests pass, including mixed-edge projection comparisons
against the pixel oracle.

`-0.634%`, `+6.381%`, and `-0.411%`; total child CPU falls by `0.569%`,
`0.609%`, and `1.108%`. The middle wall result is an isolated scheduling
outlier: both its user and system CPU improve, while the first and third wall
screens reproduce the gain. Canonical cpu-used 7 VBR remains 738,335 bytes,
SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`;

`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
The alternating twelve-pair screen rejected it: median wall time increased
`0.463%`, total child CPU increased `0.586%`, and each won only 4/12 pairs.
The stack bookkeeping outweighed the avoided allocation, so the code change
was removed. Keep the line-table profile, but do not retry partition-vector
reuse without eliminating the segment-ID pass rather than merely moving it.

## Unit 372 — share one TLS borrow across inter residual and quant scratch

The line-table profile attributed repeated samples to the residual-emission
call site. Each non-zero transform entered one thread-local `RefCell` for its
residual buffer and, while that borrow remained live, entered a second TLS
`RefCell` for transform and quantization storage. Both buffers have the same
tile-worker lifetime and are consumed serially.

The retained change groups the residual and quantization fields under one
thread-local scratch object. The hot emit path borrows it once, splits the
disjoint fields, and passes the quantization storage directly into the
existing transform/quant routine. The test-only wrapper still exercises the
quant routine independently. No buffer is shared across worker threads, and
the active-prefix and prior-transform-size tests both pass.

Two alternating twelve-pair screens against Unit 370 reproduce the gain.
Median wall time changes by `-1.621%` and `-0.150%`, with 10/12 and 6/12
wins. Total child CPU falls by `2.125%` and `1.058%`, with 9/12 and 7/12
wins. The cpu-used 7 VBR stream remains 738,335 bytes with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`;
exact-VBP CBR remains 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
Encoder all-target release clippy passes with warnings denied; formatting and
diff checks pass.

## Unit 373 — reject a frame coefficient arena

The residual-emission profile and Unit 372's successful scratch consolidation
suggested replacing every non-zero transform's `Vec<i32>` allocation and
`i16`-to-`i32` collection with one flat coefficient arena owned by the frame's
coefficient source. Block slots held arena ranges, including replacement
semantics for repeated simulation writes.

The first exact-output candidate preserved the canonical exact-VBP CBR stream
at 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`, but
an alternating twelve-pair screen against Unit 372 increased median wall time
by `1.001%` and total child CPU by `2.301%`, with only 3/12 wins. Reserving the
exact worst-case coefficient capacity also preserved the stream, but made the
result worse: median wall time increased `1.374%`, total child CPU increased
`3.037%`, and it won only 2/12 wall and 1/12 CPU pairs.

The existing small per-block allocator performs better than contiguous arena
writes and conversions on this workload. Both arena variants were removed.
Do not retry coefficient packing without a profile showing that allocation or
conversion, rather than coefficient production and replay, is the bottleneck.

## Unit 374 — quantify exact-tree leaf inflation; reject uniform AQ lookup

The existing realtime phase counters show why the quality-complete path is
not merely a few percent slower. Across the canonical 120-frame, four-tile
CBR point, exact VBP produces 144,958 final leaves versus 51,346 for the
standard tree (`2.82x`). Its final-picker and emission phases consume about
673 ms of aggregate worker time, while the standard tree's descent and
emission consume about 382 ms. The next large speed change must therefore
reduce exact-tree per-leaf work or reach the required quality with fewer
leaves; isolated sub-percent kernels cannot close the gap alone.

The line profile also attributed work to copying exact leaves and recovering
their AQ segment IDs from the old hint partition. A candidate detected a
uniform segment once per superblock and reused it for all exact leaves,
falling back to the established cell lookup for mixed-AQ hints. The canonical
stream remained 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`, and
both exact-history tests passed.

The alternating twelve-pair screen rejected it. Median wall time increased
`1.804%`, total child CPU increased `2.513%`, and each won only 5/12 pairs.
The one-time scan and added branch cost more than the short existing lookups
on AQ-off input. The source change was removed. Do not add another
precomputed segment representation without eliminating work elsewhere in the
same exact-leaf conversion.

## Unit 375 — reject coarser exact-VBP threshold variants

The Unit 374 leaf-count result motivated a threshold sweep instead of another
primitive optimization. A temporary runtime probe multiplied the exact VBP
64x64, 32x32, and 16x16 thresholds independently. Doubling all three reduced
the sampled total child CPU from about 1.012 s to 0.970 s, but lost 0.251 dB
at the canonical 2 Mbps point. Four- and eight-times variants lost 0.646 dB
and 0.951 dB. Those broad settings are not credible quality candidates.

Doubling only the 16x16 threshold looked Pareto-positive in the initial sweep:
the stream moved from 983,226 bytes / 37.669123 dB luma to 981,485 bytes /
37.692285 dB. A clean build then removed all runtime sweep fields and
hard-coded only that one threshold change, so its code shape could be compared
fairly with Unit 372.

The alternating twelve-pair comparison rejected it. Median wall time increased
`6.207%`, total child CPU increased `1.018%`, and CPU won only 2/12 pairs.
Although the tree is coarser, its surviving leaves cause more expensive work;
the isolated point is a quality-only win and fails the joint Pareto rule. All
threshold-sweep and hard-coded source changes were removed. Do not infer speed
from leaf count alone; require a paired product measurement because leaf size
also changes mode-search and transform cost.

## Unit 376 — reject copy-based winning-prediction retention

Pinned libvpx's picker retains candidate prediction buffers and copies the
winner into the destination instead of rebuilding its luma interpolation in
the encode pass. Rvp9's picker scratch previously exposed no equivalent
handoff, so final emission repeated the winning prediction.

A source-exact candidate added a protected thread-local luma buffer. Whenever
a fractional-MV candidate became the current best, it copied that candidate's
tight prediction into the buffer. A fresh final pick could then copy the
retained winner directly into the reconstruction plane. Integer motion,
cached/descent picks, changed causal MVs, compound prediction, and a distinct
ME-side denoised reference all retained the established emission path.

The canonical exact-VBP stream remained 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
The alternating twelve-pair screen nevertheless changed median wall time by
`+0.742%` and total child CPU by `+0.364%`, with only 4/12 CPU wins. Copying
each provisional winner costs more than rebuilding the final interpolation.
The complete source change was removed. Prediction reuse remains plausible
only with libvpx-style buffer-slot rotation or another ownership transfer that
does not copy pixels during the candidate loop.

## Unit 377 — reject heap-slot winning-prediction rotation

The no-copy follow-up replaced the two inline luma prediction arrays with
three boxed arrays. Candidate evaluation used the primary and alternate
slots; when a fractional candidate became best, the active slot swapped its
box pointer with the protected winner slot. This made every provisional
winner handoff constant-time and left only the final copy into reconstruction.

The canonical exact-VBP stream again remained 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
The alternating twelve-pair screen rejected the representation: median wall
time increased `3.236%`, total child CPU increased `1.321%`, and CPU won only
3/12 pairs. Heap indirection on every candidate is more expensive than the
saved final interpolation on this workload. The source was restored to the
inline two-buffer scratch. Do not revisit winner-prediction retention without
a representation that preserves inline candidate access and transfers
ownership without copying.

## Unit 378 — reject gating Phase-2 positive-control atomics

Every final RT-picker leaf updates the global Phase-2 reused/fresh counters,
although only an ignored positive-control test and `RVP9_RT_PROFILE` consume
them. A candidate added an explicit instrumentation enable flag, loaded it
once per tile job, and skipped the per-leaf relaxed atomic read-modify-write
in normal production encoding. The focused test enabled the flag around its
existing non-zero-reuse assertion. The canonical exact-VBP stream remained
byte-identical.

The first alternating twelve-pair screen appeared promising: wall time fell
`3.839%` with 9/12 wins, while total child CPU changed only `+0.064%`. Two
required repeats did not reproduce it. Wall changed `-0.011%` and `+0.077%`;
total child CPU increased `0.294%` and `0.384%`, with only 5/12 and 4/12 CPU
wins. The initial wall result was scheduling noise, and the production effect
does not clear the measurement floor. The source and test changes were
removed. Keep the counters until a broader stats redesign removes them as
part of another measured win.

## Unit 379 — reject low-temporal-variance intra suppression

The exact-tree path already computes libvpx's `force_skip_low_temp_var`
signal, but rvp9's final intra fallback did not apply the corresponding outer
gate from `vp9_pickmode.c:2519-2523`. Temporary process-wide counters measured
the canonical 120-frame exact-VBP point before changing behavior. Of 116,529
leaves that passed the existing outer RD threshold, 8,573 matched the
low-temporal-variance gate. The fallback evaluated 177,088 intra modes after
146,749 adaptive-threshold prunes and produced 49,221 intra winners. The
source-faithful gate would suppress 502 of those winners.

Applying the complete low-temporal-variance gate reduced median total child
CPU by `2.673%` with 11/12 wins. It was not quality-neutral: the 2 Mbps stream
moved from 983,226 bytes / 37.669123 dB luma to 983,422 bytes / 37.654601 dB.
The gate is therefore a useful speed ceiling, not a retainable Pareto change.

A narrower follow-up kept DC and V but skipped H only on the gated 32x32
leaves. The 2 Mbps point looked Pareto-positive in isolation: 980,070 bytes /
37.676317 dB luma, and two alternating twelve-pair screens reduced total child
CPU by `0.746%` and `0.544%`. The required seven-point curve rejected that
single-point result. Across 750-4,000 kbps the H-only candidate regressed
BD-rate by `+0.447767%` relative to Unit 372, consuming almost the entire final
parity tolerance before comparison with libvpx. Exact-tree Foreman at 100,
250, and 500 kbps stayed byte-identical, so it did not offset the synthetic
curve regression.

All diagnostic and behavioral source changes were removed. Do not retry a
blanket low-temporal-variance intra gate or infer curve efficiency from the
2 Mbps point. Any future intra shortcut must preserve the full curve and
should target the coefficient work of non-winning candidates rather than
removing directional winners.

## Unit 380 — reconstruct intra fallback in place

Every non-skipped intra-fallback candidate built its prediction in one 4 KiB
stack buffer, copied it into a second 4 KiB reconstruction buffer, and then
ran the transform round trip. The round-trip contract already required the
reconstruction buffer to start as an exact prediction copy because the inverse
kernels add residuals in place. The retained change builds intra prediction
directly in that reconstruction buffer and makes reconstructing calls read
their residual prediction from the same initial buffer. Non-reconstructing
diagnostic calls continue to read the separate prediction argument.

Two more general representations were rejected while isolating the change. A
runtime enum selecting separate versus in-place prediction increased total
child CPU by `0.238%`; const-generic specialization increased it by `0.805%`.
The retained contract-based form adds neither a production branch nor a
second transform-body instantiation.

The canonical exact-VBP CBR stream remains 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
Standard cpu-used 7 VBR remains 738,335 bytes with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.
Two alternating twelve-pair exact-path screens reduce median total child CPU
by `0.233%` and `0.567%`, with 8/12 and 7/12 wins; median wall time falls
`0.320%` and `0.386%`, with 8/12 wins in both.

The focused in-place prediction oracle passes in debug and release modes, and
release all-target core clippy passes with warnings denied. The complete
release-mode core test run passed 1,625/1,626 tests; the sole failure is the
pre-existing `sub_pixel_search_unsupported_block_size_panics_in_debug` test,
which correctly does not panic in a release build. rvp9-decoder, pinned
libvpx vpxdec, and ffmpeg decode the exact stream to identical 162,201,600-byte
I420 output, SHA-256
`f12ccfafd437c8778bd0c10380b1f80d01c3582c1455e0de195cf43815c65db9`.

## Unit 381 — reuse large-block chroma skip predictions

The large-block AcDc skip probe already constructs U and V motion-compensated
predictions before the UV model-RD path. When either plane rejected the early
exit, the picker discarded those pixels and immediately constructed them
again for model-RD. The retained change writes the probe into the existing
per-worker chroma scratch and returns a two-bit readiness mask. The UV path
reuses every completed plane and builds only a plane that the original
U-first early exit did not reach.

The first candidate always tested both planes so both predictions would be
available. That changed the original early-exit work and regressed total child
CPU by `1.995%` with only 1/12 wins. The corrected form returns immediately
when U fails and reports only U ready; when V fails, or both planes pass, it
reports both ready. The focused oracle covers all three outcomes and proves
that the unvisited V scratch remains untouched after a U rejection.

Three quiet-host alternating twelve-pair exact-path screens against Unit 380
reduce median total child CPU by `0.690%`, `0.247%`, and `0.258%`, with 8/12,
7/12, and 9/12 wins. Median wall deltas are `+0.064%`, `+0.449%`, and
`-1.753%`; treat wall as flat at this sample length. The canonical exact-VBP
CBR stream remains 983,226 bytes with SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
Standard cpu-used 7 VBR remains 738,335 bytes with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

The complete debug core suite passes 1,626 unit tests, three frame-allocation
tests, and the compile-fail doctest. The focused release test, release
all-target core clippy with warnings denied, formatting, and diff checks also
pass. Byte identity with Unit 380 makes its already-proven cross-decoder
output apply unchanged.

## Unit 382 — reuse reconstruction coefficient scratch

The fresh Unit 381 exact-path profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit381-exactvbp-profile.json.gz`, with symbols in its adjacent
sidecar. On the tile workers, `_platform_memset` accounts for 671 of 11,043
self samples (`6.08%`). Most samples come from `reconstruct_via_round_trip`,
where every reconstruction tile initialized full 1,024-element coefficient,
quantized-coefficient, and dequantized-coefficient arrays before using only
the active transform prefix.

The retained change moves the four round-trip buffers into the existing
per-worker candidate scratch. The forward transform overwrites the active
coefficient prefix, and both quantizers already clear and overwrite their
active output prefixes. After quantization the coefficient buffer is dead, so
the inverse path reuses it for widened dequantized coefficients instead of
initializing another transform-sized stack array. The intra fallback borrows
the same scratch after the inter-candidate loop releases it. No unsafe code is
introduced.

Two quiet-host alternating twelve-pair screens against Unit 381 reduce median
wall time by `6.384%` and `6.833%`, and total child CPU by `6.838%` and

`1.7231x` total CPU, down from Unit 380's `1.8250x` wall and `1.8568x` total

Both product streams remain byte-identical. Exact-VBP CBR is 983,226 bytes,
SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`;

`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.
The reconstruction oracle starts all reusable coefficient buffers with poison
and proves that the result and pixels match clean scratch. The complete debug

## Unit 384 — hoist partition-histogram environment lookup

The Unit 383 profile is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit383-exactvbp-profile.json.gz`, with symbols in its adjacent

read the diagnostic-only `RVP9_PART_HIST` environment variable after every

`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

## Unit 385 — reuse intra-emission transform scratch

The exact-tree phase counter records 144,958 final leaves across the canonical
120-frame point. Aggregate worker time is 204.55 ms in final mode picking,

intra-winning emission path amplified avoidable work: every transform created

qcoeff, dqcoeff, widened-qcoeff, and widened-dqcoeff vectors.

The retained change uses the existing tile-worker residual/quant scratch for
intra-in-inter emission. Hybrid transforms overwrite the active coefficient
prefix directly, quantization overwrites the active qcoeff/dqcoeff prefixes,

the qcoeff vector retained by the frame coefficient source remains allocated.

hybrid type and proves the active output is independent of prior scratch.

total child CPU. This is a material improvement but the final `1.05x` speed
gate remains open.

`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.
Standard cpu-used 7 VBR remains 738,335 bytes with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

candidate traversal and returns both results together. The original candidate
API remains available as a wrapper, so decoder and external callers keep the
same contract.

`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`.

`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

## Unit 388 — reject lean VBP output and disabled candidate-trace gating

## Unit 389 — reject full-pixel start-SAD handoff

`run_newmv_search` measures SAD for the nearest/near predictor seeds and, when
available, the superblock int-pro seed before choosing the full-pixel search
start. Both full-pixel search implementations then measure that winning start
again. Libvpx passes an existing `start_mv_sad` into its wrapper, so a candidate
threaded the raw SAD through whenever bounds clamping left the selected seed
unchanged. Differential coverage proved the supplied and locally measured SAD
produce identical normal- and fast-diamond results.

The candidate preserved the canonical 983,226-byte exact-VBP CBR stream with
SHA-256
`efe991edf3dd32934037a921fa0ef3c18977aa76632236aa8d4100503213d220`, but
the optional-value plumbing cost more than the redundant SAD saved. Two
alternating twelve-pair screens against Unit 387 changed median total child CPU
by `+0.154%` and `+0.471%`, and wall time by `+0.229%` and `+0.174%`. The
complete source and test change was removed. Unit 387 remains the clean
incumbent; do not revisit this as an API-field micro-optimization.

## Unit 390 — restore libvpx's speed-tiered filter-search gates

The rvp9 speed-feature dispatcher only enabled `cb_pred_filter_search` for
cpu-used 6 above 1280×720. Pinned libvpx v1.14.1 progressively lowers that
resolution threshold: speed 5/6 above 1280×720, speed 7 above 640×480, and
speed 8 above 352×288 (`vp9_speed_features.c:658,742,800`). The stale rvp9
gate therefore searched interpolation filters on every fractional candidate
at the canonical 1280×704 cpu-used 7 point, doing more mode-decision work than
the reference.

The retained dispatcher follows all three ordered libvpx thresholds and adds
boundary coverage for cpu-used 6, 7, and 8. Two alternating twelve-pair
exact-path screens against Unit 387 reduce median total child CPU by `0.375%`
and `0.768%`, and wall time by `1.033%` and `0.696%`. The second screen wins
all twelve CPU and wall pairs.

This is also a quality win on the canonical exact-VBP CBR point. Output falls
from 983,226 to 982,894 bytes while luma PSNR rises from `37.669123` to
`37.778322` dB and average YUV PSNR rises from `36.998041` to `37.057764` dB.
The new stream SHA-256 is
`b22a0973eaedd7f3abf39c5005ee8b5203e02e8433520526e1f9ea77106d9a8a`.
Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg produce identical raw I420 with
SHA-256
`4ee2a44b6eb7f5dbb59880b2285dc4eee3164f2dae0548c9f8838d47ee7c8fad`.
The standard cpu-used 7 VBR product remains byte-identical at 738,335 bytes
with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.

The full debug core suite passes 1,626 unit tests, three allocation tests, and
the compile-fail doctest. Four-tile exact-VBP-history determinism, release

checks pass. Retain the corrected source-parity gate.

## Unit 391 — reject flattened retained-coefficient replay

The Unit 390 profile is `/tmp/rvp9-unit390-exactvbp-profile.json.gz`, with
symbols in its adjacent sidecar. Retained coefficient replay is the largest
final-packing body. Its nested outer/zero-run loop reloads the first token and
probability row of each nonzero group. A candidate replaced that loop with one
linear token walk and an explicit outer-start state, preserving the retained
format and arithmetic grammar.

The existing retained-token probability-change and block-pass differentials
passed, and the candidate preserved Unit 390's exact 982,894-byte stream with
SHA-256
`b22a0973eaedd7f3abf39c5005ee8b5203e02e8433520526e1f9ea77106d9a8a`.
It was nevertheless materially slower. Two alternating twelve-pair screens
regressed median total child CPU by `1.877%` and `2.090%`, and wall time by
`1.355%` and `2.317%`. The nested loop likely gives the compiler or branch
predictor a better hot zero-run path than the explicit state branch. The
complete source change was removed; retain Unit 390.

## Unit 392 — reject paired MV-list early exits

The fused LAST/GOLDEN motion-candidate walk continued probing spatial
neighbours after both two-entry candidate lists were complete. A candidate
stopped the matching-reference pass once both nearest positions had been
visited and both lists were full, skipped the different-reference pass when
both lists were already full, and stopped that fallback pass on completion.
A focused lookup-count oracle proved the full-first-two-neighbour case used
two lookups instead of eight, while the existing four-query differential
proved identical candidates, constant-motion flags, and mode context.

The candidate preserved Unit 390's exact 982,894-byte stream with SHA-256
`b22a0973eaedd7f3abf39c5005ee8b5203e02e8433520526e1f9ea77106d9a8a`,
but the removed lookups did not produce a repeatable speed gain. Two
alternating twelve-pair screens changed median total child CPU by `+0.801%`
and `-0.365%`; wall time changed by `-0.023%` and `+0.516%`. The branch cost
and rarity of both lists filling early likely cancel the saved lookups. The
complete source and test change was removed; retain Unit 390 and do not
revisit this as another local branch variant.

`b22a0973eaedd7f3abf39c5005ee8b5203e02e8433520526e1f9ea77106d9a8a`;

## Unit 395 — fuse adjacent horizontal 16-tap NEON filtering

The Unit 393 exact-path profile attributes `1.90%` self time to the AArch64
horizontal 16-tap loop filter. Although the loop-filter caller selects the
dual dispatch slot for adjacent mask bits, rvp9's dual implementation called
the eight-lane single-edge kernel twice. Pinned libvpx v1.14.1 instead loads
both adjacent edges and filters all sixteen lanes together
(`vpx_dsp/arm/loopfilter_neon.c:vpx_lpf_horizontal_16_dual_neon`).

The retained kernel widens the masks and narrow filter to sixteen NEON lanes,
while keeping two widened accumulators for the seven- and fifteen-tap sums.
A manual optimized kernel diagnostic measured the horizontal dual path at
`0.5185x` the two-single runtime. The analogous fused vertical transpose was
`1.1900x` and was removed; vertical dual filtering remains two singles.

Six alternating twelve-pair exact-path screens against Unit 393 reduce median
total child CPU by `0.862%`, `1.666%`, `1.022%`, `0.961%`, `0.204%`, and
`0.696%`. Each screen has 7–11 wins out of 12. Median wall-time changes are
`-1.209%`, `-3.055%`, `-2.605%`, `-2.003%`, `-0.409%`, and `-1.194%`.

The exact-VBP CBR product remains 982,894 bytes with SHA-256
`b22a0973eaedd7f3abf39c5005ee8b5203e02e8433520526e1f9ea77106d9a8a`;
the standard cpu-used 7 VBR product remains 738,335 bytes with SHA-256
`6f8029d6b44af7b215e7ea78333f697322585f30edb303639e2aa6fb542b4f2b`.
Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg produce identical 162,201,600-byte
raw I420 with SHA-256
`4ee2a44b6eb7f5dbb59880b2285dc4eee3164f2dae0548c9f8838d47ee7c8fad`.

The seven focused NEON differentials pass, including randomized single and dual
edges, flat and step edges, and the widened threshold boundary. The complete
rvp9-core library passes 1,627 tests. All-target core clippy with warnings
denied, formatting, and diff checks pass. No divergence-ledger entry is needed
because this restores libvpx's horizontal dual-kernel structure without
changing codec behavior.

## Unit 396 — reject low-resolution exact-VBP production default

The official 320x256 Foreman source used by earlier Stage 4a sweeps is no
longer present locally. A reproducible natural-motion substitute was made by
cropping the checked-in 352x288 profile-1 Foreman source to 320x256,
converting it to 4:2:0, and retaining 60 frames. This is a diagnostic corpus
variant, not a replacement for the missing official gate input.

On that variant, opt-in exact VBP is dramatically faster than the current
production RD descent: twenty alternating pairs measure `0.3077x` total CPU
and `0.3179x` wall. It remains too slow against pinned vpxenc, at `1.5836x`
total CPU and `1.5180x` wall. A candidate made exact VBP the default only for
cpu-used 7 realtime default-content CBR at resolutions no larger than
352x288; its default output was byte-identical to the opt-in path.

The quality gate rejects the promotion. At the 250 kbps target the candidate
is 23,156 bytes and `35.583016 dB` luma PSNR, while the incumbent is slightly
smaller at 22,939 bytes and scores `36.264981 dB`: a `0.681965 dB` loss at
essentially matched rate. A seven-point 75–1,000 kbps diagnostic curve makes
the result unambiguous: exact VBP regresses luma BD-rate by `+15.865829%`
relative to the incumbent and average-YUV BD-rate by `+15.810365%`. Both rvp9
paths happen to beat vpxenc strongly on this substitute clip, so the result
does not explain the missing official Foreman `+3.8327%` product failure.

The source and focused policy test were removed completely. Do not promote
exact VBP by resolution from the historical Foreman result; it does not
generalize even within the Foreman family. Recover the exact official corpus
input before treating its curve as current evidence. The next structural
quality experiment should compare the production RD tree and exact VBP leaf
choices on the same failing official clip, once that input is restored.

## Unit 408 — reuse transform-size decision scratch

Fresh Unit 410 profiling on the canonical 320x256 60-frame CBR clip attributes

`cce48653e85bc791e47e0a874d18832738fa15422621692c6bad31ea6f1d7e51`.

## Unit 419 — reject cached zero-motion candidate repricing

A stream-exact architecture prototype cached the context-independent
prediction, transform, and chroma measurements for LAST zero-motion candidates,
then recomputed the final pass's causal mode, reference, skip, and RD costs.
This is the smallest candidate-level reuse slice: every fresh final picker
evaluates one zero-motion prediction and integer motion fixes its filter to
EightTap, so the expensive measurements do not depend on causal neighbours.

The repricing itself worked. The canonical output remained byte-identical at
SHA-256 `cce48653e85bc791e47e0a874d18832738fa15422621692c6bad31ea6f1d7e51`.
Directly comparing the same cache-bearing binary with reuse disabled versus
enabled showed median total CPU `-0.632%` with 55/60 wins and user CPU
`-0.667%` with 56/60 wins. Evidence is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit419b-reuse-effect.txt`.

However, retaining a complete zero-motion record for every speculative
descent node cost more than reuse saved. The full-payload prototype was
`+0.255%` CPU over 80 pairs despite a roughly 5% lower instrumented final
picker time. Separating a compact record through every candidate return was
worse (`+1.725%` CPU), because it enlarged the hot return path. Deriving the
record only from an already-cached zero-motion descent winner removed all
extra per-node storage but hit too few final leaves and still measured
`+0.578%` CPU over 60 pairs. Evidence is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit419b-paired-speed-80.txt`,
`/tmp/rvp9-unit419c-paired-speed.txt`, and
`/tmp/rvp9-unit419e-paired-speed.txt`.

All source variants were removed. Do not attach candidate payloads to every
descent result or restrict reuse to only the descent winner. A future
candidate-reuse design must retain data only after the partition structure is
known, or otherwise cover enough repeated work without per-speculative-node
copy/storage overhead. The next experiment returns to a measured arithmetic
kernel or removes work inside descent itself.

## Unit 432 — reject cached descent-score reuse

Three exact prototypes tested whether the final 16x16 picker could reuse work from
its speculative descent pass. All preserved the accepted Unit 430 stream, but none
reduced CPU reproducibly.

16x16 leaves below `base_qindex * 100`. Forty alternating pairs regressed median
total child CPU by `+2.6849%` and wall time by `+2.5939%`; it won only 3/40 CPU
pairs. Its archived binary is `/tmp/rvp9-unit432-smooth100-reuse-candidate`.

recomputed chroma, context-dependent rate, and the final argument minimum. Only
about 12–18 of roughly 460 leaves per frame qualified. Sixty alternating pairs
regressed median total child CPU by `+0.593%` and wall time by `+0.537%`.

The third prototype generalized reuse first to one cached integer-pel winner and
then to the complete four-candidate fixed set. The one-winner form was measurement
noise after eighty pairs: total child CPU `+0.0417%`, wall `-0.032%`, and 39/80
CPU wins. The four-candidate form regressed median total child CPU by `+1.2603%`
and wall by `+0.9619%`, with only 20/80 CPU wins. Copying and probing the additional
cached state costs more than recomputing these candidates in the causal context.

All prototype source was removed and the worktree is clean. Do not add more cached
descent state without first proving that a materially larger exact computation can
be reused without copying per-candidate buffers. The next experiment is a
call-site-level split of final-picker scoring and emitted-block work from the fresh
Unit 430 production profile, `/tmp/rvp9-unit430-canonical-foreman-default-cbr-profile20.json.gz`.

## Unit 433 — prune losing transform-size candidates exactly

Fresh production instrumentation split the canonical CPU7 CBR inter-frame work

`/tmp/rvp9-unit430-rt-emit-profile.txt`.

CPU with 60/60 wins. It was not safe to promote. Foreman regressed `+2.109842%`
luma BD-rate relative to Unit 430, Mandelbrot regressed `+9.798900%`, and
testsrc2 crossed the final reference gate at `+0.771522%` versus pinned vpxenc.
Noise was non-monotonic and remains diagnostic-only. Evidence is
`/tmp/rvp9-unit433-*-no-emit-tx-rd-curve.json`; no source change was retained.

The retained change instead applies an exact lower-bound test inside the full
transform-size search. Rate, transform distortion, and the remaining tile
contributions are non-negative. Once a candidate's partial RD cost, including
its fixed transform-size signaling cost, reaches the best complete candidate,
the unevaluated tiles cannot recover under the strict argmin and are skipped.
The first largest transform remains exhaustive because no prior best exists.

resolved report is `/tmp/rvp9-unit434-profile-analysis.txt`. Internal phase

search, `10.44%` to candidate evaluation, and `10.33%` to emit-side luma TX

A temporary patched-libvpx F.0.2 oracle build at the pinned
`12f3a2ac603e8f10742105519e0cd03c3b8f71dd` revision compared the 256x256
crop, 60 frames, CPU7 CBR 250 kbps. Rvp9 emitted 18,265 leaves and evaluated
46,520 LAST candidates; libvpx emitted 31,887 leaves and evaluated 105,397
LAST candidates. Rvp9 therefore performs materially fewer mode candidates,

## Unit 446 — correct CPU6's NSTEP full-pixel search

Pinned libvpx CPU6 does not use one multiscale diamond walk. Its NSTEP wrapper
runs progressively smaller starts at step parameters 6 through 10, ranks the
winners with variance plus MV cost, and performs an eight-move unit refinement.
The candidate in `crates/rvp9-core/src/mv_search/full_pixel.rs` ports that
wrapper and its `num00` redundant-restart suppression; CPU7/8 remain on
FAST_DIAMOND. `crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/inter.rs::run_newmv_search`
now dispatches the typed NSTEP policy to the faithful wrapper.

The final CPU6 seven-point VBR results versus pinned vpxenc are:

- Foreman: luma `-2.715157%`, average `-1.571265%`.
- testsrc2: luma `+4.125957%`, average `+10.208160%`.
- Mandelbrot: luma `+1.042557%`, average `+21.926043%`.

Compared with the accepted pre-unit baseline, this recovers about 6.2 BD-rate
points on Foreman and 2.0 points on Mandelbrot while leaving testsrc2 luma
effectively flat. Evidence is `/tmp/rvp9-unit464-cpu6-nstep-num00-*.json`.
Libvpx's `num00` skipping reduced the large-testsrc timing cost from the first
faithful candidate's `+10.352%` to `+6.199%` total child CPU versus the prior
rvp9 CPU6 binary (12 alternating pairs, two 120-frame encodes per sample).
This is not a finished Pareto result: it stays only as the measured
rate-distortion prerequisite for the next CPU6 search-kernel optimisation.
