## Unit 447 — native 720p corpus invalidates the CPU7 green claim

The synthetic `testsrc_1280x704` speed field is not a sufficient quality
corpus. A bicubic 1280x704 Foreman diagnostic first exposed a smooth-motion
failure: default CPU7 measured about `+226%` luma BD-rate. Disabling the three
large-frame shortcuts recovered most of that catastrophic loss but still left
about `+46%`; the main shortcut defect was unconditional reuse of an entire
speculative descent pick. At a representative point, reused decisions coded
NEWMV over `72.9%` of inter area versus libvpx's `20.1%`.

Native 60-frame 1280x704 crops from the repository-declared Xiph corpus then
confirmed that the problem is content-dependent rather than only an upscale
artifact. CPU7 VBR luma BD-rate versus pinned vpxenc was:

- `in_to_tree`: `+129.736130%` (`1.46219 dB` curve overlap).
- `ducks_take_off`: `-28.928665%` (`3.45685 dB` overlap).
- `old_town_cross`: `+131.439608%` (`1.61582 dB` overlap).

Evidence is `/tmp/rvp9-unit462-cpu7-native-*-base.json`. Rvp9 severely
underspends the target on the two failing clips; at the same time, the wide
content split proves that a global bitrate-model multiplier cannot be the
production fix. Unit 444 remains valid evidence for its exact small gate and
synthetic speed field, but its statement that Stage 4a is focused-green is
superseded: CPU7 is not corpus-green.

Rejected large-frame remedies were a global VBR bits-per-MB sweep, enabling
the dormant golden-frame allocator, disabling intra fallback, disabling all
large-frame shortcuts, causal-context guarding of cached decisions, skip-only
cache reuse, unconditional cached-MV reuse followed by a causal repick, and
NEWMV-to-causal-mode rewrites/snapping. Full causal repicking recovers several
dB on upscaled Foreman but measures about `1.643x` pinned vpxenc total CPU;
the cheap gates either miss most of the quality loss or regress the three
native curves. No large-frame policy change remains in the source.

Exact next experiment: keep CPU7's accepted fast default while profile-guided
work replaces whole speculative-pick reuse with a cheap causal re-evaluation,
or makes the full final picker fast enough. Judge every candidate first on the
three native Xiph curves plus the existing Foreman/testsrc2/Mandelbrot set;
then rerun the official Stage 4a gate and warmed CPU7 speed series. For CPU6,
profile the now-faithful NSTEP path and remove measured duplicate SAD/variance
work without changing its selected motion vector.

## Units 448–494 — native corpus exposes mode/skip gap; retain reference VBR stack as opt-in

Fresh 60-frame native-resolution CPU7 VBR curves at commit `34bb5a9` confirmed
the broad gap from Unit 447: `in_to_tree +129.736130%`,
`ducks_take_off -28.928665%`, and `old_town_cross +131.439608%` luma BD-rate.
Exact variance-based partitioning reduced the failing clips to
`+67.616%/+105.583%`, but its tree search was roughly 50% slower. Full emitted
transform RD improved those exact-tree results further to
`+60.627%/-24.105%/+100.404%`; removing TX4 made that path 8.128% faster over
12/12 pairs but worsened both failing clips, so neither transform variant was
retained. A 15-frame GOLDEN cadence, forced 16x16 maximum transforms, and
disabling intra fallback all regressed the three-clip screen and were removed.

Temporary E8 tracing in both encoders found two rate-control mismatches. Rvp9
used a deliberate 4x VBR bits-per-MB prior, while pinned libvpx uses 1x.
Libvpx also schedules one-pass GOLDEN refreshes from frame rate and resolution:
10 frames at 30 fps and 11 at the native clips' 50 fps and at 60 fps. Boosted
frames use the independent `GF_ARF_STD` correction slot and the compiled
1.75x-rate top-Q clamp. With all four details matched, rvp9's keyframe Q became
93 like vpxenc and the exact-tree native curves improved to
`+45.707%/+5.379%/+83.762%`. Full transform RD reached
`+39.024%/+6.488%/+75.484%` but remained too slow.

An E1 decision trace at 1500 kbps then showed the remaining causal mismatch.
Average inter spend was close (`31,466` versus `32,097` bits), but rvp9 used
intra on 4.4% of blocks versus 0.4%, NEWMV on 33.3% versus 45.5%, and skip on
59.2% versus 83.1%. Reference allocation is therefore no longer the leading
exact-tree hypothesis; inter-mode, residual, and skip decisions are.

The source-aligned allocator cannot yet be the production default. On the

production result `-8.534253%` to `+20.131756%` luma BD-rate. With the dynamic
interval active, isolation gave `-8.974944%` with multiplier 4 and GOLDEN RC
off, `+5.469915%` with multiplier 4 and GOLDEN RC on, and `+12.335849%` with
multiplier 1 and GOLDEN RC off.
On native `in_to_tree`, those cases measured `+132.250910%`, `+132.643388%`,
and `+206.545309%`. The exact libvpx choices compensate for libvpx's coding
distribution, not rvp9's current one.

The retained green unit keeps production defaults unchanged: multiplier 4,
fixed eight-frame GOLDEN cadence, and GOLDEN refreshes classified as ordinary
inter for rate allocation. `RVP9_BPM_MULTIPLIER=1 RVP9_VBR_GF_RC=1` now enables
the complete pinned-reference path for controlled diagnostics. Focused coverage
checks the 30/50/60 fps interval formula, custom GOP cadence, independent
`GF_ARF_STD` slot, and 1.75x GOLDEN top-Q bound. The clean release build passes
118 rate-control tests (one diagnostic ignored) and all nine GOP tests.

## Unit 497 — fixed-q block oracle isolates mode, skip, and coefficient-rate gaps

The F.0.2 per-block oracle compared rvp9 with the instrumented pinned libvpx
encoder at fixed qindex 120 on 64 frames of 256x256 Foreman. The strict run is
`target/track_f_oracle/unit497/run_6a6f07a4`; it contains 33,898 rvp9 records
and 36,828 libvpx records. The different partition histories mean a strict
whole-record match is not expected, so the useful diagnostic is the 27,669
shared `(frame, mi_row, mi_col)` keys and the 22,446 keys that also share block
size.

Rvp9 selects intra for 4,461 records versus libvpx's 1,011, and marks 11,727
records skipped versus libvpx's 18,381. Rvp9 selects NEARESTMV/NEARMV/NEWMV
12,582/3,094/11,305 times; libvpx selects them 17,755/5,807/11,204 times.
Among same-size shared candidates, rvp9's median luma coefficient-rate ratios
are `1.897x` for ZEROMV, `2.132x` for NEARESTMV, `1.952x` for NEARMV, and
`2.549x` for NEWMV. Median distortion ratios stay near one
(`0.965x`–`1.061x`).

The oracle also exposed an exact `1.5x` RD-multiplier departure: rvp9 uses
96,900 while libvpx uses 64,600 at qindex 120. This is the deliberate realtime
natural-content lambda calibration in
`crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/inter.rs::lambda_atten`, not a newly found
arithmetic bug. Candidate motion vectors and causal references still diverge,
so the coefficient-rate ratios do not yet prove a transform primitive defect.

`RVP9_LA=0` disables the deliberate realtime lambda attenuation and restores

`in_to_tree`/`ducks_take_off`/`old_town_cross`.

The production small curves also improve: Foreman moves from `-8.53425%` to

generalise, however. It moves from
`+129.736%/-28.929%/+131.440%` to
`+135.627%/-30.096%/+133.743%`; both important failing clips regress.
The global lambda change is therefore rejected and no source change remains.

## Unit 502 — exact-tree cost is the causal final picker

A 60-frame CPU7 profile on native 1280x704 `in_to_tree` separates the two
paths cleanly. Production consumed 246.03 ms of aggregate encoder-worker time:
103.34 ms in descent, 121.60 ms in emission, and no final-pick time. The exact
tree consumed 514.77 ms: 343.02 ms in the final picker, 121.48 ms in emission,
and no descent-pick time. Its 86,025 leaves are 1.657x production's 51,920.
The final picker is therefore the complete incremental cost; emission is
unchanged. Profiles are `/tmp/rvp9-unit502-{prod,exact}-profile.log`.

This rules out emission as the next speed target. Exact-tree speed requires
fewer committed leaves, cheaper causal leaf decisions, or a design that reuses
only decision state whose contexts remain valid after the tree is committed.
Earlier full-candidate caches lost their saved repricing time to speculative
storage and copying, so repeating that representation is not useful.

## Unit 503 — fixed-q exact tree has equal quality but 45.7% excess payload

The F.0.2 oracle reran 64-frame 256x256 Foreman at qindex 120 with
`RVP9_EXACT_VBP_TREE=1 RVP9_LA=0`. The artifact is
`target/track_f_oracle/unit503/run_6a6f09ec`. Source lambda now agrees exactly
at 64,600, but rvp9 still emits 119,835 bytes against libvpx's 82,270 bytes,
a 45.7% excess. Aggregate luma PSNR is effectively equal: 37.53363 dB for
rvp9 and 37.51622 dB for libvpx, a +0.017 dB rvp9 difference. The cropped
source and PSNR logs are `/tmp/rvp9-unit503-*`.

Excluding the keyframe, rvp9 has 25,704 leaf decisions versus libvpx's 36,828,
with 21,308 shared same-size positions. Rvp9 records only 7,528 final skips
versus libvpx's 18,381. On shared same-size candidate probes, its median luma
rate remains 1.98x/2.23x/2.00x/2.60x for ZERO/NEAREST/NEAR/NEW. Full-skip
state also diverges sharply: rvp9 reports no full skip while libvpx reports
AC/DC skip on 2,045/6,429/1,229/7,045 probes for those modes. Final shared
decisions include 5,841 rvp9-nonskip/libvpx-skip mismatches.

Direct model-RD and block-YRD oracles already agree exactly when both encoders
receive identical inputs. The fixed-q result therefore confirms that the
excess bits come from the coupled partition, prediction, and motion field—not
from a low-level transform or entropy primitive. Retuning a primitive from
these already-diverged live candidates would hide the cause.

## Unit 505 — product VBP trace reaches the reconstructed keyframe

A temporary product-path trace compared three native `in_to_tree` frames with
the pinned libvpx VBP oracle. The single-thread run has 428 common fresh-tree
records and identical source hashes throughout. On frame 1, qindex agrees on
all 220 records and the first three partition thresholds agree, but the
selected reference and MV agree on only 140. Predictor hashes disagree on all
220 records, including positions whose reference and MV agree. Frame 2 also
has different qindex and predictor hashes on all 208 common records.

The first frame-1 superblock record demonstrates the causal split. Both use
qindex 186, but rvp9 selects LAST `(232,-192)` while libvpx selects LAST
`(248,256)`, and their predictor hashes differ. More importantly, matching
reference/MV records still have different predictors because the reconstructed
keyframe is already different. The trace instrumentation was removed. Saved
evidence is `/tmp/rvp9-unit505-rvp9-vbp-t1.log` and
`/tmp/rvp9-unit505-libvpx-vbp-t1.jsonl`.

The block-statistics harness now reports keyframe partition counts, partition
area, and area-weighted luma modes. On Unit 503's fixed-qindex streams, rvp9's
keyframe is 95.3% 16x16 and 4.7% 32x32. Libvpx is 35.4% 4x4, 52.1% 8x8,
7.8% 16x16, and 4.7% 32x32. Rvp9 uses only DC/V/H; libvpx also uses every
directional mode and TM. Rvp9 spends nearly the same keyframe payload
(`35,648` versus `35,368` bits) but produces 37.42 dB versus libvpx's
38.03 dB luma PSNR. The keyframe is therefore a measured source of the causal
reference-field divergence, not merely a downstream symptom.

## Units 506–507 — 8x8 keyframe leaves recover quality but fail rate control

Temporarily allowing the existing keyframe partitioner to split 16x16 blocks

Its luma PSNR rose from 37.42 dB to 38.04 dB, matching libvpx's 38.03 dB.

cannot express libvpx's 8x8-to-four-4x4 partition and per-subblock BMI modes,
so it buys the recovered prediction quality with too many 8x8 mode symbols.

`+43.8142%/+7.42436%/+89.4340%`. The patch was removed. Reports are

## Unit 510 — sub-8 picker resolves causal mode costs internally

The standalone full-ten-mode sub-8 keyframe picker previously accepted four
pre-resolved mode-cost rows. That contract could not represent libvpx: BMI 1
uses BMI 0 as its left-mode context, BMI 2 uses BMI 0 above, and BMI 3 uses
BMI 1 above plus BMI 2 left. The caller cannot know those winners before the
picker runs.

`PickIntraSub8x8Params` now carries the full keyframe luma mode-cost table and
the neighbouring blocks' four BMI modes. The raster walk resolves external
contexts from above BMI 2/3 and left BMI 1/3, then resolves internal contexts
from the earlier winners exactly like pinned libvpx
`vp9_above_block_mode`/`vp9_left_block_mode`. A focused test covers all four
contexts and unavailable-neighbour DC fallback. All 554 active encoder
library tests pass (one diagnostic ignored), as do encoder all-target clippy
with warnings denied and rustfmt.

Exact next experiment: add a diagnostic keyframe partition path that can
stamp a high-variance 8x8 cell as Block4x4 without changing production. Then
wire those leaves to this picker in the live causal simulator and require
whole-stream agreement under rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg before
running the fixed-q keyframe comparison.

## Unit 513 — live subblock coefficient contexts improve the reference chain

Pinned `rd_pick_intra4x4block` receives pointers into the live tile above/left
coefficient contexts. Each winning 4x4 transform writes its EOB flag back, so
later BMI blocks and later leaves price their first coefficient token with the
same causal state. Rvp9 had hard-coded context zero.

The diagnostic keyframe walk now owns one `TileCoefCtx` per tile, seeds each
sub-8 pick from its two external luma contexts, updates the two local context
arrays after every BMI winner, and commits the actual simulator EOB flags for
the next leaf. The path remains behind `RVP9_EXACT_KF_SUB8=1`; production does
not allocate or update these diagnostic contexts. Focused tests prove that
contexts 0 and 2 produce different token costs and that four zero-EOB winners
starting from non-zero boundaries consume contexts `[2, 1, 1, 0]`.

At fixed qindex 120, the first keyframe grows from 35,416 to 36,216 bits while
luma PSNR rises from 38.16 to 38.31 dB; pinned libvpx is 35,368 bits and 38.03
dB. The 64-frame stream shrinks from 124,458 to 115,241 bytes, showing that the
cleaner keyframe reduces downstream inter cost. Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec,
and ffmpeg all produce the same 6,291,456-byte I420 output with SHA-256
`088d72b3a7949f0429e17c8d1406ae5e0716fe9b0cff137e4402057b314fe2ef`.

The native CPU7 luma BD-rates are now
`+39.313659%/+6.701459%/+76.876911%` on
`in_to_tree`/`ducks_take_off`/`old_town_cross`. Against Unit 512, live contexts
improve the first two clips by 0.255 and 0.241 points but regress old town by
0.503 points. Against the no-keyframe-descent exact baseline, the sub-8 stack
still improves in-tree and old town while regressing ducks by 2.47 points. It
therefore remains a measured diagnostic prerequisite, not a production
default.

## Unit 518 — standalone Tx8 top-right extension corrects the next D63 decision

The Unit 517 diagnosis was wrong: the 8x8 TM leaf at `(112,8)` already
received different causal left pixels. Its transform was downstream, not the
first cause. The first differing larger leaf is Block8x8 at `(104,8)`. Both
encoders receive the same source, qindex 119, coefficient context 2, RD
multiplier 65,430, top pixels `[181,181,181,181,184,186,188,189]`, left
pixels `[187,197,158,142,195,140,137,187]`, and keyframe mode-cost row.

Rvp9 previously copied 16 raw pixels from the reconstruction buffer. The
eight top-right pixels were still zero because a standalone 8x8 leaf contains
one Tx8 and no transform to its right has been reconstructed. Libvpx's
`vp9_predict_intra_block` recognizes that availability shape and repeats the
last causal top pixel. Rvp9's D63 prediction consumed the zeroes, produced
spurious 95/47-valued pixels, and lost to V. The V candidate itself already
matched libvpx exactly.

The exact Block8 caller now copies the eight causal top pixels and fills the
remaining eight slots with the last one. The corrected live D63 candidate and
winner match pinned libvpx exactly: coefficient rate 31,315, total rate
34,834, pixel distortion 15,072, and RD 6,380,756. A focused test pins those
values and all 64 reconstructed pixels. The native-50fps paired small-block
trace then agrees for calls 0 through 799 across source, coefficient context,
mode-cost row, winner, rates, distortion, RD, and reconstruction. At call 800
the encoders enter different partition regions, so the next cause is again in
the larger partition walk rather than 4x4 coefficient pricing.

Fresh timing configuration checks found that the earlier native screens used
the Xiph inputs' declared 50fps rate-control timing while reporting bitrate as
if they were the scoped 30fps target. Multiplying reported bitrate alone does
not repair that evidence because frame rate changes rate-control decisions.
All native acceptance measurements must pass `--fps=30/1` explicitly to both
encoders.

With both legs explicitly matched at 30fps, the fresh pinned-vpxenc luma
BD-rates are `+41.931593%/-1.262049%/+98.190423%`; average-YUV BD-rates are
`+38.611595%/-0.475956%/+89.517771%` on
`in_to_tree`/`ducks_take_off`/`old_town_cross`. Versus a clean Unit 517 binary,
the luma movements are `-0.485067/+0.032045/+0.311801` points and average-YUV

## Unit 520 — exact keyframe variance tree matches all partition nodes

At qindex 83, the first divergent 32x32 source node has 4x4-average
accumulators `sum=3456`, `sum_squares=186750`, and residual 126 over 64
samples. Libvpx retains its 256x variance scale and compares `504 > 450`, so
it splits. Rvp9 divided both operands by 256 and compared `1 > 1`, so it did
not. The exact keyframe path now retains the native fixed-point scale.

Two adjacent libvpx rules were required to make the tree coherent: keyframe
roots always split, and a high-variance 16x16 child propagates a force flag to
its 32x32 parent. That prepass exposed an older indexing bug: the flags were
stored in libvpx's quadrant-major order but looked up as a 4x4 raster. The
lookup now maps `(row,col)` through its 32x32 quadrant and local child index.
Focused tests pin the fractional split boundary, mandatory root split, child
propagation, and quadrant-major lookup.

On the explicit-30fps `in_to_tree` 1000 kbps keyframe, rvp9 and pinned libvpx
now visit the same 16,092 partition nodes across all 220 superblocks with

64x64 `220 SPLIT`; 32x32 `842 SPLIT/38 NONE`; 16x16
`2906 SPLIT/462 NONE`; 8x8 `2569 SPLIT/9055 NONE`.

## Unit 523 — keyframe coefficients, skip state, and loop filter align

The source-aligned `in_to_tree` keyframe now matches pinned libvpx through the
complete decoded reconstruction. All 12,124 leaf records match in block size,
skip context/value, transform size, luma mode, and chroma mode. All 43,704
emitted transform blocks match in plane, position, transform size, EOB, and
dequantized-coefficient hash.

The remaining pre-filter match exposed two production differences. Rvp9 did
not promote an intra leaf to `skip=true` when every Y/U/V transform had EOB
zero, and the keyframe writer did not clear coefficient contexts after a skip
leaf. The encoder now records the post-encode all-zero result on each leaf,
splats it into both writer and loop-filter MI grids, and reuses the existing
decoder-faithful skip-context reset. The F.0.2 decision oracle is recorded
after residual generation so its skip and EOB fields describe emitted syntax.

Pre-filter I420 then became bit-exact at SHA-256
`6cc0760e21dbbadae1f9ad8bd6fa5db03632bf8f700d110cf8b79bc824f15d05`.
Post-filter output still differed because rvp9 disabled mode/reference loop
filter deltas while libvpx enabled its keyframe defaults. Keyframes now signal
and apply `[1, 0, -1, -1]`; inter frames retain that state without re-sending
unchanged values. The final one-frame I420 is bit-exact at SHA-256
`15919afdad5601969f6b3a8fdd67ef46ac5599d7988f5251cfdf3b9e5dd97200`.

The corrected six-point explicit-30fps CPU7 VBR screen improves all three
clips. Luma BD-rate versus pinned vpxenc is

`+38.327730%/-0.653580%/+87.912951%` on
`in_to_tree`/`ducks_take_off`/`old_town_cross`. Relative to Unit 522, luma
moves `-0.144105/-0.079826/-0.044912` points and average-YUV moves
`-0.143347/-0.088736/-0.128813` points. The exact keyframe is therefore a

## Unit 526 — VBR Block32 residual pricing matches pinned libvpx

The Unit 525 note's `model skip-transform 2` interpretation was wrong. A
fresh 20,000-record `VPX_F02_MODEL_ORACLE_OUT` capture on pinned libvpx shows
that the matched Block32 uses the ordinary model in VBR: model
rate/distortion `5632/312624`, variance/SSE `18764/19796`, Tx8, skip-transform
none. Libvpx enables `model_rd_for_sb_y_large` only for CBR
(`vp9_pickmode.c:2034-2037`); rvp9 had incorrectly selected it for every
Block32 and Block64 regardless of rate-control mode.

`InterRdCalibration::large_block_model` now carries that rate-control policy.
Realtime CBR retains the per-transform large model and its dequant-squared
thresholds; realtime VBR uses the ordinary zbin-threshold model. Block32 and
larger blocks also stop taking the small-block `model_only`/`model_dist`
shortcut: libvpx's `use_simple_block_yrd` gate is strictly below Block32.
Under the temporary full-int-pro partition diagnostic, the previously matched
NEWMV `(4,4)` EIGHTTAP_SMOOTH candidate now exactly matches libvpx's final
luma `block_yrd` rate/distortion `10240/312787`.

The fresh six-point CPU7 VBR screen improves two clips materially and moves
the third by only five hundredths of a point. Luma BD-rate versus pinned
vpxenc is `+25.358695%/-6.073745%/+47.780757%`; average-YUV is
`+23.805033%/-5.411316%/+43.654200%` on

moves `-1.723242/-0.050540/-0.993962` points and average-YUV moves

## Unit 528 — reject partial high-precision MV syntax

The first traced NEWMV `(4,4)` costs 3,571 units in rvp9 and 4,793 in libvpx.
The 1,222-unit difference is explained by frame precision, not a broken MV
cost table: pinned libvpx enables high-precision MV syntax below qindex 200,
while rvp9's production header keeps the existing `RVP9_HIGHMV` gate off.
Each nonzero component therefore costs one additional high-precision bit in
libvpx. This is a real source departure, but the prior rejection concerned
full eighth-pel search as well as syntax. The narrow experiment enabled only
the existing header/cost gate while retaining rvp9's current adaptive
quarter/half-pel search.

The six-point CPU7 VBR screen rejects that partial change. Relative to Unit
527, luma BD-rate moves `+0.539412/-0.023199/+0.592415` points and average-YUV
moves `+0.577322/-0.013403/+0.528784` points on

`+25.403793%/-5.907084%/+47.687873%`; average-YUV is
`+23.848123%/-5.235457%/+43.571063%`. The unweighted mean regresses by
0.369543 luma points and 0.364234 average-YUV points. Leave high-precision
syntax disabled; its more faithful rate price changes mode selection without
the prediction gain needed to repay those bits.

## Unit 529 — honor per-superblock chroma sensitivity in realtime RD

Pinned libvpx computes `x->color_sensitivity[2]` in `chroma_check` from each
plane's actual inter-prediction SAD relative to `y_sad >> 2`, then excludes an
insensitive plane from prediction and modeled UV RD
(`vp9_pickmode.c:846-905,1173-1207,2377-2392`). Rvp9 already had the matching
real-partition-MV calculation in `partition_color_sensitivity`, but only ran
it when the F02 diagnostic was enabled. Production mode search therefore
modeled both UV planes unconditionally. The first matched Block32 trace showed
the exact consequence: rvp9 added UV `128/58920` with both flags true while
libvpx added `0/0` with both flags false.

Production mode search now computes the per-superblock mask unconditionally,
propagates it through final inter and intra-fallback evaluation, skips
prediction work for each insensitive plane, and excludes that plane from the
UV model. Partition descent remains deliberately luma-only. The new masked
model test covers single-plane and all-plane exclusion; the existing encoder
test pins color sensitivity to the real UV prediction SAD. The CBR-only large
block chroma skip probe still evaluates both planes and remains separate from
this VBR unit.

libvpx selects LAST+NEAREST `(4,4)` with EightTapSmooth. The already-emitted
left neighbour has the same reference, MV, filter, and final skip state in both
streams, so this is a candidate-ranking mismatch rather than a causal wire-grid
mismatch.

## Unit 546 — isolate the first rate-control overspend

The accepted Unit 536 and pinned libvpx keyframes for `in_to_tree` at
1000 kbps decode byte-exactly across all 1,351,680 I420 bytes. Both score
38.55 dB luma / 39.25 dB average PSNR. Their packets are not byte-equal:
rvp9 spends 114,741 bytes and libvpx 108,400 bytes for the same decoded
pixels. The first inter frame is also close at the shared q166: rvp9 scores
36.10 dB luma in 899 bytes versus libvpx 36.20 dB in 666 bytes.

The next frame exposes a rate-control oscillation. Unit 536 chooses q112 and
spends 10,946 bytes; libvpx chooses q205 and spends 527 bytes. Rvp9 gains only
0.83 dB luma on that roughly 20x spend. Its later large packets cluster at the
intended 10-frame golden cadence, but frame 2 is an extra burst. Because the
opening reconstruction is exact, this state mismatch is not inherited from a
weaker reference.

## Units 547–549 — reject libvpx one-pass correction damping

An env-gated trace in a temporary pinned-libvpx build identified the exact
state difference. Libvpx's one-pass path reads the unpopulated
`twopass.gf_group.rf_level[index]` for `damped_adjustment[]`; it remains enum
value zero (`INTER_NORMAL`) on every one-pass frame. The opening keyframe thus
primes the inter damping-history slot. On frame 1, libvpx damps the 3% actual-
to-model correction to a factor of 0.27 and then picks q205. Rvp9 keys damping
by the correction-factor level itself, so its first inter applies the full
correction, collapses the factor to about 0.04, and picks q112. The temporary
libvpx instrumentation was removed; `third_party/libvpx` is clean.

Unit 547 shared the `INTER_NORMAL` damping flag across one-pass frame kinds and
added a focused regression test. It removed the oscillation: frame 2 moved to
q207 and 394 bytes. The full six-point screen nevertheless regressed on every
clip. Luma BD-rate became `+17.805636%/-2.404836%/+40.399591%` and average-YUV
became `+17.039855%/-2.176296%/+38.052107%` on
`in_to_tree`/`ducks_take_off`/`old_town_cross`, versus Unit 536's
`+17.111637%/-6.026639%/+39.518502%` and
`+16.308237%/-5.346707%/+36.880456%`.

Unit 548 also passed `--min-q=0`, matching vpxenc's default instead of rvp9's
default 4. It produced luma `+17.483324%/-1.712734%/+40.691667%` and average-
YUV `+16.648216%/-1.517850%/+38.153607%`, still worse on every clip. Unit 549
additionally ported libvpx's rounded Q-history update
`ROUND_POWER_OF_TWO(3 * avg + q, 2)`. It produced luma
`+17.984679%/-2.433667%/+40.890048%` and average-YUV
`+17.235374%/-2.204630%/+38.501667%`, again all regressions. All source and
test edits were removed; Unit 536 remains accepted.

This rules out the conspicuous frame-2 burst as the primary BD-rate cause. It
is a real control-flow departure, but the burst accidentally compensates for
rvp9's weaker mode decisions. Do not retain the reference-like controller in
isolation. Exact next experiment: stay on frame 1, where q and the reference
pixels already match, and measure the repeated loss behind rvp9's 35% larger,
0.10 dB worse inter packet. Start with candidate/model distortion at the first
divergent Block32 leaves, not another rate-control change.

## Units 550–552 — keyframe coefficient forward updates accepted

The decoder-side Unit 550 decomposition isolated a 50,728-bit keyframe excess
despite byte-exact decoded I420 output and identical partition, luma-mode,
chroma-mode, skip, transform-size, coefficient-token, and EOB-branch counts.
Rvp9 spent only 16 compressed-header bits and 917,768 tile-data bits; pinned
libvpx spent 2,784 header bits and 864,272 tile bits. Libvpx was paying once to
forward-update coefficient probabilities, then recovering far more in tile
coding. Commit `3cbf1b9` makes these keyframe fields visible in
`e1_block_stats`.

Unit 552 extends the keyframe tile writer with optional coefficient counts,
builds the existing libvpx-shaped TWO_LOOP plan before the compressed header,
uses the updated probabilities for tile coding, and retains the forward-
updated bank with `refresh_frame_context=true` and
`frame_parallel_decoding_mode=true`. Commit `ee14574` contains the focused
implementation and regression test. At 1000 kbps the keyframe moved from
917,928/867,200 rvp9/libvpx bits to 871,368/867,200. Its compressed header is
2,688/2,784 bits and its tile data is 868,536/864,272 bits. The remaining
keyframe excess is 4,168 bits, down 91.8%.

The full six-point corpus screen is a reproducible Pareto-quality win. Luma
BD-rate is `+15.867457%/-6.908839%/+38.100897%`; average-YUV is
`+15.073826%/-6.239849%/+35.486752%` on
`in_to_tree`/`ducks_take_off`/`old_town_cross`. Relative to Unit 536, every
clip improves: luma moves `-1.244180/-0.882200/-1.417605` points and
average-YUV moves `-1.234411/-0.893142/-1.393704` points.

The 1000 kbps candidate decodes through rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and
ffmpeg to the same 81,100,800-byte I420 output, SHA-256
`273b6405aabc8c950303e44c713b682246cb75b9e026c9246fcf65a03281eb47`.
The modes-writer slice passes 125 tests; the full encoder library passes 566
tests with one ignored diagnostic; encoder/core all-target clippy passes with
warnings denied; rustfmt and `git diff --check` pass.

Nine warmed alternating runs on `in_to_tree`, 1000 kbps, CPU7, one thread,
and the source-aligned environment measured medians of 0.640287 s for Unit
536, 0.641154 s for Unit 552, and 0.427456 s for pinned vpxenc. Unit 552 is
1.001355x Unit 536, so the quality gain adds no material speed regression.
The current rvp9/vpxenc ratio is still 1.499930x and remains far outside the
1.05x final gate. A detached Unit-536 timing worktree remains at
`/Users/md/worktrees/rvp9-2/unit552-baseline`; normal removal refused because

Exact next experiment: regenerate the paired frame-1 candidate trace from

## Unit 556 — reject emitted-DCT gating of the sub-32 skip tie-break

The frame-1 shared-block aggregation found 20 cases with matching coordinates,
block size, qindex, LAST reference, mode, MV, filter, and prediction SSE where
rvp9 charged coefficient rate but libvpx selected its later skip-side RD
branch. The largest was Block16 `(50,50)`: both encoders chose LAST+NEARESTMV
`(0,2)`, EightTap, q166, SSE 7,785, and variance 7,775. Rvp9 charged 6,016
luma coefficient-rate units while its eventual emitted transform had zero
EOB and the final block was skip=true.

Matched temporary libvpx instrumentation ruled out the variance model itself:
`model_rd_for_sb_y` also returned rate 6,016, distortion 118,368, and
`SKIP_TXFM_NONE` with the same DC/AC thresholds 361/708. Libvpx's later
`block_yrd` plus encode-vs-skip comparison is the difference; it may set
`SKIP_TXFM_AC_DC` even when the Hadamard result is not skippable. Rvp9's
natural-content S2 gate deliberately forbids that override below Block32.
Disabling S2 globally was already decisively unsafe at 1000 kbps: ducks fell
from 24.836518 dB to 23.990161 dB.

Unit 556 tested a narrower rule behind `RVP9_S2_DCT_EOB_PROBE=1`. Only when
skip-side RD already won for a sub-32 Hadamard-nonskippable candidate did it
run the emitter-matching DCT + `quant_fp`; it allowed the skip override only
when that probe produced zero EOB. The focused core test compiled and passed.
The three-clip 1000 kbps checkpoint still rejected it:

- `in_to_tree`: 1,437.036 kbps / Y 35.192765 / average 36.290103, versus Unit
  552's 1,439.956 / 35.184695 / 36.282023 (small win).
- `ducks_take_off`: 1,796.128 kbps / Y 24.803764 / average 26.112129, versus
  1,796.852 / 24.836518 / 26.137228 (0.032754 dB luma loss).
- `old_town_cross`: 1,504.156 kbps / Y 35.229337 / average 36.362730, versus
  1,497.564 / 35.244096 / 36.377130 (0.4402% more bits and 0.014759 dB luma
  loss).

The apparently safe emitted-zero subset still changes future reference state
and mode contexts in content-dependent ways. It is not a corpus-wide Pareto
improvement, so the source edit was removed and Unit 552 remains accepted.
The pinned libvpx binary was rebuilt after restoring the temporary oracle
filter.

Exact next experiment: keep the S2 policy fixed and decompose the remaining
shared candidate gaps by syntax, chroma, mode/MV, and reference cost. Look for
a repeated component whose correction reduces the *ranking* gap without
changing the residual-vs-skip policy; require the 1000 kbps checkpoint to win
or stay neutral on all three clips before paying for a full curve.

to `StreamEncoder::new_with_parallelism` and vpxenc. Focused tests prove that
the production request selects one worker and four legal tiles at 1280 pixels,
and that explicit 30 fps overrides a 50 fps source header. All six binary tests,

The corrected trace is
`target/track_f_oracle/unit559_matched_720p30/run_6a6f9af7`. It uses 60 frames,

source-aligned environment. Frame 1 uses q166 in both encoders. It contains

and 196 also share qindex, reference, mode, motion vector, interpolation filter,
and prediction SSE.

Across those 196 exact-input pairs, rvp9 minus libvpx component totals are

libvpx skips contribute +145,800 rate and +59,309,047 RD; the 134 common-skip
cases contribute −40,549 rate and −20,183,814 RD. The corrected trace therefore

A one-tile rvp9 diagnostic produced luma BD-rate

## Unit 561 — keyframe skip-probability forward updates accepted

The corrected trace isolated a probability-bank mismatch before the remaining
picker differences. At every frame-1 tile start, reference, mode, and filter
costs matched, but rvp9 charged 1,024 units for `skip=true` while pinned
libvpx charged 3,284. Rvp9's keyframe count pass collected only coefficient
counts, so `write_skip_probs` emitted three identity updates and frame 1 used
the default skip bank. Libvpx always runs `update_skip_probs` in the compressed
header, including keyframes.

The keyframe count pass now records each leaf's skip symbol. Before writing the
compressed header, it derives the ideal binary probability for each context,
runs the existing libvpx-exact probability-difference savings search, and
places each profitable result in the post-header frame context. The writer and
encoder/decoder mirrors retain the same forward-updated bank. A focused test
proves a noisy keyframe changes the skip bank and that the encoder mirror
exactly equals rvp9-decoder's bank after decoding.

The repaired two-frame trace is
`target/track_f_oracle/unit561_kfskip_720p30/run_6a6f9e9b`. Frame 1 remains
q166. All four tile-start rvp9 skip costs move from 1,024 to the exact libvpx
value 3,284; filter costs remain exact at 1,069. This closes the first causal
probability difference without changing the residual-versus-skip policy.

The full six-point CPU7 VBR curves use 500/750/1000/1500/2500/4000 kbps,
60-frame 1280x704 crops, 30 fps, one thread, tile request six, and the
source-aligned environment. Luma BD-rate versus pinned vpxenc is

`+14.975962%/-6.315550%/+35.485322%` on

moves `-0.108244/-0.100171/+0.043462` points and average-YUV moves

## Unit 562 — reject source-exact CPU7 real `block_yrd`

The Unit 561 next-experiment interpretation was incomplete. Rvp9's
6,272/120,192 result exactly matches `model_rd_for_sb_y` at q166, variance
7,871, SSE 7,919, AC dequant 341, and effective qstep 42. Libvpx's 103,942
distortion is not divisible by eight and therefore cannot be the simple
model's shifted output. Direct speed-feature inspection resolves the policy:
`use_simple_block_yrd` starts disabled, is enabled at speed 7 only for SVC
enhancement layers, and becomes unconditional at speed 8. The old Unit 436
claim that CPU7 always takes the simple model is wrong; it inferred the policy
from the function's internal size gate without checking its caller-side speed
feature.

A temporary typed calibration disabled `model_only` at CPU6/7 while retaining
it at CPU8. This makes the CPU7 picker run its real Hadamard `block_yrd` path,
matching pinned libvpx's policy. The focused policy and 72 inter tests passed,
but all three 1000 kbps checkpoints failed the Pareto rule versus Unit 561:

- `in_to_tree`: 1,435.540 kbps / Y 35.157123 / average 36.257572, versus
  1,429.996 / 35.185721 / 36.282055;
- `ducks_take_off`: 1,811.048 kbps / Y 24.809576 / average 26.129227, versus
  1,795.180 / 24.831714 / 26.132964;
- `old_town_cross`: 1,497.332 kbps / Y 35.186708 / average 36.321700, versus
  1,494.280 / 35.245299 / 36.381045.

The source-exact policy spends more bits and lowers PSNR everywhere, so it was
removed. Unit 561 remains accepted. The result establishes that rvp9's current
prediction/ranking system depends on the model-only approximation that earlier
work retained for its measured quality and speed benefit; removing it requires
a coupled correction, not a policy toggle.

Exact next experiment: keep model-only pricing and compare its chosen
prediction against libvpx's lower real-`block_yrd` candidate at the first
mode/MV divergence. Determine whether a repeated motion-search, filter-search,
or reference-context difference produces a worse predictor before attempting
to replace the residual price.

A fresh production-matched 60-frame F.0.2 trace at 1000 kbps confirms that

8x8-area cells to `NEARESTMV` versus libvpx's 405,860, while `NEWMV` is
318,893 versus 369,851. Skip area is close, so this is not a global skip-count
deficit.

A fixed-q 200 trace removed rate-control and high-precision-MV differences.
Among exact coordinate-and-size matches where rvp9 chose `NEARESTMV` and
libvpx chose `NEWMV`, 2,060 rvp9 `NEWMV` candidates survived production
gates and 1,656 had lower prediction distortion than rvp9's `NEARESTMV`.
For the 109 leaves where both encoders used the exact same `NEWMV`, rvp9's
median candidate rate was 1.60x libvpx's and every rvp9 `NEWMV` still lost
its local argmin.

The bounded experiment kept model distortion and every non-`NEWMV` candidate
unchanged, but used rvp9's real Hadamard `block_yrd` rate for sub-32

## Unit 571 — retain coupled current-frame non-coefficient probability updates

The fixed-q old-town trace exposed a broader compressed-header mismatch than
motion search. Rvp9 already forward-updated coefficient probabilities from
current-frame counts, but gathered every mode/MV count only while packing the
final tiles. Pinned libvpx gathers complete counts before the header and
savings-gates current-frame updates for TX, skip, inter mode, interpolation,
intra/inter, references, Y mode, partition, and motion vectors.

The retained implementation ports both update policies: standard probability
families use the existing exact diff-update savings search, while MV families
use libvpx's distinct seven-literal-bit cost test and odd probability target.
One-thread encoding gathers full counts and retained coefficient tokens in the
same pre-header traversal. Parallel tile coefficient records need a count-only
replay to recover mode/MV counts. `RVP9_FORWARD_MODE_PROBS=0` remains only as
a differential opt-out.

At fixed qindex 200 on 60-frame 1280x704 old-town, decoded quality is exactly
unchanged at Y `30.213125` dB and average-YUV `31.572761` dB. The IVF shrinks
from 78,059 bytes (`312.236` kbps) to 77,546 bytes (`310.184` kbps), a
`0.657%` fixed-symbol saving. The six-point CPU7 VBR luma BD-rates versus
pinned vpxenc are now `+15.222327%/-9.692528%/+38.256838%` on
in-to-tree/ducks/old-town, versus Unit 561's
`+15.745779%/-6.972353%/+38.107266%`. Average-YUV is
`+14.465214%/-9.031002%/+35.699395%`, versus
`+14.975975%/-6.315552%/+35.485312%`. Relative to Unit 561, the new path
improves luma by `0.440556%` and `2.798594%` on the first two clips and
regresses old-town by `0.108366%`; average-YUV moves
`-0.434158%/-2.785842%/+0.153818%`. The old-town trade is retained as a
measured source-parity prerequisite because every fixed-symbol update is net
bit-saving and the curve movement comes through one-pass rate-control
feedback.

The count-and-record fusion and final-packing count reuse reproduce the initial
two-pass diagnostic stream byte-for-byte. Nine warmed alternating one-thread
runs measure median user CPU at `1.006670x` and wall at `1.007037x` the prior
path. The candidate remains roughly `1.5x` pinned vpxenc overall, so the final
speed gate is still open.

The 1000 kbps in-to-tree candidate IVF SHA-256 is
`86b85cc919c26aba3d1915d710f7fb642851043343f412751fbe4d2e57d0615f`.
Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg each produce the same 81,100,800-byte

## Unit 574 — retain qindex-derived motion-search rate multipliers

Decoder-side fixed-q 200 bit accounting localized rvp9's remaining old-town
payload excess to coefficients (`+24,252.962` modeled bits), motion vectors
(`+22,785.207`), and skip syntax (`+14,455.109`). The first causal NEWMV
divergence was the top-left 64x64 leaf of frame 1: both encoders started from
`(0,0)` with `FAST_DIAMOND`, but rvp9's full-pel winner was `(4,1)` while
pinned libvpx chose `(5,1)`.

Direct runtime tracing found a stale calibration in
`crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/inter.rs:run_newmv_search`. At internal
qindex 200, pinned libvpx uses `sadperbit16=9`, `errorperbit=10285`, and
`rdmult=658246`; rvp9 hard-coded both motion-search rate multipliers to `16`.
Replacing those constants with libvpx's 8-bit qindex formulas makes the first
full-pel result exactly `(5,1)`. The remaining sub-pel choice differs because
the reconstructed references differ: rvp9 and libvpx have identical MV-cost
terms at the six sampled half-pel positions, while their measured variances
differ. No interpolation change was made.

The six-point CPU7 VBR curves use the established
500/750/1000/1500/2500/4000 kbps, 60-frame 1280x704, one-thread matrix. Luma
BD-rate versus pinned vpxenc is now
`+14.792792%/-10.157464%/+38.160992%` on
in-to-tree/ducks-take-off/old-town-cross. Average-YUV BD-rate is
`+13.985011%/-9.484911%/+35.691787%`. Relative to Unit 571, all six metrics
improve: luma moves `-0.429535/-0.464936/-0.095846` points and average-YUV
moves `-0.480203/-0.453909/-0.007608` points.

At 1000 kbps the candidate points are:

- `in_to_tree`: `1434.532` kbps / Y `35.206105` / average `36.302919`;
- `ducks_take_off`: `1795.200` kbps / Y `25.067965` / average `26.354207`;
- `old_town_cross`: `1493.684` kbps / Y `35.244615` / average `36.375503`.

Nine warmed alternating in-to-tree runs show no resolvable wall-time change:
both Unit 571 and Unit 574 have `0.61 s` median wall time. The coarse median
user times are `0.59-0.60 s`; no speed claim beyond neutrality is made.

All three 1000 kbps streams decode bit-exactly through rvp9-decoder, pinned

## Unit 577 — reject AQ-off skin-map gating as a speed optimization

Ten-iteration 1 kHz `samply` profiles compared Unit 576 with pinned vpxenc on
the 60-frame in-to-tree CPU7 VBR checkpoint. Unit 576 recorded 6,738 samples
versus vpxenc's 4,406, consistent with the roughly 1.5x speed gap. The first
symbolized view attributed 539 Unit 576 leaf samples to
`compute_skin_map_rows`; pinned libvpx enables skin detection only for one-pass
CBR cyclic-refresh AQ, not the AQ-off VBR checkpoint.

A candidate gated serial and worker-pool skin-map production to CBR cyclic
refresh. All three 1000 kbps outputs were byte-identical to Unit 576. A fresh
profile contained no `compute_skin_map_rows` samples and 6,608 total samples,
but repeated process timing did not reproduce a speed win. Nine alternating
single encodes had equal `0.68 s` median user time. Five alternating batches of
ten encodes measured median user time `6.84 s` for the candidate versus
`6.80 s` for Unit 576, with wall medians `7.01 s` versus `6.94 s`. The apparent
profile attribution was therefore dominated by inline-symbol attribution and
sampling noise rather than a reproducible wall-time bottleneck.

The candidate source changes were removed. Unit 576 remains accepted. The
profile's strongest remaining behavioral mismatch is interpolation-filter
selection: pinned libvpx searches non-NEWMV filters only while its causal
`filter_ref` remains `SWITCHABLE`, then inherits a concrete above/left filter;
rvp9 searches every fractional mode on its chessboard cells and otherwise
forces `EIGHTTAP`. Exact next experiment: carry libvpx's causal `filter_ref`
into the picker, reproduce that search/inheritance condition, and measure the
three-clip 1000 kbps checkpoint before retaining it.

## Unit 578 — reject causal interpolation-filter inheritance

The candidate reproduced pinned `vp9_pickmode.c`'s causal `filter_ref` rule:
use the above inter neighbour first, otherwise the left inter neighbour;
search a fractional non-`NEWMV` candidate only while that reference remains
`SWITCHABLE`, and otherwise inherit the concrete filter. Focused tests covered
neighbour priority, intra-neighbour exclusion, the `NEWMV` exception, and
concrete-filter inheritance.

The six-point CPU7 VBR luma BD-rates versus pinned vpxenc were
`-1.057162%/-14.043755%/+4.698088%` on

`-0.741492%/-13.294819%/+4.668328%`. Compared with Unit 576's luma
`-5.757972%/-11.538703%/+3.831972%`, the candidate improved ducks but lost
about one percentage point in the three-clip mean and pushed old-town farther
beyond the per-clip gate.

Five alternating batches of ten warmed in-to-tree encodes measured median
user time `6.35 s` versus Unit 576's `6.48 s` (`0.9799x`) and wall time
`6.50 s` versus `6.62 s` (`0.9819x`). The reproducible roughly 2% speed win
does not compensate for the quality regression, so the candidate source and
tests were removed. This source-faithful local rule is not Pareto-compatible

Exact next experiment: use the Unit 576 and pinned profiles to split

## Unit 579 — reject reusable Hadamard output scratch

Symbolizing the Unit 576 profile against its exact release binary attributes
1,006 of 6,738 samples (`14.93%`) directly to
`reconstruct_via_round_trip`. The Hadamard-only product path allocated a
zeroed transform-sized coefficient array for each tile even though the fused
subtract/Hadamard kernels overwrite every active coefficient.

The bounded candidate moved that array into the existing per-thread
`RoundTripScratch`. A poison-buffer regression proved all supported realtime
transform sizes overwrite the active prefix. The resulting 1000 kbps streams
for in-to-tree, ducks-take-off, and old-town-cross were byte-identical to Unit
576.

Five alternating batches of ten warmed in-to-tree encodes nevertheless had
identical medians: `6.74 s` user and `6.87 s` wall for both variants. The
compiler already removes or amortizes the apparent initialization cost. The
candidate source and test were removed.

## Unit 582 — retain the pinned libvpx lowbd 8x8 forward DCT path

The Unit 581 profile attributed 356 of 6,647 samples (`5.36%`) to the 8x8
forward DCT, versus `1.41%` in pinned vpxenc. Rvp9's general AArch64 transform
uses scalar-equivalent first-pass arithmetic plus a conservative overflow
scan and scalar fallback. Pinned libvpx's low-bit-depth encoder instead uses
its approximate i16 first-pass multiply, widened one-coefficient second-pass
butterflies, and no overflow scan.

The retained change adds that pinned lowbd transform as a separate core entry
point and uses it only for inter tx-size selection and coefficient emission,
where residuals come from u8 pixels. The general transform and its full-range
scalar-equivalence contract remain unchanged. A focused oracle pins the
otherwise surprising constant `-255` residual result (`DC = -16319`) observed
directly from pinned `vpx_fdct8x8_neon`.

All 18 combinations of the three Stage 4a clips and 500, 750, 1000, 1500,
2500, and 4000 kbps are byte-identical to Unit 576. Its accepted BD-rate
curves and cross-decoder hashes therefore remain exact. Two reversed-order
series of five batches, ten warmed in-to-tree encodes per batch, produced
combined medians of `6.50 s` user and `6.645 s` wall versus Unit 581's
`6.55 s` and `6.715 s`. Ratios are `0.9924x` user and `0.9896x` wall. One
Unit 581 wall sample suffered a host-scheduling outlier (`16.46 s`), but the
paired medians remain separated without relying on it.

Validation passed: the pinned lowbd transform oracle; the unchanged general
transform oracle; all 1,648 `rvp9-core` library tests; all 569 active

all-target clippy with warnings denied; rustfmt; and `git diff --check`.

## Unit 585 — reject copied selected-TX coefficient cache

The candidate added reusable per-thread candidate and selected caches to
`InterEmitScratch`. The transform-size loop copied each candidate tile's
quantized and dequantized coefficients into the candidate cache, copied a
winning candidate into the selected cache, and reused the selected data in
luma emission. Trellis-enabled paths remained on the original computation.

The 1000 kbps in-to-tree stream was byte-identical to Unit 584, confirming
the cached coefficients preserved the encoded decision and reconstruction.
Two reversed-order series of four batches, ten warmed encodes per batch,
measured combined medians of `6.205 s` user and `6.355 s` wall versus Unit
584's `6.225 s` and `6.370 s`. Those apparent `0.997x` aggregate ratios did
not reproduce pairwise: the median paired wall ratio was about `1.001x`.
Copying each candidate and then each new winner consumed the transform work
saved during emission.

The candidate source was removed. Unit 584 remains accepted.

Exact next experiment: test a zero-copy variant of the same measured
duplicate. Quantize each TX-size candidate directly into one reusable cache,
swap that cache with the selected cache when it wins, and read the selected
cache during emission. This removes both coefficient copies while preserving
the exhaustive TX argmin and exact stream bytes.

## Unit 586 — reject zero-copy selected-TX coefficient cache

The follow-up quantized each candidate directly into a reusable per-thread
buffer and swapped buffer ownership when a candidate became the best. It
therefore removed both Unit 585 copies while preserving the exhaustive
transform-size argmin. A focused oracle compared every selected cached tile
against a fresh transform and quantization for both fast and zbin quantizers.
The 1000 kbps in-to-tree stream remained byte-identical to Unit 584.

Two reversed-order series of four batches, ten warmed encodes per batch,
measured combined medians of `6.305 s` user and `6.425 s` wall versus Unit
584's `6.315 s` and `6.440 s`. Ratios were `0.998x` user and `0.998x` wall,
but the median paired wall ratio was `0.999x` with wins and losses in both
orders. The duplicate selected transform is too small a share after Units
582–584 to justify the cache state and heap buffers.

The candidate source and focused test were removed. Unit 584 remains
accepted. Do not revisit emit-side selected-TX caching without a new profile
showing a materially larger duplicate.

Exact next experiment: return to the dominant picker path. Attribute

## Unit 587 — retain libvpx realtime large-block intra `block_yrd`

The Unit 584 profile attributed `28.00%` inclusive time to
`reconstruct_via_round_trip`. Large intra-in-inter candidates ran both the
Hadamard/fast-quantizer coefficient pricing used by pinned libvpx and a second
DCT/zbin-quantizer/inverse-DCT reconstruction used only to calculate pixel
SSE. Pinned v1.14.1 `vp9_pickmode.c:block_yrd` instead caps this large-block
pricing transform at 16x16 and uses its coefficient error directly.

The retained source-aligned change uses the existing Hadamard-only pricing
path for realtime blocks at least 32x32, caps it at 16x16, skips DCT
reconstruction, and uses coefficient distortion for the partition and RD
score. Compatibility calibration retains the old reconstruction behavior. A
focused test proves the compatibility path produces DCT coefficients while
the realtime large-block path produces Hadamard rate and distortion without
a DCT EOB.

The complete three-clip, six-bitrate Stage 4a screen produced luma BD-rates
against pinned vpxenc of `-5.912166%`, `-11.279091%`, and `+2.598429%` for
in-to-tree, ducks-take-off, and old-town-cross. Average-plane BD-rates were
`-5.217758%`, `-10.613724%`, and `+2.796618%`. Relative to Unit 584, the
old-town-cross luma result improves by `1.234` percentage points, in-to-tree
improves by `0.154`, and ducks-take-off regresses by `0.260`. The result is a
clear aggregate Pareto improvement, though old-town-cross still misses the
intermediate `<= +2%` and final `<= +0.5%` gates.

## Unit 588 — reject Hadamard coefficient-scratch reuse

The post-Unit-587 profile contained `2.83%` self time in `_platform_memset`
versus `0.86%` in pinned vpxenc. The candidate reused `RoundTripScratch`'s
qcoeff buffer as the Hadamard coefficient destination instead of creating a
zero-initialized, transform-sized local array for each tile.

The 1000 kbps in-to-tree stream remained byte-identical to Unit 587. Four
reversed-order batches of ten warmed encodes produced median wall times of
`5.375 s` for the candidate and `5.320 s` for Unit 587, a `1.010x`
regression. The local zero initialization was not the measured excess; buffer
reuse instead made code generation or locality slightly worse.

The candidate source was removed. Unit 587 remains accepted. Do not revisit
this coefficient-scratch alias without disassembly or line-level evidence.

The built-in realtime phase timer attributes the 59 inter frames to
`290.68 ms` final picking, `54.05 ms` coefficient emission, and `46.74 ms`
other orchestration (`391.44 ms` total). Exact VBP descent itself is outside
the timed picker and showed zero recursive-RD time. The next experiment will
remove the 64x64 source materialization before exact VBP: extend its pure
input with explicit source/predictor strides and read the frame plane in
place. Preserve exact tree traces and the Unit 587 stream bytes.

## Unit 589 — reject strided in-place VBP source reads

The candidate extended `FixedTreeInterInput` with independent source and
predictor strides, added a strided-vs-materialized tree oracle, and passed the
production frame plane directly to the exact VBP tree. This removed the
per-fresh-tree 64x64 source copy while leaving its predictor and arithmetic
unchanged. The 1000 kbps in-to-tree stream remained byte-identical to Unit
587.

Four reversed-order batches of ten warmed encodes produced median wall times
of `5.305 s` for the candidate and `5.245 s` for Unit 587, a `1.011x`
regression. The materialized source's contiguous reuse across the tree's
4x4/8x8 average scans repays the copy; frame-stride reads lose more locality
than they save.

The candidate source and focused test were removed. Unit 587 remains
accepted. Keep the contiguous VBP input. Exact next experiment: retain that
layout but hoist its fully overwritten source and predictor arrays out of the
superblock loop, so they are initialized once per frame rather than once per
fresh tree. Require byte identity and a separated paired timing win.

## Unit 590 — reject frame-scoped VBP buffers

The follow-up kept both 64x64 VBP inputs contiguous but hoisted their source
and predictor arrays from the superblock branch to frame/tile-job scope. Both
builders still overwrote every active byte before the tree read it. The 1000
kbps in-to-tree stream remained byte-identical to Unit 587.

Four reversed-order batches of ten warmed encodes produced median wall times
of `5.265 s` for the candidate and `5.270 s` for Unit 587 (`0.999x`). Wins
and losses occurred in both orders, so the apparent half-percent result is
host noise rather than a separated improvement.

The candidate source was removed. Unit 587 remains accepted. Do not spend
more time on VBP buffer lifetime without stronger line-level evidence. Exact
next experiment: compare the absolute Unit 587/vpxenc sample counts outside
mode picking, then select a source-aligned algorithmic or SIMD difference
large enough to recover multiple percentage points.
### Unit 591 — rejected causal interpolation-filter inheritance

- Hypothesis: mirror pinned libvpx realtime `filter_ref` inheritance (above inter
  neighbour first, then left) so non-NEWMV candidates avoid redundant switchable
  interpolation searches. Profiling showed rvp9 spending 447 samples in horizontal
  and vertical convolution versus 214 in vpxenc.
- The implementation passed focused core and encoder tests. Four paired 60-frame
  `in_to_tree` runs made the candidate stable near 5.16–5.17 s versus the clean
  Unit 587 baseline pairs at 5.23–5.27 s, about 2% faster.
- Full six-point curves rejected the trade. Luma BD-rate versus vpxenc changed from
  `-5.912166%` to `-0.820893%` on `in_to_tree`, from `-11.279091%` to
  `-13.789750%` on `ducks_take_off`, and from `+2.598430%` to `+3.943177%`
  on `old_town_cross`. Average-plane BD-rate was `-0.446716%`, `-13.051273%`,
  and `+3.912278%`, respectively.
- Conclusion: the shortcut is behaviorally source-aligned but not a Pareto move in
  the current encoder. It worsens the remaining failing clip and consumes nearly all
  of the clean clip's quality margin. The source and focused test were removed.

### Units 604–606 — fixed-q oracle isolates compensating coding policies

- A fresh fixed-q120, 60-frame, 1280x704 old-town F.0.2 comparison is at

  On exact same-size/mode/reference/MV leaves where rvp9 selects EightTap and

  `crates/rvp9-core/src/mode_decision/inter.rs:y_skip_tie_break_allowed`, not
  a pure model-arithmetic error (the identical-input model oracle remains

- Six clean alternating ten-encode batches rejected that architecture. Unit
  597's batch times were `5.59/5.58/5.56/5.97/5.78/5.92 s` versus
  `5.83/5.61/5.62/5.78/5.70/5.79 s`; medians were `5.685 s` and
  `5.740 s`, so the candidate was `0.97%` slower. The apparent packet saving
  moved coefficient and count work into the hotter picker and widened its
  state and control flow instead of deleting enough arithmetic. The entire
  candidate was removed.
- Do not revisit the packet count path without new operation-level evidence.
  The next experiment should profile and remove output-preserving work around
  the outer partition/picker orchestration or final post-pick encoding, where
  Unit 601 still places the unexplained gap.

### Units 611–612 — retain native i16 coefficients in one arena

- Resolving Unit 601's outer-picker samples to source lines placed `78` of
  its `299` self samples at the per-transform residual-emission closure. The
  hot path converted every native `i16` quantizer result into a separately
  allocated `Vec<i32>` before the count and packet traversals.
- Unit 611 replaced the per-transform vectors with one contiguous arena. An
  `i32` arena kept output exact but reduced the instrumented coefficient
  insertion phase only from `9.34 ms` to `9.10 ms` over 59 old-town inter
  frames. Unit 612 then retained the quantizer's native `i16` values through
  the arena and generalized token writing over `i16`/`i32`, removing the
  widening copy and halving coefficient storage.
- Unit 612 is byte-identical to Unit 597 for all three 1000 kbps clips and
  old-town 2500. The 1000 kbps SHA-256 values remain
  `59e12f5f...54e6`, `d89d5bb4...9e3c0`, and
  `ac75e78b...f77a`. rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg each decoded
  old-town 1000 to the same `81,100,800` bytes with SHA-256
  `f483c09c...c9701`.
- The host became heavily contended by unrelated release builds during the
  timing run, so these are supporting compute-time measurements rather than
  the final wall-time gate. Twelve alternating old-town encodes had user-time
  medians of `0.835 s` for Unit 597 and `0.825 s` for Unit 612 (`0.988x`),
  with ten candidate wins and two ties. Six in-to-tree pairs moved the user
  median from about `0.740 s` to `0.735 s`; ducks was neutral before a host
  load transition. A longer four-batch old-town run had user-time medians of
  `6.815 s` and `6.690 s`, but two control batches overlapped fresh load and
  must not be used as a final speed claim.
- Focused token, writer, arena replacement/merge, decoder round-trip, format,
  and clippy checks pass. The candidate's old-town stream is cross-decoder
  bit-exact. Keep the unit as an output-preserving measured compute reduction;
  repeat the full warmed wall-time matrix once the host is quiet.
- Exact next experiment: rebuild the sampling profile on Unit 612 and compare
  the remaining outer-picker self samples. Target the next largest exact
  source line, not the now-removed coefficient allocation/widening work.

### Unit 613 — read full chroma source blocks in place

- A fresh Unit 612 sample profile at 10 kHz recorded `7,997` weighted samples.
  The outer partition/picker function held `505` self samples. Source-line

  block. The sensitivity probe now passes that source slice and its real

- The candidate is byte-identical to Unit 612 for all three 1000 kbps clips
  and old-town at 2500 kbps. Their SHA-256 values remain
  `59e12f5f...54e6`, `d89d5bb4...9e3c0`, `ac75e78b...f77a`, and
  `cda3e229...19c6` respectively.
- A matched candidate profile recorded `8,422` weighted samples. The
  sensitivity call fell from `151` self samples to `4`; outer-picker self
  samples fell from `505` to `392`. Twelve alternating old-town encodes under
  a still-loaded host reduced median process user time from `0.680 s` to
  `0.665 s` (`0.978x`, 9/12 candidate wins). Wall medians were `0.710 s` and
  `0.700 s` (`0.986x`, 7/12 wins). Treat the user-time result and sample
  deletion as acceptance evidence; reserve final wall claims for a quiet-host
  warmed matrix.
- Both focused sensitivity tests, encoder all-target clippy with warnings
  denied, formatting, and diff checks pass. The exact stream checks cover the
  exercised product behavior.
- Exact next experiment: profile the retained residual-emission closure at
  `crates/rvp9-encoder/src/lib.rs:7676`. Split its subtract, transform,
  quantize, inverse-transform, and coefficient-arena costs before changing it;
  the enclosing source line still holds `135` self samples but does not yet

### Units 614–615 — reject the diagnostic cache; skip discarded tile-MT replay

- Unit 613's existing emission counters split the 59 inter frames into
  `25.84 ms` prediction, `21.32 ms` forward-transform/quantization,
  `13.16 ms` inverse transform, `9.57 ms` coefficient insertion, and
  `9.54 ms` residual subtraction. These are all required coding operations;
  the residual closure is not a dead-work target.
- Unit 614 cached the global bit-accounting diagnostic switch in each
  `BoolWriter`. It preserved all four stream hashes and passed the writer and
  accounting tests, but twenty alternating one-tile pairs were neutral to
  slower: wall `1.007x`, process user time `1.007x`. Disassembly explained
  the result: fat LTO already proves the diagnostic switch remains false in
  the production CLI and removes its atomic load entirely. The candidate was
  removed. Do not retry diagnostic-flag caching on the fat-LTO product.
- The same disassembly exposed a real tile-MT-only waste. Forward non-coef
  probability adaptation walks modes through a count-only writer. With
  picker-recorded tile coefficients, that pass also replayed every retained
  coefficient token even though each arithmetic write immediately returned
  without updating bytes or counts. Unit 615 now consumes each retained block
  boundary and nonzero flag, updates coefficient contexts, and skips only the
  discarded token walk. Final tile writers still replay every token against
  the post-header probability table.
- A focused regression constructs a deliberately invalid retained probability
  coordinate and proves count-only replay never reads it while still consuming
  the block and setting above/left contexts. The existing emitted-replay and
  extra-block mismatch oracle remains green.
- Unit 615 is byte-identical to Unit 613 for all three one-tile 1000 kbps
  streams, old-town one-tile 2500, and old-town four-thread/four-column-tile
  2500. The hashes remain `59e12f5f...54e6`, `d89d5bb4...9e3c0`,
  `ac75e78b...f77a`, and `cda3e229...19c6`.
- The one-tile path is correctly neutral because it already gathers all
  counts while recording tokens in one traversal. Twelve alternating
  five-encode batches on the four-thread/four-tile path reduce wall median
  from `1.510 s` to `1.410 s` (`0.934x`, 11/12 wins) and process-user median
  from `0.715 s` to `0.700 s` (`0.979x`, 8/12 wins, three ties). The host was
  still loaded, so use this as paired acceptance evidence rather than the
  final absolute latency claim.
- Matched 10 kHz profiles confirm the mechanism. Main-thread retained replay
  self samples fall from `251/3,838` (`6.54%`) to `91/3,759` (`2.42%`). Core
  all-target clippy with warnings denied, both focused retained-pass tests,
  formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Exact next experiment: establish fresh Unit 615 versus pinned-vpxenc speed
  ratios for both the one-thread/one-tile and four-thread/four-tile matched
  old-town points. Then use the slower field's profile, not the now-removed
  count-only replay, to choose the next optimization.

### Unit 616 — parallelize keyframe reconstruction across column tiles

- Fresh matched old-town 2500 measurements showed that Unit 615 still missed
  the speed gate. Twelve warmed alternating batches measured `1.176x` pinned
  vpxenc with one thread/one tile and `1.582x` with four threads/four column
  tiles. The host was loaded, so these ratios select the bottleneck rather than
  serving as final acceptance numbers.
- Matched 10 kHz four-thread profiles isolated the scaling failure. In a normal
  GOP, rvp9's main thread spent `696/3,759` weighted samples in the keyframe
  reconstruction while pinned vpxenc distributes its keyframe tile work across
  all workers. In an all-keyframe run, Unit 615 kept all `42,798` inclusive
  keyframe-encode samples on the main thread; vpxenc spread similar work over
  its main thread and three workers.
- Unit 616 runs the independent full-height keyframe column tiles on the
  stream's existing worker pool. Each job owns retained frame-shaped scratch,
  partition decisions, coefficient storage, and causal intra-neighbour state.
  The stream thread merges disjoint reconstruction rectangles, partitions, and
  coefficient slots in tile-column order. Prediction and F.0.2 diagnostics keep
  the prior serial path because their sinks are thread-local.
- The normal old-town 2500 four-tile stream remains byte-identical to Unit 615
  (`cda3e229f892c002877caf37abc9baa190b578b25beea8b967cf0ea7fe0d19c6`).
  A 60-frame all-keyframe stress stream is also identical
  (`22fe08532351cbb7ea3afe731a855aec1b80d6242e7efac5c0b3b00822a2832c`).
  rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg produced the same decoded raw hash
  (`230e96b83aa5f8527dbf75d87a50fdc6340b354da20dce75a489d00bc5a50f33`).
- Twelve alternating normal-GOP observations reduced the Unit 615 wall median
  from `0.286334 s` to `0.265882 s` (`0.9286x`, candidate won all twelve).
  Eight alternating all-keyframe observations reduced the median from
  `4.109031 s` to `2.595495 s` (`0.6316x`, candidate won all eight). These are
  paired acceptance results under host load, not quiet-host absolute budgets.
- Against pinned vpxenc, twelve alternating normal-GOP observations measured
  candidate `0.302310 s` versus vpxenc `0.206935 s`, or `1.4609x`. Unit 616 is
  a large Pareto improvement but does not close the final `1.05x` speed gate.
- The post-change all-keyframe profile is archived at
  `/tmp/rvp9-unit616-allkf-profile.json.gz` with its text summary beside it.
  Main-thread final keyframe tile traversal is now the largest serial phase:
  `write_tile_intra_keyframe_with_counts` is `17,831/33,069` inclusive samples
  (`53.9%`). Keyframe reconstruction is active on every worker and accounts for
  `46,825/132,267` inclusive all-thread samples.
- Both four-tile thread-independence tests, encoder all-target clippy with
  warnings denied, formatting, and diff checks pass. The stream-level test
  covers both the newly parallel keyframe and the existing inter path.
- Exact next experiment: parallelize the independent pre-header count traversal
  and final arithmetic write for keyframe column tiles, reusing the inter packet
  writer's ordered `WorkerPool` result pattern. Preserve byte-exact output and
  keep bit-accounting diagnostics serial.

### Unit 617 — parallelize both keyframe packet tile traversals

  remained serial. Unit 617 now runs each independent column tile through the
  existing stream worker pool for both passes. Worker-local `FrameCounts` are
  added in tile order before building the unchanged compressed-header update
  plan; final tile buffers are also joined and assembled in tile order.
  Bit-accounting diagnostics retain the serial path because their sink is

  `2.617414 s` to `1.652849 s` (`0.6315x`, candidate won all eight). The host

- The post-change five-iteration normal-GOP profile is archived at

  The remaining normal-GOP main-thread work is inter encoding: tile picking

- Both four-tile thread-independence tests, both sequential two-tile packet

- Exact next experiment: collect a fresh five-iteration pinned-vpxenc profile

### Unit 618 — parallelize inter pre-header mode counting

- Matched five-iteration 10 kHz profiles at Unit 617 recorded `53,863`
  all-thread weighted samples for rvp9 and `35,240` for pinned vpxenc. Encoder
  binary self samples were much closer (`29,645` versus `27,107`, `1.094x`),
  but rvp9's main-thread sample count was `13,484` versus `9,082` (`1.485x`).
  The remaining speed gap is therefore mostly critical-path scheduling rather
  than proportionally more coding work.
- The profile comparison identified a safe serial packet phase. With recorded
  coefficient tiles, rvp9 walked all four inter mode trees serially before the
  compressed header to gather non-coefficient probability counts. Unit 615 had
  removed discarded coefficient-token replay from that pass, but the remaining
  partition/mode traversal was still independent per column tile. Unit 618 now
  executes those four count-only traversals on the existing worker pool and
  folds their `FrameCounts` in tile order. Bit-accounting diagnostics retain
  the serial path.
- The old-town 2500 four-tile stream remains byte-identical to Unit 617, with
  SHA-256
  `cda3e229f892c002877caf37abc9baa190b578b25beea8b967cf0ea7fe0d19c6`.
  The existing four-tile thread-independence tests cover the new pass and both
  remain green.
- Twelve alternating observations reduced the Unit 617 wall median from
  `0.227009 s` to `0.219156 s` (`0.9654x`, candidate won all twelve). A fresh
  twelve-observation comparison measured Unit 618 at `0.237343 s` versus
  pinned vpxenc at `0.174888 s`, or `1.3571x`. Host load was still changing,
  so use the paired result as acceptance evidence and not as a final absolute
  latency claim. The final `1.05x` gate remains open.
- Both focused four-tile tests, encoder all-target clippy with warnings denied,
  formatting, and diff checks pass.
- Exact next experiment: profile Unit 618 with five matched iterations. Verify
  that the serial pre-header traversal left the main-thread packet subtree,
  then choose between the remaining inter packet critical path and the
  deliberately one-worker loop filter. Do not raise loop-filter worker count
  without first replacing its overlapping full-plane mutable slices; that
  would reintroduce the aliasing defect closed by RVP9-BUG-KILN-00024.

### Unit 618 profile — packet work reduced; inter picking still dominates

  ratio. Its profile is `/tmp/rvp9-unit619-rd-profile.json.gz`:
  `choose_inter_luma_tx_size` was `13.97%` inclusive and `5.90%` self time.

### Unit 626 — reject zero-copy selected-TX cache

- The candidate quantized TX8 and TX16 directly into two per-thread buffers,

- Twenty alternating four-thread old-town observations measured Unit 623 at
  `0.237264 s` median and the cache at `0.237138 s`, or `0.9995x`; the median
  paired ratio was `0.9947x`, with the candidate winning 12 of 20 pairs. This

  RVP9-BUG-KILN-00024 safety fix.

### Unit 627 — reject Hadamard output reuse

- The candidate reused the round-trip scratch `qcoeff` prefix as the
  Hadamard transform output, eliminating a per-tile zero-initialized array.
  It was byte-identical, but thirty alternating old-town four-thread pairs
  measured a `1.0012x` median paired wall ratio and only 14 of 30 wins.
- The compiler already removes or hides most of the apparent initialization,
  while aliasing the Hadamard output with later quantizer scratch gives no
  useful work reduction. The source change was removed.
- An alias-safe multiworker loop filter would require changing the DSP
  boundary away from whole-plane mutable slices. Unit 624 attributes only
  about 2.3% of all samples to the encoder loop-filter path, so that broad
  unsafe refactor is deferred in favor of the larger entropy and picker gaps.

### Unit 628 — snapshot bit-accounting state per BoolWriter

- `BoolWriter::write` previously loaded the global diagnostic `AtomicBool`
  for every arithmetic-coded bit. Bit accounting is initialized before a
  stream's writers and stays fixed for their lifetime, so each writer now
  snapshots the enabled state once. Count-only writers pin it off.
- Forty alternating old-town four-thread pairs measured wall medians of
  `0.248667 s` for Unit 623 and `0.247878 s` for the candidate. The ratio of
  medians was `0.9968x`; median paired wall was `0.9970x` with 24/40 wins.
  Median paired user CPU was `0.9977x` with 25/40 wins. This is a small but
  reproducible work reduction under variable host load.
- The 2500 kbps stream and all three 1000 kbps checkpoint streams are
  byte-identical to Unit 623. The full ignored E4 accounting harness passes
  and reports its normal per-category totals, proving the diagnostic remains
  active when requested. Focused BoolWriter and bit-accounting tests, core
  all-target clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt, and diff checks pass.
- Exact next experiment: reduce the retained coefficient replay/tokenization
  cost or one measured inter-picker subtree without changing Unit 623's
  coefficient decisions.

### Unit 629 — specialize coefficient record versus emit loops

- `encode_coefs_impl` and its token-cache loop now take a const
  `EMIT_BITS` parameter. Final/direct encoding instantiates the emitting
  path; the count-only retained-token pass instantiates a branch-free
  non-emitting path. The record/emit choice remains once per transform
  block, but every per-coefficient `if emit_bits` and the token-cache
  ternary are compile-time folded.
- Forty alternating four-thread old-town pairs against Unit 628 measured
  wall medians of `0.229564 s` and `0.227976 s`, or `0.9931x`; median paired
  wall was `0.9940x` with 28/40 wins. Median user CPU fell from `0.706957 s`
  to `0.701336 s`, or `0.9920x` by medians and `0.9924x` paired, with 37/40
  wins.
- The 2500 kbps stream and all three 1000 kbps checkpoints are
  byte-identical to Unit 628/623. All 1,652 core library tests, the complete
  retained-token/detokenize focus, the ignored E4 accounting harness, core
  all-target clippy with warnings denied, rustfmt, and diff checks pass.
- Exact next experiment: profile the cumulative Units 628–629 build to

### Unit 632 — retain dot-product sub-pixel variance dispatch

  variance shape to the existing plain NEON implementation. Existing
  all-offset/all-shape differential tests prove the NEON and dot-product
  kernels return identical variance and SSE.

  three 1000 kbps checkpoints, but it was slower. Forty alternating
  four-thread old-town pairs measured `1.0064x` median paired wall time with
  12/40 wins and `1.0142x` paired user CPU with 6/40 wins. The source change
  was removed; the dot-product path remains the correct local dispatch.

  search structure, not a slower rvp9 kernel. Exact next experiment: measure
  NEWMV fractional-search call/probe counts against pinned libvpx before
  changing the search loop.

### Unit 645 — reject persistent inter-packet tile buffers

- The candidate retained four fixed-size arithmetic-coder destinations in

### Unit 646 — reject broad and low-signal NEWMV pruning

- Disabling NEWMV on every block no larger than 32x32 produced a large local
  speed signal: forty four-thread old-town pairs measured `0.781142x` paired
  wall time and `0.727204x` paired child CPU. The output also shrank from
  883,331 to 770,625 bytes, so this was a rate-distortion trade rather than an
  output-preserving search saving.
- The complete three-clip, six-point curve decisively rejects the trade.
  Ducks-take-off regressed to `+80.475241%` luma and `+85.533457%`
  average-YUV BD-rate. In-to-tree and old-town-cross lost enough quality that
  their candidate and pinned-vpxenc PSNR ranges no longer overlap. This is not
  a usable speed lever, even as a Stage 4a intermediate.
- Extending libvpx's existing low-temporal-variance short circuit to VBR level
  2 changed no bytes on old-town 2500 and measured `1.004180x` paired wall and
  `1.000458x` paired CPU across forty pairs. The exact-VBP low-variance flags
  do not cover the expensive searches on this corpus point.
- Moving the adaptive RD-threshold check ahead of NEWMV search matches pinned
  libvpx's source order and kept the stream byte-identical, but a diagnostic
  counted only 1,546 avoided searches over the 60-frame old-town run. Forty
  pairs measured `1.035444x` wall and `1.007302x` CPU on a heavily contended
  host, with no positive signal worth retaining. The candidate and all
  diagnostic logging are fully removed.
- E3 diagnostics show why a blanket prune fails: NEWMV wins 15.7% of 1,087
  leaves on the final sampled frame and 29.8% of 2,149 leaves on the preceding
  frame. It is not a rare fallback; a useful optimization must make the search
  itself cheaper or identify a stronger pre-search rejection oracle.
- Exact next experiment: use the committed Unit 644 profiles and pinned
  `vp9_pickmode.c` to identify one structural mismatch that removes measured
  active work without suppressing NEWMV winners. A partner-tier diagnosis is
  in flight because the broad prune, low-variance gate, threshold reorder, and
  earlier packet/ownership hypotheses have all been ruled out.
