### Unit 658 — add the encoder row-MT wavefront primitive

- Symbolicating the Unit 656 main-thread wait stacks to source lines assigns
  1,345 samples to the four static tile picker jobs, 449 to packet tile
  traversals, 248 to the overlapped loop-filter join, and only 49 to the
  parallel reconstruction copy. The picker tail is therefore the structural
  speed target; rearranging complete tile jobs cannot shorten it.
- `row_mt::RowSync` is the first behavior-neutral prerequisite for splitting
  each tile into superblock-row jobs. It mirrors pinned libvpx's encoder
  `VP9RowMTSync` with a fixed one-column wavefront: row `r` waits until row
  `r-1` publishes the same superblock column. The final-column sentinel,
  dummy tile-MT mode, and frame reset semantics are explicit.
- The implementation uses only `Mutex<i32>` and `Condvar`; it adds no unsafe
  code and changes no encoding path. Six focused tests cover dummy and first-
  row no-ops, real blocking and release, the end-of-row sentinel, reset, and
  poisoned-state panic instead of deadlock.
- Focused tests, encoder release all-target clippy with warnings denied,
  encoder doctests, rustfmt, and diff checks pass. Exact next unit: add the
  per-tile-column superblock-row job queues and deterministic work-stealing
  selection, still disconnected from production dispatch, with concurrency
  and one-owner-per-job tests before touching the giant picker.

### Unit 659 — add bounded row jobs and tail work stealing

- `RowMtContext` now owns one ordered superblock-row queue and one `RowSync`
  per column tile. Workers start round-robin by column. Once a worker drains
  its column it selects the queue with the most unclaimed rows; ties resolve
  to the lowest column, matching pinned libvpx's scan order.
- Queue claims are mutex-linearized and publish lock-free remaining/drained
  hints for the stealing scan. The context contains no borrowed frame data,
  unsafe code, or production dispatch hook yet. It therefore establishes the
  one-owner-per-`(tile_col, sb_row)` invariant before shared reconstruction or
  mode grids are introduced.
- Five new tests cover ordered single-owner claims, round-robin home columns,
  largest-queue and lowest-column selection, independent per-tile wavefronts,
  and seven concurrent claimers draining all 44 jobs exactly once. All eleven
  row-MT tests and encoder release all-target clippy with warnings denied pass;
  rustfmt and diff checks are green.
- Exact next unit: create a behavior-identical single-row picker entry point
  and drive one complete tile through it serially. Preserve the current whole-
  tile wrapper and prove packet bytes, reconstruction, partitions, MV grid,
  RD-threshold state, and exact-VBP history remain identical before any row
  jobs share those arenas.

### Unit 662 — make row-wavefront failure cancellation-safe

- Partner review found a prerequisite liveness defect in the disconnected
  row-MT design: a job panic before `RowSync::write` would leave dependent
  rows blocked while `WorkerPool::scope` waited forever to join them. No
  production row dispatch is safe until failure wakes every waiter.
- `RowSync::read` and `write` now return a typed `RowSyncCancelled` error.
  `cancel` publishes the failure and takes each progress mutex while calling
  `notify_all`, preventing the check-to-wait lost-wakeup race. Poisoned mutexes
  are recovered only on this mandatory wake path. `RowMtContext::cancel`
  propagates one worker failure to every tile-column wavefront.
- Three new tests prove cancellation wakes a genuinely blocked reader, reset
  clears the cancelled state for a later frame, and context cancellation
  reaches all tile columns. All fourteen row-MT tests and encoder release all-
  target clippy with warnings denied pass; rustfmt and diff checks are green.
- The reviewed ownership plan supersedes sharing whole frame slices. Each
  logical worker will own a full shadow reconstruction, grids, partitions,
  history, coefficients, and diagnostics. Only immutable once-published SB
  bottom edges and MI slabs cross workers, guarded by `RowSync`. Per-row RD
  tables and ordered post-join token replay avoid schedule-dependent state.
- Exact next unit: add the immutable `SbBoundary` representation and a safe
  one-time publication grid with exact-once, dependency-order, and cancellation
  tests. Keep Unit 660's closure only until a concrete
  `InterRowWorker::encode_job` replaces it; do not put whole output slices
  behind a mutex.

### Unit 663 — enforce exact-once SB boundary publication order

- `SbBoundary` carries the completed superblock's bottom Y/U/V edges and
  final bottom MI row. `SbBoundaryGrid` allocates one `OnceLock` per
  `(tile_col, sb_row, tile-local sb_col)`, including unequal tile widths.
- The only advancing API stores the immutable boundary before calling
  `RowSync::write`. The corresponding reader waits through `RowSync::read`
  before exposing the boundary above. A missing boundary after visible row
  progress is a typed internal error rather than silent uninitialized state.
  Duplicate publication is also a typed error.
- Five focused tests cover unequal tile/row indexing, two concurrent writers
  racing for one exact-once slot, a genuinely blocked reader observing the
  fully published boundary, an injected progress-before-publication defect,
  and cancellation without publication. All nineteen row-MT tests, encoder
  release all-target clippy with warnings denied, encoder doctests, rustfmt,
  and diff checks pass.
- This remains disconnected from production and adds no unsafe code or encode
  overhead. Exact next unit: add worker-local boundary import/export helpers
  around owned shadow recon and MI grids, then test two serial shadow workers
  handing one synthetic SB row across the same publication protocol. Only
  after that oracle is green should the giant picker become
  `InterRowWorker::encode_job`.

### Unit 664 — prove worker-local shadow boundary handoff

- `RowWorkerShadow` binds one worker's private tight YUV420 reconstruction
  planes and tile-local MI grid to frame-global SB coordinates. It exports a
  completed SB's bottom Y/U/V and MI edges and imports the published edge into
  the top-neighbour locations required by a lower row. Constructor tripwires
  reject malformed planes, non-SB-aligned tile layouts, and inconsistent MI
  shapes before any worker runs.
- The focused oracle uses two distinct 128x128 full-frame shadows for the
  second column tile. The first worker exports SB `(row=0,col=1)`, publishes
  it through `SbBoundaryGrid`/`RowSync`, and the second worker waits then
  imports it above row 1. It proves all 64 Y, 32 U/V, and eight MI cells move
  exactly while adjacent pixels, the current row, and remaining MI cells stay
  at their independent-worker sentinels.
- All twenty row-MT tests pass. Encoder release all-target clippy and doctests
  pass with warnings denied; rustfmt and diff checks are clean. The helpers
  remain disconnected from the encode path, so stream bytes and speed are
  unchanged.
- Exact next unit: replace Unit 660's captured row closure with a concrete

  full-frame shadow remains the destination allocation; other workers replace
  only their assigned regions.
- Y/U/V merges remain safe and parallel by plane. This replaces the bespoke
  full-height tile-column copy type with the same scale-aware row merge that

  remain unchanged in this unit.

  `4a027127...e8239`, old-town `e1e93662...c06c4605`. Both focused four-tile

  Release all-target clippy passes with warnings denied; rustfmt/diff are

### Unit 670 — reject concurrent row sharing on the four-tile product point

- The opt-in prototype let four independent full-frame workers claim real
  `(tile,row)` jobs from one shared queue, published immutable reconstruction
  and MI boundaries after every SB, cancelled all wavefronts on unwind, and
  merged only exact owned rows. Default tile-MT remained off this path.
- The first thread-count oracle exposed two real protocol gaps. Row workers
  initially received empty variance-partition hints; supplying the canonical
  hints restored frame-1 equality. Four-worker stealing then diverged at tile
  2, row 1 because VP9 `MV_REF_BLOCKS` reaches three MI rows above while the
  boundary carried only one. Publishing the bottom three MI rows restored
  serial/two-/four-worker packet, reconstruction, RD-table, VBP-history, and
  previous-MV equality. All 24 row-MT primitive tests passed.
- All three source-aligned 60-frame streams became byte-identical to Unit 669:
  in-to-tree `925761c7...c44715`, ducks `d119c7f0...6c037`, and old-town
  `58494826...ad9e2`. Rvp9-decoder, pinned vpxdec, and ffmpeg agreed on every
  81,100,800-byte I420 output: `18f28d49...3e00d`,
  `9f048dd8...8e718c`, and `cda140b3...43ebc` respectively.
- The correct design was not Pareto-safe. With variance partitioning first on
  the caller, 15-pair median wall ratios versus Unit 669 were about
  `1.109x/1.114x/1.113x`. A parallel preparation barrier reduced these only
  to `1.076x/1.073x/1.081x`. Finally, lazy once-published tile hints restored
  pipelining but still measured `1.070x/1.066x/1.069x` wall and
  `1.014x/1.006x/1.004x` child CPU on in-to-tree/ducks/old-town. Every wall
  trial lost. Host load remained high, but the uniform 6.6–7.0% loss is much
  larger than the noise and fails the keep rule.
- Four column tiles already occupy all four configured workers. Row sharing
  therefore adds full-frame shadow allocation, boundary publication, wider
  coefficient/MI result merging, and synchronization before it can exploit a
  late imbalance. The complete Unit 670 code is removed; only this rejection
  evidence remains. Exact next experiment: return to committed Unit 669 and
  profile one output-preserving Stage 4a bottleneck that does not duplicate
  tile-MT work or widen worker-local output from tile to full frame.

  to be a multiple of 64. Earlier 1280x704 evidence was therefore a proxy,
  not the literal 720p target required by `PLAN.md`.

  SB row uses a complete square-leaf tree, ceil-rounded SB state, clamped row
  merges, edge-safe zero-MV SAD, and the bordered loop filter. Exact-VBP,
  integer projection, and A4 recursive descent remain on complete 64x64 SBs.
  The core mode writers emit the decoder's reduced partition bits and skip
  recursive quadrants outside the visible frame. The deliberate square-leaf
  departure from libvpx is recorded in `notes/divergence-ledger.md`.

  seven-mi-row partition, 64x72 end-to-end encode/decode, partial row-worker
  boundary export, and scale-aware partial row merges. All 1,655 core library
  tests and 607 encoder library tests pass (606 passed, one pre-existing
  ignored). Release all-target clippy for core/encoder/CLI passes with warnings
  denied; rustfmt and diff checks are clean.

  `12699d5f...465d`. At 1000 kbps, all three decoders agree per clip on

### Unit 673 — reject pass-0 damping-slot parity

- Direct model traces disproved an earlier inference that rvp9's bits-per-MB
  projection was wrong. On the first 1080p ducks GOLDEN refresh at target
  2500, both encoders use qindex 152, 8160 macroblocks, correction factor 1.0,
  and project exactly 440018 bits. Rvp9 emits 778296 bits; vpxenc emits
  777792. The raw correction is therefore 176% in both encoders.
- The actual divergence is libvpx's damping-history lookup. Its one-pass
  GF-group remains zero-initialized, so `rf_lvl=INTER_NORMAL` even when the
  GOLDEN correction factor comes from `GF_ARF_STD`. The INTER history is
  already warm, damping the raw 1.76 update to 1.28. Rvp9 couples both tables
  to `GF_ARF_STD`, treats the first GOLDEN sample as new, and applies 1.76.
  A temporary vpx trace proved `rf_lvl=0`, `damped=1`, and the exact projected
  sizes at frames 10/20/30/40/50; the instrumented binary produced the same
  IVF SHA-256 as the canonical binary,
  `6d78108c78e35fc1c3486735597de7a8b00ab4dfdd55cc49b27b7743cba1e629`.
- Two source changes were measured and rejected. Full pass-0 slot parity made
  rvp9 match vpxenc's qindex 166 at frame 20, but literal 1080p luma BD-rate
  became `+4.669493%/+3.893772%/-0.499364%` on
  in-to-tree/ducks/old-town, aggregate `+2.662499%`; average-YUV aggregate
  became `+3.066472%`. Restricting the decoupled damping history to GOLDEN
  refreshes preserved normal inter convergence and improved 1080p aggregate
  to `-0.467028%` luma and `-0.058420%` average-YUV, but worsened the limiting
  ducks clip to `+3.182578%` luma and `+3.408430%` average-YUV. It also moved
  720p old-town to `+1.389086%` luma / `+1.966674%` average-YUV.
- Both prototypes and their focused tests were removed. Neither is a
  reproducible Pareto improvement, and matched internal state is not the
  product gate. Candidate streams remain under
  `/tmp/rvp9-unit673-curves/` and `/tmp/rvp9-unit673-golden-only/`.
- Exact next experiment: compare and port the later-GOP one-pass VBR target
  adaptation rather than correction damping. Pinned vpxenc raises ducks
  GOLDEN targets from about 438 kbit at frames 10–30 to about 476 kbit at
  frames 40–50 after `current_video_frame > 30`; rvp9 leaves every GOLDEN
  target at 438594 bits. Trace `avg_frame_low_motion`, `baseline_gf_interval`,
  `gfu_boost`, and `af_ratio_onepass_vbr` around
  `third_party/libvpx/vp9/encoder/vp9_ratectrl.c:vp9_set_gf_update_one_pass_vbr`,
  then add only the first cross-corpus target-model prerequisite.

### Unit 676 — localize the ducks regression to GOLDEN coding efficiency

- Per-frame IVF payload and decoded-luma comparisons used the committed Unit
  672 encoder and the same 60-frame literal 1920x1080 ducks input. The failing
  matched-rate pair was rvp9 target 1568 versus vpxenc target 1500: rvp9 used
  664655 payload bytes versus 666528 (-0.281%) but reached 25.471939 dB luma
  versus 25.677832 (-0.205894 dB). The passing high-rate pair was rvp9 target
  3000 versus vpxenc target 2500: rvp9 used 1197524 payload bytes versus
  1194107 (+0.286%) and reached +0.033276 dB higher luma PSNR.

  failing rate, their combined payload was 189739 bytes versus vpxenc's
  214779 (-11.658%), and their aggregate decoded-luma PSNR was 0.826360 dB
  lower. Normal inter frames used 4.024% more bytes and were 0.182647 dB
  lower. At the passing high rate, GOLDEN refreshes used 1.835% more bytes but
  remained 0.498662 dB lower; normal inter frames used 1.500% more bytes and
  were 0.050186 dB higher. Normal-frame gains therefore hide, rather than fix,
  the GOLDEN deficit at the top of the curve.

  rate, rvp9 raises GOLDEN Q to 211/209/208/208 after frame 10 while vpxenc
  uses 196/202/203/202. At the high rate, rvp9 uses 141/176/175/175/174 and

  Unit 675 stream and vpxenc both use Q 166 at frame 20; rvp9 still spends
  12.003% more bytes and decodes 0.214826 dB lower. The next change must
  address GOLDEN prediction/reference coding, not one-pass VBR feedback.

  1080 therefore disabled it and used the bordered allocation plus six

  no unsafe contract, codec decision, or wire behavior changed.

### Unit 680 — run partial-height loop filtering directly on padded tight planes

- Temporary phase timers separated the Unit 679 caller waits without changing

  backend itself averaged `978.0 us`: filtering was `80.4%`, mask construction
  `7.9%`, plane copies `9.9%`, and allocation only `1.8%`. Avoiding allocation
  or retaining the bordered buffer therefore could not recover the measured
  join; the serial bordered filter was the correct target. The temporary
  instrumentation was removed before the candidate build. Raw timings remain
  at `/tmp/rvp9-unit680-critical-path-detail.txt`, SHA-256
  `9b5553a613dddcfd01d0e78979518cbc55e1cc5111c6b23082983dc33e657c62`.

  vectors only through the next 64-pixel superblock boundary, zero the new
  tail, and run the same split-edge backend as aligned frames. The visible MI
  dimensions and boundary masks are unchanged, and the vectors are truncated
  before reconstruction commit. This supplies addressable storage for the
  fixed-width SIMD tail without a full bordered allocation, six full-plane
  copies, or the slower serial mask/apply driver. Retained vector capacity
  makes later frames allocation-free. The one-thread fallback remains the
  proven bordered path.

### Unit 689 — gate NEWMV before motion search

- Matched temporary counters on the 60-frame old-town 1080p CPU7 VBR row
  found 305,865 rvp9 full-tree sub-pixel searches versus 276,783 in pinned
  libvpx v1.14.1 (`12f3a2ac603e8f10742105519e0cd03c3b8f71dd`). Rvp9's
  LAST/GOLDEN split was 260,283/45,582; libvpx's was 188,896/87,887.
  The largest rvp9 excess was at 8x8 and 16x16.
- Entry/rejection counters localized the difference to adaptive mode pruning.
  Rvp9 ran `run_newmv_search` before P20, then tested the found MV. Pinned
  libvpx initializes `frame_mv[NEWMV]` to `INVALID_MV`, applies P20 before
  `search_new_mv`, and therefore never gives an eventual zero NEWMV the
  zero-MV exemption. Moving the existing gate before search restores that
  ordering without changing threshold arithmetic or feature policy.
- The corrected ordering reduced the old-town search count to 271,075,
  11.37% below Unit 687 and 2.06% below pinned libvpx. All temporary rvp9 and
  libvpx counters were removed. Their final logs are

- The three 1080p target-2500 streams remained byte-identical to committed

### Unit 692 — profile exact-VBP tile picking and reject coefficient-arena recycling

- Replayed the committed CPU7 1080p old-town target-2500 row with

  spent 995.75 ms total: 624.36 ms (`62.70%`) in the final leaf picker,
  202.73 ms (`20.36%`) in coefficient emission, 168.52 ms (`16.92%`) in
  other work, and zero in recursive descent. All 204,624 final leaves were
  fresh picks. This is expected: `RVP9_EXACT_VBP_TREE=1` bypasses recursive
  RD descent, so there is no speculative picker result to reuse. The log is

### Unit 698 — derive Hadamard nonzero state from the retained SATD sum

- Started from integrated Unit 697 at `1cb89f7a`. Its five-iteration 10 kHz
  old-town profile attributed 5,828 of 10,413
  `reconstruct_via_round_trip` self samples to the fused AArch64 Hadamard
  quantization/full-metric call and another 1,402 to subtract/Hadamard. Unit
  682 had already proved rvp9 runs fewer `block_yrd` Tx8 tiles than pinned
  libvpx, so call-count reduction was rejected; the measured implementation
  excess inside the fused metric was selected instead.
- The fused Hadamard metric APIs no longer load inverse-scan positions or
  compute the exact final EOB. Their only product caller used EOB solely as
  an all-zero predicate, while the already-required SATD sum is zero exactly
  when every quantized coefficient is zero. The APIs now return that
  `nonzero` predicate alongside the unchanged SATD and coefficient error.
  The change removes an inverse-scan load, compare/select, vector maximum,
  and final horizontal maximum from every eight-coefficient batch. A focused
  differential sweep covers Tx8/Tx16/Tx32, six qindices, random, zero, DC,
  final-scan, and i16-extreme inputs against the widened exact-EOB quantizer.

### Unit 699 attribution — loop-filter completion, not tile picking, owns the wait

- Exact stack attribution supersedes Unit 699's initial tile-wait inference.
  Of rvp9's 2,013 `semaphore_wait_trap` samples, 1,057 (`52.51%`) are the
  loop-filter join at `crates/rvp9-encoder/src/frame_loop.rs:lf_job.wait`, 318
  (`15.80%`) are parallel source-map analysis, 294 (`14.61%`) are the final
  tile-writer scope, 251 (`12.47%`) are the mode-count replay scope, only 65
  (`3.23%`) are the inter tile-picker scope, and 28 (`1.39%`) are keyframe
  waits. Pinned vpxenc's 363 main-thread waits all belong to its
  multithreaded loop filter. Per-tile completion instrumentation is therefore
  not the next experiment.
- The full rvp9 profile attributes 2,629 loop-filter worker self samples to
  `apply_loop_filter_to_tight_recon_split_edge`, about `0.89 ms/inter frame`
  over five 59-inter-frame iterations, while the caller retains about
  `0.36 ms/inter frame` of residual join time. Within that worker, luma owns
  1,354 inclusive line samples and chroma 646. This selected a disjoint-plane
  scheduling hypothesis: keep the existing OS-thread topology, run luma on
  the dedicated loop-filter worker, and submit chroma into the first packet
  worker scope.

  packet-overlapped YUV420 filter across two already-owned workers. Luma runs
  on the persistent loop-filter worker. Chroma runs as an auxiliary job in
  the packet mode-count or final tile-writer scope. Luma, U, and V have
  separate allocations, and both worker scopes join before reconstruction is
  committed. Partial final superblock rows retain Unit 680's padded-storage
  boundary contract. No OS thread, unsafe block, codec decision, or encoded
  byte was added or changed.

### Unit 710 — borrow tile-local adaptive RD tables

- Unit 709's retained profile and source audit found a larger ownership cost
  than the remaining isolated inter-frame allocations. At 1080p the encoder
  owns `68` adaptive RD-threshold tables of `1,560` bytes each. Every inter
  frame cloned the complete 106,080-byte grid once, cloned that complete grid
  again for each of four tile jobs, then copied the 68 selected rows back into
  persistent state. Each worker reads and mutates only its tile's contiguous
  17-row slice.

  scheduling, table update order within each tile, raster order, codec

### Unit 712 — reject round-trip reuse and persistent Hadamard scratch

- The Unit 711 source audit rejects the proposed winner-reuse hypothesis.
  `select_interp_filter_by_luma_model` builds both filter predictions and
  passes the chosen prediction plus its existing model result into
  `evaluate_candidate_for_filter_with_pred`. That function performs the one
  full candidate evaluation. `pick_inter_mode` then copies its metrics; it
  does not reconstruct the same candidate again. Reusing a supposed second
  result would therefore remove required work or change candidate semantics.
- Address-level inspection of the profiled `reconstruct_via_round_trip`
  showed that its dominant AArch64 region is the required fused Hadamard
  quantization and coefficient-error reduction. CPU7 VBR uses the ordinary
  large-block path, so blocks at least 32x32 deliberately collect coefficient
  distortion; the existing model-only shortcut applies only below 32x32.
- A byte-preserving follow-up moved the temporary Hadamard coefficient array
  into persistent `RoundTripScratch`, because every supported transform
  overwrites its complete active prefix. The focused regression poisoned the
  reused storage before Tx8, Tx16, and Tx32 calls and reproduced identical
  rate, distortion, skip, and EOB results.
- The nine-pair four-thread CPU7 VBR screen preserved the canonical IVF hashes
  on all three clips but regressed. Median candidate/baseline ratios were
  `1.035791x/1.006960x/1.003994x` wall and
  `1.047722x/1.007083x/1.006312x` CPU for
  in-tree/ducks/old-town. Geomeans were `1.015481x` wall and `1.020191x` CPU;
  order-local paired geomeans were `1.005512x` and `1.005133x`. The source
  change was removed. The CSV SHA-256 is
  `42c303b7914d5cc5008bd8e44563bf3fc9293c7b4db56c2a66ec71c508cd7d42`;
  rejected binary SHA-256 is
  `f06856a99a023113e2ce6da52bd8877fed6c68444914b88827246306cad9b476`.
- Exact next experiment: fuse AArch64 Hadamard final-stage output with the
  existing quantized SATD/coefficient-error accumulator for the Hadamard-only
  picker. This can remove the final coefficient stores and immediate reloads
  while retaining the four 8x8/16x16 intermediate quadrants required by the
  transform. Prove the fused metrics against the existing transform-plus-
  quantize oracle across Tx8, Tx16, and Tx32 before a product A/B. Keep the
  change only if streams remain exact and repeated paired wall plus CPU
  measurements improve. CPU6/8, feature stages, other resolutions,
  conformance, and the final pinned-x86 acceptance matrix remain open.

### Unit 721 — reject arithmetic-only retained replay writes

- Unit 720 release assembly confirmed that every inlined `BoolWriter::write`
  inside `replay_retained_coefs` still loaded `count_only` at offset `0x25`
  and branched, even though `try_replay_retained_block` skips the token loop
  for count-only writers. A crate-private arithmetic-only entry point retained
  bit accounting and coder arithmetic but required a debug-checked non-count-
  only precondition.
- The full candidate routed the token tree and category extension bits through
  that entry point. It reduced `replay_retained_coefs` from `2,480` to `2,324`
  bytes and `write_retained_nonzero_token` from `5,288` to `4,936` bytes, but
  its shared extension loop became a separate `612`-byte function. The nine-
  pair screen regressed to paired geomeans `1.002484x` wall and `1.002581x`
  CPU. A 25-pair repeat was neutral at `1.000021x/0.999895x`; unpaired
  geomeans were `0.999602x/0.999940x`. Candidate
  `/tmp/rvp9-unit721-replay-arithmetic-only` has SHA-256
  `c9d72b611f0f15fc1b0cecd97f0f922ffa3bfa0669d83475bb3a3ce5cd0c06f6`;
  screen/repeat CSV SHA-256 values are
  `685b85aa7d6151bc8d99f55addeef4b53122225c0b4bf1f4496705e8ecbc96d5`
  and `1d2011adcbaed3799ff4688671d09bc7f52579069e48efa2ea79e12634c866fe`.
- A narrower candidate kept the existing category extension writer and
  bypassed the branch only for the main token tree. It removed the separate
  helper while preserving the same `2,324`/`4,936`-byte function sizes. Its
  nine-pair screen was promising at paired `0.998467x` wall and `0.999451x`
  CPU, but the 25-pair repeat did not reproduce it: paired geomeans were
  `1.000294x/1.000677x`, while unpaired geomeans were
  `1.001153x/1.001913x`. Candidate
  `/tmp/rvp9-unit721b-replay-tree-arithmetic-only` has SHA-256
  `79b0169a9e45c6f4a34d22cff8262bc511523f5ecbf0606fd555eb965f603568`;
  screen/repeat CSV SHA-256 values are
  `ef65f3e7cb73efae3f59163fc722b3d2d6b0a483e756d0643025d4ffcb8716be`
  and `14e310ba3beed61aaa4470c8031ca1f15a006926828512db77f65729082f47f3`.
- Both candidates preserved the three canonical IVF hashes and their source
  changes were removed. Smaller arithmetic-writer code alone is not a
  measurable speed lever on this host.
- Exact next experiment: audit `cost_coeffs_with_contexts` in
  `crates/rvp9-encoder/src/rdo/cost_coeffs.rs` against pinned libvpx
  `vp9_rdopt.c:358-458`. The Unit 720 profile attributes `997/59,475` self
  samples to this keyframe coefficient-cost walker. Libvpx leaves its causal
  `token_cache[1024]` uninitialised, while rvp9 zero-initialises a transform-
  sized stack array on every call. Test caller-owned initialized scratch reused
  without clearing, guarded by a focused stale-fill/causal-neighbour oracle;
  preserve token costs, candidate choices, reconstruction, and bytes.

### Unit 722 — reuse keyframe coefficient-cost token scratch

- Pinned libvpx revision `12f3a2ac603e8f10742105519e0cd03c3b8f71dd`
  declares `token_cache[32 * 32]` without initialization in
  `vp9_rdopt.c:358-458`. Its scan-neighbour table is causal: every position
  read by `get_coef_context` was written earlier in the same coefficient walk.
  Rvp9 instead zero-initialized a transform-sized stack cache for every intra-
  mode candidate in `cost_coeffs_with_contexts`.
- The public coefficient-cost API retains its existing safe, self-contained
  cache. The two realtime keyframe pickers now use an internal caller-scratch
  form and reuse one initialized 4x4 or 8x8 cache across mode candidates
  without clearing it. No unsafe code was added. An exhaustive regression
  compares zero-filled and stale-filled scratch for every EOB position across
  all four transform sizes and every reachable scan type.
- Release assembly reduced the hot cost walk's stack frame from `288` to `208`
  bytes and removed its cache-zeroing stores. Candidate
  `/tmp/rvp9-unit722-reuse-coef-cost-cache` has SHA-256
  `4b59a54083fb0795597f275814a3166c03e78878a68ea1d9f54b517baf1df55c`.
- The nine-pair screen was host-noisy and regressed at paired geomeans
  `1.003006x` wall and `1.002572x` CPU. Two independent 25-pair repeats both
  improved: repeat A paired geomeans were `0.998059x/0.999036x`; repeat B was
  `0.999488x/0.998982x`. Every run preserved all three canonical IVF hashes.
- Pooled across 50 pairs per clip, wall ratios were
  `0.999228x/0.996089x/0.999145x` and CPU ratios were
  `0.998957x/0.996410x/0.998795x` for in-tree/ducks/old-town. Paired wall
  ratios were `0.997547x/0.998550x/0.999916x`; paired CPU ratios were
  `0.998307x/0.998308x/0.999807x`. Corpus geomeans were `0.998153x` wall and
  `0.998053x` CPU, with paired geomeans `0.998671x/0.998807x`: reproducible
  improvements of `0.13%` wall and `0.12%` CPU over integrated Unit 720.
- Screen/repeat CSV SHA-256 values are
  `403aa9dee035f0aa8ee9271b70cb6dbe4907cc3969b5b7149589934b94953cc7`,
  `56510db10bbf6e9de82f537198c3643c43ec61e4b47ed6df3f39836733653746`,
  and `a67be1d9a9e46734dcccb841d1098257774a26d439c7e7f91bb4ae2ee18c5e1f`.

  `1.193498x/1.045538x/1.166886x` CPU. Corpus geomeans were `1.103299x` wall
